summary: 32-agent parallel deep audit of the AU/AV/AW plan + ALL changes made + every AX requirement; root-cause + gestalt-fix + wave-routing (read-only, tranche-dev)

result.slice: dock-animation-rootcause — WHY the dock box shrinks BEFORE the inner items fade/morph (the lag/float defect §1.1, §1.2, §1.8)

findings.requirement: §1.1 — The box must not shrink first then have items fade/shrink a few ms later. Items must fade/morph IN STEP with the box on ONE clock.
findings.currentState: The outer collapse↔expand morph runs on THREE independent timing origins that are structurally guaranteed to desync. (1) The `.glass-dock` ROOT animates `padding`, `border-radius`, `scale`, `background`, `border-color` via plain CSS transitions (src/styles/dock.css:326-340) that fire SYNCHRONOUSLY when Vue flips the `{collapsed,expanded}` class (GlassDock.vue:423) — i.e. on the browser's very next style/paint after the `visualExpanded` computed changes. (2) The INNER `.dock-layers` `width` is driven by the JS `SpringProgress` FLIP path whose first pixel write is DEFERRED through `nextTick()` → `requestAnimationFrame()` → a forced `void el.offsetWidth` reflow (useLayerTransition.ts:340,344,360) — roughly one full frame (~16ms) AFTER the root CSS transition has already begun. (3) `background`/`border-color` ride `--dock-motion-standard` (`--duration-normal` cubic, dock.css:329,339), a DIFFERENT duration/curve than the `--dock-motion-resize` spring everything else uses. So the visible silhouette of the box (its padding-driven edges + radius) starts collapsing a frame before the inner content width starts, and the user reads exactly 'the box shrinks first, then the items follow.'
findings.rootCause: ARCHITECTURAL: there is no single animation authority for the dock's OUTER silhouette. The AV.W9/AW.W2 rebuild correctly unified the *inner* concern to one spring (width owns one driver; opacity owns one; visibility owns one), but it never unified the morph ACROSS the root-element box and the inner content. The root box's geometry (padding + radius + scale) is governed by synchronous CSS-class-flip transitions, while the content width is governed by a deferred JS spring — two different elements, two different clocks, two different START FRAMES. The `nextTick→rAF→reflow` deferral was added (AU.W8) to put the class-swap and the width-set in ONE frame relative to EACH OTHER, but it inadvertently pushed BOTH a frame behind the always-synchronous root CSS transition. The clip-reveal (AW.W2) made the *inner content* track the box aperture in-step, but the aperture itself is the `.dock-layers` width clock, which is still a frame behind the root padding/radius clock — so the aperture and the box-chrome desync even though content-and-aperture are locked.
findings.gestaltFix: Collapse the dock morph onto ONE driver that owns the ENTIRE box on ONE clock. The idiomatic transposition: drive the morph from a single normalized spring progress scalar (0→1) written once per frame to a CSS custom property on the `.glass-dock` root (`--dock-morph-t`), and express EVERY animated axis — width/inline-size, padding, border-radius, scale, AND the child stagger — as pure `calc()`/interpolation off that ONE scalar (the AW.W3 stagger already proves the pattern with `--dock-morph-progress`). No CSS `transition` on the root at all; no separate inner-vs-root clocks. The spring writes one number; the box, the chrome, and the children all derive their frame state from it synchronously in the same paint. This removes the nextTick/rAF/reflow deferral skew (everything starts the same frame), removes the `--dock-motion-standard` second curve (background/border interpolate off the same `t`), and makes 'one clock' a structural guarantee rather than a timing-coincidence. Mirrors the keyframes.js-first-dock spirit (one element, one transition) but upgraded to a single spring scalar feeding a token-interpolation surface — DRY, no dual-driver, no magic deferral.
findings.evidence: src/styles/dock.css:326-340 (root CSS transition list: padding/scale/border-radius on --dock-motion-resize, background/border-color on --dock-motion-standard); useLayerTransition.ts:340,344,360 (nextTick→rAF→void offsetWidth deferral before the spring's first width write); GlassDock.vue:423 (synchronous class flip); dock.css:581 (`.dock-layers { transition: width --dock-motion-resize }` — inner-only). Compare e8380d7:useLayerTransition.ts (the perfected first impl: ONE element, width via CSS transition, class-swap synchronous at watch-fire — one clock by construction).

findings.requirement: §1.2 — Fix from FIRST PRINCIPLES with the layering system; the native View-Transitions path must not desync the box.
findings.currentState: On the real-Chrome DEFAULT path (NATIVE_VT=true), the layer swap is wrapped in `startViewTransition` and only `.dock-layers` carries a `view-transition-name` (GlassDock.vue:277-284). The browser snapshots and morphs ONLY `.dock-layers`. But the `.glass-dock` ROOT (padding, border-radius, scale, background, border) has NO `view-transition-name`, so its CSS transitions run on the LIVE DOM — which has ALREADY been mutated to the new state inside the VT callback. The live root therefore snaps/transitions to its target box while a frozen VT snapshot of the inner content cross-fades/morphs on top on the browser's separate VT clock. Two fully independent timelines (live CSS transition vs. ::view-transition-group animation) over the same visual morph.
findings.rootCause: The VT capture boundary is drawn around the wrong element. The morph is conceptually 'the whole dock box reshapes,' but only the inner content layer is enrolled in the View-Transition. An uncaptured animating ancestor is the canonical VT desync anti-pattern: the live ancestor and the snapshotted descendant cannot share a clock because one is real-DOM CSS and the other is a pseudo-element snapshot. This is the same class of two-clock fork as the FLIP path, just on the VT engine instead of the JS engine.
findings.gestaltFix: If the morph is kept on VT at all, the `view-transition-name` must sit on the `.glass-dock` ROOT (the element whose box IS the morph), not on the inner `.dock-layers` — so the browser captures and interpolates the entire box (padding, radius, size) as ONE group on ONE VT clock, with NO live CSS transition on the root competing. Better still under the §1.1 single-scalar gestalt: RETIRE the dock's dependence on View-Transitions for the box morph entirely and run the ONE-spring-scalar driver on every engine (VT becomes unnecessary once a single scalar owns the whole box — it was only ever a parallel mechanism that re-introduced a second clock). One driver, every engine — the AV.W9.0 'one authority per concern' invariant extended from 'one driver per property' to 'one driver for the whole box.'
findings.evidence: GlassDock.vue:275-284 (view-transition-name on `.dock-layers` only); useLayerTransition.ts:262-288 (NATIVE_VT branch mutates state inside startViewTransition; root box uncaptured); view-transition.css:59-86 (the VT group runs `--dock-resize-spring` while the live root runs the same-named CSS transition — two timelines, same curve, different clocks). The `proof:dock-animation-live` gate samples `.dock-layers` width + active-layer opacity ONLY (proof-dock-animation-live.mjs:13-28) — it never observes the root padding/radius vs. inner timeline, so this desync ships GREEN (the §13/§171 headless-green-but-visually-broken gap).

findings.requirement: §1.8 — The dock springiness must be perfected (iOS spring physics) and read as ONE continuous spring.
findings.currentState: The morph is split across a JS `SpringProgress` (the inner width, useLayerTransition.ts:399-439), a CSS `linear()` spring token `--spring-dock` (the root padding/radius/scale, dock.css:331-337), and a SECOND CSS curve `--dock-motion-standard` (background/border). The JS spring and the CSS `--spring-dock` token are kept bit-identical by hand (DOCK_SPRING const at useLayerTransition.ts:20 MUST manually mirror the regen-spring-tokens.mjs PRESETS row — a documented drift hazard). Three curves + a hand-synced duplication is not 'one continuous spring.'
findings.rootCause: Because the box morph is split across two elements/clocks (§1.1), it is ALSO split across two spring representations (the analytic JS solver and the sampled CSS `linear()`). The hand-mirroring requirement (`A retune MUST touch BOTH this const and the PRESETS row`) is a direct symptom: a single-authority morph would have a single spring definition, not two that must be kept identical by convention and a gate.
findings.gestaltFix: Under the §1.1 single-scalar driver, the spring exists ONCE — the JS `SpringProgress` analytic solver — and EVERY axis (size, padding, radius, scale, color, child stagger) reads its normalized output. The CSS `--spring-dock` linear() token and its hand-synced `DOCK_SPRING` mirror are DELETED for the morph (the token may survive only for non-morph decorative transitions if any remain). One spring, sampled once per frame, fed to a `calc()` interpolation surface — eliminates the drift-hazard duplication AND guarantees iOS-continuity because every property literally shares the same `(value, velocity)` trajectory, including across an interruptible retarget (the velocity-continuity the AV.W9.2 code already implements for width alone now governs the whole box for free).
findings.evidence: useLayerTransition.ts:5-20 (DOCK_SPRING const + the 'MUST touch BOTH' drift warning); dock.css:331-337 (root reads --dock-motion-resize = --spring-dock token); tokens.css:163,1329 (--spring-dock linear() + --dock-resize-spring); proof-spring-tokens-synced.mjs (a whole gate exists solely to police the hand-duplication — evidence the duplication is structural debt).

findings.requirement: §13/§171 — every visual wave closes on a LIVE audit, not a headless proof; the dock motion gate must catch the box-vs-content desync.
findings.currentState: `proof:dock-animation-live` (proof-dock-animation-live.mjs) is the dock's only behavioral gate. It forces the FLIP path, samples ONLY `.dock-layers` width and active-layer opacity, and asserts they co-settle within ~33ms. It never samples the `.glass-dock` root padding/border-radius, never compares the root-box START frame to the inner-content START frame, and never observes the VT-uncaptured-ancestor case. So the exact defect §1.1 reports (root box leads inner content by a frame) is INVISIBLE to the gate and ships GREEN.
findings.rootCause: The gate was written to catch the AV.W8b dual-driver FREEZE (zero rising width frames), not the LEAD/LAG desync between the root box and the inner content. It measures the wrong pair: it locks inner-width to inner-opacity (which AW.W2 already made co-incident by deleting active-pane opacity), but the user-visible defect is root-box-chrome vs. inner-content, a pair the gate does not sample.
findings.gestaltFix: Extend (or replace) the behavioral gate to sample the ROOT box geometry (computed padding-inline + border-radius + bounding width of `.glass-dock`) alongside the inner-content geometry on the SAME rAF timeline, and assert their morph onsets occur in the SAME frame (lead/lag ≤ 1 frame) on BOTH the FLIP and the VT engine. Under the §1.1 single-scalar redesign this becomes trivially true (one scalar drives both), so the gate is really a regression-lock on the gestalt. Pair it with a live Playwright + frontend-design visual audit per the §0 VISUAL TRUTH mandate — a gate that samples numbers still cannot certify 'reads as one continuous iOS spring.'
findings.evidence: proof-dock-animation-live.mjs:13-28 (WHAT IT MEASURES: `.dock-layers` width + active-layer opacity only), :54-61 (co-settle tolerance keyed to the inner pair, not root-vs-inner); the AV.W9 commit body claims 'the freeze is gone' (true) but the desync the user reports is a different defect the gate cannot see.

proposedWaves.title: Dock single-scalar morph — one spring, one clock, one box
proposedWaves.scope: Rebuild the dock collapse↔expand (and the DockLayerGroup pane swap, which shares useLayerTransition) onto a SINGLE normalized spring-progress scalar written once per frame to `--dock-morph-t` on the `.glass-dock` root. Express EVERY animated axis — inline-size/width, padding, border-radius, scale, background/border tint, and the existing child stagger — as pure calc()/interpolation off that one scalar (generalize the AW.W3 `--dock-morph-progress` pattern to the whole box). DELETE: the root `.glass-dock` CSS `transition` list (dock.css:326-340) for the morph axes; the `--dock-motion-standard` second curve for the morph; the `.dock-layers { transition: width }`; the nextTick→rAF→reflow deferral (the spring now seeds the box directly with no separate root clock); the `--spring-dock` CSS linear() token + its hand-synced DOCK_SPRING mirror + proof:spring-tokens-synced (one analytic spring remains). Retire the View-Transitions box-morph branch (NATIVE_VT) — a single scalar owns the box on every engine, so VT is no longer needed and only re-introduces a second clock; remove the view-transition-name on `.dock-layers` and the dock entries in view-transition.css. Preserve: the AV.W9.2 interruptible velocity-continuity (now governs the whole box for free), the AW.W2 clip-reveal aperture semantics (the aperture IS the box, now perfectly in-step), the PRM fast-path, the a11y visibility 3-state fork. KISS/DRY: one driver, one spring, one clock, zero dual-driver races.

proposedWaves.title: Dock motion gate — root-box-vs-inner-content lockstep + live visual audit
proposedWaves.scope: Rewrite proof:dock-animation-live to sample the `.glass-dock` ROOT box geometry (computed padding-inline, border-radius, bounding width) on the SAME rAF timeline as the inner content, and assert the morph ONSET of root-chrome and inner-content occur within ≤1 frame on BOTH engines (and post-AX.W01, that they derive from the single `--dock-morph-t` scalar). Add a VT-path assertion that no uncaptured ancestor animates against a snapshot. Add a live Playwright + frontend-design visual audit step (per §0 VISUAL TRUTH) that certifies 'reads as one continuous iOS spring, no lead/lag float' — not just numeric co-settle. Demote/retire the now-redundant static syntactic gates if AX.W01 removes their subject.

result.notes:
CORE ROOT CAUSE (the one-clock lockstep regression the prompt asked me to pinpoint): the dock has NO single authority for its OUTER box. The box silhouette (padding + border-radius + scale on the `.glass-dock` ROOT) is driven by synchronous CSS-class-flip transitions, while the inner content width is driven by a JS spring deferred a full frame behind via nextTick→rAF→reflow. The root box therefore STARTS its morph ~16ms before the inner content — exactly 'the box shrinks first, then the items follow.' This is NOT a single bad commit; it is the accreted shape of the AU.W8 (deferred-frame FLIP) + AV.W9 (single inner-spring) + AW.W2 (clip-reveal) + AW.W3 (VT + stagger) sequence, each of which correctly unified ONE inner concern but none of which unified the morph ACROSS the root box and the inner content. The keyframes.js-first / e8380d7-perfected dock did NOT have this defect because it animated ONE element's width via ONE CSS transition with the class-swap synchronous at watch-fire — one element, one clock by construction. The modern split into root-CSS-box + inner-JS-spring is the regression.

SECONDARY (equally blocking on real Chrome): the native View-Transitions path enrolls ONLY `.dock-layers` in the VT, leaving the `.glass-dock` root box as an uncaptured animating ancestor running live CSS transitions against a frozen VT snapshot — a second, engine-specific two-clock fork invisible to the gate.

WHY IT SHIPPED GREEN: proof:dock-animation-live samples only inner-width + active-layer-opacity and locks THAT pair; it never compares root-box onset to inner-content onset, so the user-visible lead/lag is outside the gate's measurement (the §13/§171 headless-green/visually-broken gap, exactly as REQUIREMENTS warned).

GESTALT FIX (first-principles, no workaround): one analytic spring → one `--dock-morph-t` scalar on the root → every axis (size/padding/radius/scale/color/child-stagger) interpolates off that one scalar in the same paint. Deletes the dual clocks, the dual spring representations (JS solver + CSS linear() token + their hand-synced mirror), the deferral skew, and the VT box branch. Routes to AX.W01 (rebuild) + AX.W02 (gate + live visual audit). This is in-slice; dock-with-slider keepDockOpen (§1.3), overflow/wrap (§1.4), sidebar consolidation (§1.5), rail (§1.6), and the icon-button-token-ladder removal (§1.7) are ADJACENT dock requirements outside this slice's root-cause mandate and should be picked up by sibling AX dock waves.

result.slice: dock-layering-firstprinciples — DockLayerGroup / DockLayer / useLayerTransition FLIP: in-step container↔content reveal

findings.requirement: §1.1 — Animations COMPLETELY broken: box shrinks FIRST, then inner items fade/shrink a few ms later (the float/lag defect). Items must fade/morph IN STEP with the box on one clock.
findings.currentState: There are TWO entirely different morph engines forked at composable construction (useLayerTransition.ts:108 `NATIVE_VT`). On Chrome/Safari (the real default) the VT path runs (useLayerTransition.ts:262-288): the box+crossfade are a browser-owned View-Transition snapshot of the `.dock-layers` element, while the SAME element is the outer width-FLIP subject and ALSO carries a `view-transition-name`. The spring-keyed child stagger (`--dock-morph-progress`, the in-step mechanism) is written per-frame ONLY inside the FLIP rAF loop (useLayerTransition.ts:418); on the VT path `armStagger`/`setStaggerProgress` never run, so the in-step reveal the lockstep work was built for is DEAD on the default engine. The browser cross-fades old→new pane PIXELS on the `::view-transition-group` clock (view-transition.css:59-86) which is a SEPARATE animation from any box-size change the dock root makes via its own `transition: padding/transform` (dock.css:326-340). Net: on Chrome the user sees exactly the reported lag — the snapshot crossfade and the box geometry settle on decoupled clocks.
findings.rootCause: The architecture grew THREE+ overlapping morph authorities that were never unified into one: (a) the outer collapsed↔expanded width FLIP on `.dock-layers` (SpringProgress in px space), (b) the dock-root CSS transition on padding/transform/border-radius/scale (dock.css:326-340, a DIFFERENT clock — `--dock-motion-resize` linear() vs the JS SpringProgress ODE), and (c) the View-Transition snapshot crossfade which on the default engine supplants (a) entirely but is itself a third clock. The original e8380d7 implementation was ONE clock — a single CSS `width` transition with class-driven opacity, ~135 lines. Each subsequent wave (AQ.W6 VT fork, AU.W8 single-frame rAF, AV.W9 dual-driver excision, AW.W2 clip-reveal, AW.W3 spring-keyed stagger) added a coordination layer to compensate for the previous layer's seam instead of collapsing them. The lag is structural: no single timeline owns box-geometry AND content-opacity together on the default engine. The `--dock-morph-progress` in-step scalar — the one genuinely correct idea — is only wired into the fallback nobody runs.
findings.gestaltFix: Collapse to ONE driver, one clock, on every engine. Retire the VT fork for the dock entirely (VT snapshots are the wrong tool here — they crossfade rasterized PIXELS, which is precisely why content lags geometry; iOS docks morph LAYOUT, not snapshots). Make the single SpringProgress the sole authority: it owns the dock ROOT box (width/height), and its normalized progress scalar drives EVERYTHING else as pure CSS `calc()` off `--dock-morph-progress` — child opacity/translate (already built, AW.W3), the leaving-pane fade, padding, border-radius, the pill↔card shape. No CSS `transition` on any morph property anywhere (delete dock.css:326-340's padding/transform/border-radius/scale transitions as morph drivers; they become calc() off the one scalar). One spring tick → one synchronous write of box + scalar → every dependent property is a deterministic function of that scalar in the SAME frame. This is the genuine 'one clock' the charter demands and is impossible to desync.
findings.evidence: useLayerTransition.ts:108 (NATIVE_VT fork), :262-288 (VT path, no per-frame stagger), :418 (stagger only in FLIP rAF); view-transition.css:59-86 (separate VT-group clock); dock.css:326-340 (third clock on root); original single-clock at git e8380d7:src/components/custom/dock/composables/useLayerTransition.ts (135 lines)

findings.requirement: §1.2 — Fix from FIRST PRINCIPLES with the layering system; reference keyframes.js's first dock + the perfected glass-ui dock; audit for the regression.
findings.currentState: useLayerTransition.ts is 479 lines (was 135 at e8380d7, 291 at AU.W8 6dd0d14) carrying FIVE parallel concern-machineries inside one watch: NATIVE_VT path, PRM fast-path, FLIP retarget/velocity-continuity, on-demand will-change lifecycle, clip-reveal `data-morphing` lifecycle, and spring-keyed stagger lifecycle. dock.css has ~1227 lines with the layer-crossfade contract expressed as comment-archaeology (every AU/AV/AW wave left a tombstone block explaining what was retired). The keyframes.js reference dock (demo/@/components/custom/animation-controls/composables/usePaneHover.ts) is dramatically simpler — a hover linger via vueuse `useTimeoutFn`, no measure/pin/FLIP dance at all; it sizes via natural layout + CSS.
findings.rootCause: The regression is ACCRETION, not a single bad commit. The system was correct and simple at e8380d7 (one CSS clock). It became a god-composable because each fix for a downstream seam (the dual-driver freeze AV.W9.0, the 100ms desync AU.W2, the clip-spill AW.W2) was applied as a NEW coordination layer rather than a re-derivation. The `useDockTransition` composable was merged away (9e3c92c→gone) but its FLIP logic was folded into `useLayerTransition` without consolidating, doubling the surface. The comment density (every block cites a wave letter + retired-arm rationale) is itself evidence: the file documents its own scar tissue rather than expressing a clean model.
findings.gestaltFix: Re-derive from first principles as ONE small composable (~120-150 lines target). Model: a layer group is a finite-state morph between two intrinsic sizes; the ONLY runtime job is (1) measure to-size once via a hidden/cloned measure pass or `getBoundingClientRect` after a class swap, (2) drive one SpringProgress from from-size→to-size, (3) expose normalized progress as a CSS var. Everything else (opacity, stagger, shape, padding, clip) is declarative CSS keyed off that var — ZERO additional JS lifecycle. Delete the VT fork, the will-change micro-lifecycle (let `will-change` be a static hint on `[data-morphing]` in CSS), and fold clip-reveal + stagger into the single progress scalar. Velocity-continuity (retarget) stays — it's the one piece of genuine iOS-spring value (keyframes.d.ts:800 `set target`). The keyframes.js usePaneHover pattern (vueuse timer for the OPEN/CLOSE intent, separate from the MORPH) is the model for the state half; useDockState already does this — keep it.
findings.evidence: useLayerTransition.ts is 479 lines vs 135 at e8380d7 vs 291 at 6dd0d14; useDockTransition.ts merged out at 9e3c92c (no longer exists); keyframes.js demo/@/components/custom/animation-controls/composables/usePaneHover.ts (the simple reference)

findings.requirement: §1.1 corollary — the outer collapsed↔expanded pair and the inner DockLayerGroup pair must morph identically and in-step.
findings.currentState: There are now TWO useLayerTransition instances per dock: one on `.dock-layers` for the outer collapsed↔expanded pair (GlassDock.vue:253), one on `.dock-layer-stack` for the inner DockLayer pair (DockLayerGroup.vue:57). Each independently forks VT vs FLIP. When a DockLayerGroup is nested inside a collapsible GlassDock, BOTH `.dock-layers` and `.dock-layer-stack` get `view-transition-name` (GlassDock.vue:277, DockLayerGroup.vue:82) — nested VT names on ancestor+descendant in one capture, which the spec handles but with surprising containing-block semantics, and on the FLIP path two independent springs write inline size on parent+child simultaneously with no coordination.
findings.rootCause: The composable was made 'reusable at any nesting level' (its docstring) but reuse without a shared coordinator means two clocks again whenever the levels are both active. The outer pair morphs the dock width; the inner pair morphs the stack width INSIDE it — these are physically coupled (the inner stack's width IS part of the outer content's natural width) but the two springs don't know about each other, so a simultaneous collapse+layer-swap double-animates the same pixels.
findings.gestaltFix: One morph orchestrator per dock instance, not per layer-pair. The outer collapsed↔expanded swap is just another layer transition in the SAME group as the inner pane swaps — model the dock as a single stack whose active 'layer' is (expandedState × activePane). When the dock collapses, the active layer becomes the summary; when a pane switches, it becomes pane-N. One spring, one scalar, measured once. The inner DockLayerGroup should NOT instantiate its own morph engine when nested in a collapsible dock — it should defer to the dock's orchestrator (provide/inject the morph controller, the same DI pattern dockContext already uses).
findings.evidence: GlassDock.vue:253 (outer instance) + DockLayerGroup.vue:57 (inner instance); both set view-transition-name GlassDock.vue:277-284 + DockLayerGroup.vue:82-89

findings.requirement: §1.8 / §1.1 — the dock springiness must be perfected (iOS spring physics); springy, iOS-like, interruptible.
findings.currentState: The morph runs on `DOCK_SPRING = {response:0.32, dampingFraction:0.7}` (useLayerTransition.ts:20) mirrored to a baked `--spring-dock` linear() (tokens.css:163) — ~+4.6% overshoot, ζ=0.7. But on the DEFAULT (VT) engine the SpringProgress never runs; the VT group animation uses the BAKED linear() approximation (view-transition.css:61), and directional types swap in `--spring-snappy` for collapse (view-transition.css:85). So 'iOS spring' is only real on the FLIP fallback; the engine most users hit runs a sampled-49-point linear() approximation of a spring, not the live ODE — and it can't be interrupted mid-flight (a linear() is a fixed curve; the VT can't retarget with velocity continuity). The retarget/velocity-continuity (the actual iOS interruptible-spring contract, useLayerTransition.ts:311-332) ONLY exists on the fallback.
findings.rootCause: Same root as §1.1: the dual-path means the iOS-spring properties (live ODE, velocity-preserving interrupt) live on the path nobody runs, while the path everyone runs uses a frozen linear() sample that cannot interrupt. A baked linear() CANNOT deliver interruptible spring physics by construction — it's a fixed timing function.
findings.gestaltFix: With the single-driver collapse (AX.W01), the live SpringProgress ODE runs on EVERY engine — so iOS spring physics (overshoot, velocity-continuity on interrupt) is universal, not fallback-only. The baked `--spring-dock` token stays ONLY as the CSS-only hint for properties that legitimately can't be JS-driven (none, after the collapse — everything keys off the progress scalar). Retune the single spring once for the iOS-control feel; with one driver there is no token/JS drift to keep in sync (the current 'A retune MUST touch BOTH' warning at useLayerTransition.ts:13 disappears).
findings.evidence: useLayerTransition.ts:20 (DOCK_SPRING) vs tokens.css:163 (--spring-dock baked linear); view-transition.css:61,85 (VT uses baked curve); retarget only on FLIP at useLayerTransition.ts:311-332

findings.requirement: §1.3 — Dock-with-slider is broken (the keepDockOpen contract).
findings.currentState: The keepDockOpen wiring (Slider.vue:55-82) is structurally present: acquire on pointerdown, release on window pointerup/pointercancel. BUT the release listener is attached to `window` because reka-ui sets pointer-capture on the thumb (Slider.vue:71-81). If the morph driver (or a reflow during a dock collapse) interrupts the gesture, or if `useOptionalDockContext` returns null because the Slider is portaled/teleported out of the dock subtree, the token is never balanced. More critically: the slider's `data-held` reflection reads `dock?.held.value` (Slider.vue:138) which is the dock's reactive `isHeld`, but the hold→visual path competes with the morph's `data-morphing`/`data-held` writes on the SAME root, and a mid-drag idle-collapse race (the AW.W3 proof story at dock-with-slider.vue:124-148 explicitly exists because this was fragile) means the contract is timing-dependent, not structural.
findings.rootCause: keepDockOpen is a ref-counted token on useDockState (keepOpenCount), but it's acquired/released across an async window-scoped listener that can be orphaned by pointer-capture transfer, teleport, or unmount-during-drag (onBeforeUnmount release at Slider.vue:136 is the only safety net). The contract couples the slider's gesture lifecycle to the dock's collapse timer through two independent reactive paths (token count + data-held) that can race the morph driver writing the same attributes. It's a coordination contract layered on top of the already-overloaded dock state, not a first-class part of the morph model.
findings.gestaltFix: Make 'held' a FIRST-CLASS input to the single morph state machine, not a side-channel token race. The dock state is a function of (hoverIntent, pinned, heldCount); the morph is a function of that state. Acquire/release should be a synchronous reactive edge tied to reka-ui's own drag state (the SliderRoot exposes pressed/dragging state — subscribe to it directly rather than hand-rolling window pointerup), so there is no orphan-able async listener. With one morph driver (AX.W01) there is no `data-morphing`/`data-held` write race because the driver owns one scalar and `held` is just a state input, not a competing attribute writer.
findings.evidence: Slider.vue:55-82 (acquire/release window listener), :136 (unmount safety net), :138 (data-held read); dock-with-slider.vue:124-148 (the AW.W3 proof story that exists because the hold was fragile)

findings.requirement: §1.1 — clip-reveal aperture must work on the default engine (the 'box IS the reveal aperture' contract).
findings.currentState: The clip-reveal contract (dock.css:111-161, AW.W2) gates `overflow:clip` on `[data-morphing]`, set by the driver at gesture start. On the FLIP path `setMorphing` is set in the rAF (useLayerTransition.ts:377) and content is revealed by the growing box. On the VT path `setMorphing` is set (useLayerTransition.ts:267) but the box is NOT actually growing via the clip — the VT snapshot replaces the live box with a rasterized old→new crossfade, so the clip aperture reveals nothing; the VT pseudo-element animation is what paints. The two reveal mechanisms (clip-aperture vs VT-snapshot-crossfade) are fundamentally different and only one is correct iOS-feel (the aperture); the default engine gets the wrong one.
findings.rootCause: The clip-reveal aperture (the genuinely correct iOS dock mechanism — content laid out once at full size, box uncovers it) was built for the FLIP path, then `setMorphing` was bolted onto the VT path too for symmetry — but a VT snapshot doesn't reveal-through-aperture, it crossfades pixels. The aperture and the snapshot are incompatible reveal models stapled together.
findings.gestaltFix: Keep ONLY the clip-reveal aperture (it's the correct model) and drop the VT snapshot entirely (AX.W01). Content lays out once at natural size; the single spring grows the box; `overflow:clip` on the morph axis makes the box the aperture; the spring-keyed stagger fades children in-step as the aperture uncovers them. This is iOS-exact and runs identically on every engine because it's pure layout + one spring + calc(), no snapshot.
findings.evidence: dock.css:111-161 (clip-reveal gated on data-morphing); useLayerTransition.ts:267 (VT path sets morphing but snapshot supplants the aperture) vs :377 (FLIP path where aperture actually reveals)

findings.requirement: §0 / §11 — No god modules (>500 lines split); DRY; KISS; no fallbacks/special-cases; excise legacy or fail loudly.
findings.currentState: useLayerTransition.ts (479 lines) is just under the 500 threshold but is a god-composable by concern-count (5 lifecycles in one watch). dock.css is ~1227 lines mixing shell/density/crossfade/grid/wrap/scroll/instrument-strip with extensive retired-arm tombstone comments (e.g. dock.css:584-599 documents a RETIRED @supports block; :689-700 documents another retired arm). The PRM fast-path, the FLIP fallback, and the VT path are three special-cases of one operation. CLAUDE.md and the SFC headers carry 'DO-NOT-SPLIT' assertions (GlassDock.vue:2) that pre-empt the refactor.
findings.rootCause: The 'one driver per concern, fail-closed' invariant (AV.W9.0) was applied by RETIRING arms and leaving their tombstones, rather than re-architecting so the arms never existed. The result is a file that's mostly archaeology. The 479-line composable is the sum of compensations, not a model.
findings.gestaltFix: After the single-driver collapse (AX.W01), useLayerTransition shrinks to a measure+spring+scalar core (~130 lines). Split dock.css into cohesive co-located concern files: dock-shell.css (root/density/glass), dock-layers.css (the crossfade+aperture+stagger contract), dock-layout.css (grid/wrap/scroll/instrument-strip). Delete every retired-arm tombstone comment — the git history is the archive, not the source file. Each remaining block expresses the CURRENT model only.
findings.evidence: useLayerTransition.ts 479 lines / 5 lifecycles; dock.css ~1227 lines with retired-arm tombstones at :584-599, :689-700; GlassDock.vue:2 DO-NOT-SPLIT marker

findings.requirement: §0 / §11 — brittle nested-selector + reactivity audit; non-idiomatic Tailwind + magic-number/calc chains.
findings.currentState: The dock-root transition lists (dock.css:326-340, :367-374) hand-enumerate 6-7 properties each on different sub-tokens (`--dock-motion-resize` vs `--dock-motion-standard`), and the per-child stagger is a hand-rolled nth-child cascade with hardcoded onset fractions (dock.css:776-795: 0.08, 0.16, 0.24, 0.32, 0.4). The crossfade contract is a comma-group over two distinct state vocabularies (`.layer-active`/`.is-active`/`.is-leaving`, dock.css:648-687) kept in sync by a load-bearing comment (dock.css:610-619 'a later refactor greps for this marker'). The `--dock-morph-progress` calc ramps (dock.css:758-771) are correct in spirit but duplicated across `.dock-layers` and `.dock-layer-stack` selectors.
findings.rootCause: The two state vocabularies (.dock-layer for the outer pair, .dock-layer-item-host for the inner) were never unified, so every crossfade/stagger rule is written twice and kept in sync by convention + greppable comments. The nth-child onset fractions are magic numbers because there's no token expressing 'stagger step'.
findings.gestaltFix: Unify on ONE state vocabulary for both pairs (after AX.W02 merges the morph orchestrator) — `.is-active`/`.is-leaving` everywhere, so the crossfade+stagger contract is written ONCE. Express the stagger onset as a single `--dock-stagger-step` token × the child index (CSS `sibling-index()` where Baseline, else a short generated set), removing the hand-typed 0.08/0.16/... ladder. The progress-keyed calc ramps become one shared `@utility` or a single selector over the unified vocabulary.
findings.evidence: dock.css:326-340 + :367-374 (hand-enumerated transition lists), :776-795 (magic onset fractions), :610-619 (greppable sync comment), :648-687 (doubled state-vocab comma-group)

findings.requirement: §13 / §0 — VISUAL TRUTH: a wave closes on a live Playwright + frontend-design audit, not a green headless gate. The dock gates passed green while the dock lagged.
findings.currentState: proof:dock-animation-live (scripts/proof-dock-animation-live.mjs) DOES mount a real browser and measure painted frames — but it FORCES the FLIP path (removes startViewTransition so NATIVE_VT=false, per its own header) because the FLIP path is 'the deterministic, live-DOM-measurable path'. So the gate asserts the path users DON'T hit and never measures the VT path's geometry/content desync — the exact defect §1.1 reports. The VT-path assertion is only 'browser runs >=1 VT-group animation' (presence, not lockstep). The syntactic gates (proof:dock-motion-single-source, proof:dock-opacity-lockstep) regex-scan source and can't see the cross-clock desync at all.
findings.rootCause: The behavioral gate was written to be DETERMINISTIC, so it forced the measurable path — but that path is the fallback. The default-engine desync (geometry on the root's CSS transition + content on the VT snapshot clock) is structurally outside what the gate measures. Green gate + visually-broken default engine is the cardinal AW lesson restated.
findings.gestaltFix: After the single-driver collapse there is ONE path on every engine, so the live gate measures the real thing by construction. The gate should assert the in-step contract DIRECTLY: sample the dock-root box dimension AND a representative child's opacity/transform every frame on the DEFAULT engine (no startViewTransition removal) and assert they rise on ONE timeline (co-settle within 1 frame). Add a frontend-design visual audit step (screenshot diff across the morph) to the wave-close, per the standing visual-truth gate-philosophy (§13).
findings.evidence: scripts/proof-dock-animation-live.mjs header (forces FLIP path by removing startViewTransition); VT assertion is presence-only ('Zero VT-group animations ... would mean the morph is not painting')

proposedWaves.title: Dock morph — single-driver, single-clock re-architecture (retire the VT fork)
proposedWaves.scope: Collapse the dual VT/FLIP morph into ONE SpringProgress driver that runs on every engine. The spring owns the dock box (width/height); its normalized progress is written to `--dock-morph-progress` every frame and EVERY other morph property (child opacity/stagger, leaving-pane fade, padding, border-radius/shape, clip-aperture reveal) is a pure CSS calc() off that scalar — zero CSS transitions on morph properties, zero View-Transition snapshot. Keep the clip-reveal aperture (the correct iOS mechanism) and velocity-continuity retarget (the interruptible-spring contract). Delete the NATIVE_VT branch, the will-change micro-lifecycle, the baked-linear()/JS-ODE dual-source, and the dock VT-group CSS recipes. Result: geometry and content morph in-step on one clock everywhere; useLayerTransition shrinks from 479→~130 lines. This is the headline fix for §1.1/§1.2/§1.5(clip)/§1.8.

proposedWaves.title: Unify outer collapsed↔expanded + inner DockLayerGroup morph onto one orchestrator
proposedWaves.scope: Model the dock as a single morph stack whose active layer is (expandedState × activePane). Replace the two independent useLayerTransition instances (one on .dock-layers, one on .dock-layer-stack) with one orchestrator per dock that the nested DockLayerGroup defers to via provide/inject (reuse the dockContext DI pattern). Unify the two state vocabularies (.dock-layer / .dock-layer-item-host → one is-active/is-leaving set). Eliminates the nested-VT-name and dual-spring-on-coupled-pixels problems.

proposedWaves.title: keepDockOpen contract — first-class held-state input, no orphan-able async token
proposedWaves.scope: Re-wire the Slider↔dock hold as a synchronous reactive edge off reka-ui's own drag/pressed state (drop the hand-rolled window pointerup listener). Make `held` a first-class input to the single dock-state→morph model so there is no token-count vs data-held race against the driver. Re-validate dock-with-slider across collapse-under-drag, teleport, and unmount-mid-drag.

proposedWaves.title: Dock module hygiene — split dock.css, excise tombstones, unify the stagger/crossfade contract
proposedWaves.scope: Split dock.css (~1227 lines) into cohesive co-located files (dock-shell / dock-layers / dock-layout). Delete every retired-arm tombstone comment (git is the archive). Express the per-child stagger onset as one `--dock-stagger-step` token × child index (remove the magic 0.08/0.16/... ladder). Write the crossfade+stagger contract ONCE over the unified state vocabulary (post-W02). Confirm useLayerTransition lands well under the god-module threshold.

proposedWaves.title: Dock visual-truth gate — measure the DEFAULT engine in-step contract + frontend-design audit
proposedWaves.scope: Rewrite proof:dock-animation-live to measure the DEFAULT engine (no startViewTransition removal) and assert box-dimension AND a representative child's opacity/transform rise on ONE timeline (co-settle within 1 frame). Retire the syntactic dock-motion-single-source/opacity-lockstep regex gates (superseded by the single-driver structure). Add a frontend-design screenshot-diff visual audit to the dock wave-close per the standing §13 visual-truth philosophy.

result.notes: Cardinal finding: the dock layering system has THREE+ overlapping morph clocks (the outer width-FLIP SpringProgress, the dock-root CSS transition on padding/transform/border-radius, and the View-Transition snapshot crossfade) and on the DEFAULT engine (Chrome/Safari, where users live) the genuinely-correct in-step machinery (spring-keyed `--dock-morph-progress` child stagger + clip-reveal aperture) DOES NOT RUN — it's wired only into the FLIP fallback (NATIVE_VT=false) that nobody hits. The reported 'box shrinks first, then items lag' defect is therefore STRUCTURAL on the default engine: geometry settles on the root's CSS transition / VT snapshot while content cross-fades on the VT-group animation, two decoupled clocks. The single correct architectural idea (one normalized morph-progress scalar driving everything via calc()) already exists in the code (AW.W3) but is only half-wired. The fix is not another coordination layer — it is to DELETE the View-Transition fork for the dock entirely (VT crossfades rasterized pixels, the wrong primitive for a layout morph), keep the clip-reveal aperture + one live SpringProgress on every engine, and make all dependent properties pure calc() off the one scalar. This collapses useLayerTransition from 479→~130 lines, makes iOS interruptible-spring physics universal instead of fallback-only, and makes the green-gate/visually-broken gap impossible (one path = the live gate measures the real thing). Severity-ranked: AX.W01 is a blocker that subsumes the §1.1/§1.2/§1.8 headline and the §1.5-clip/§1.1-springiness corollaries; W02-W05 depend on it. Historical anchor: git e8380d7 had a correct 135-line single-clock implementation — the regression is pure accretion across AQ.W6→AU.W8→AV.W9→AW.W2/W3, each wave compensating for the prior seam instead of re-deriving. The keyframes.js reference (usePaneHover) confirms the right shape: a simple vueuse timer for OPEN/CLOSE intent (= useDockState, keep it) cleanly separated from the MORPH (= the single spring). I did not run the live demo (audit-only, no dev server assumed); all findings are grounded in source + git archaeology + the gate-script self-documentation, which explicitly admits it forces the fallback path.

result.slice: dock-slider — the keepDockOpen contract (Slider.vue + dock context)

findings.requirement: §1.3 — Dock-with-slider is broken (the keepDockOpen contract). A <Slider> dragged inside a <GlassDock> must acquire a dockKeepOpen token for the gesture's duration so the dock does NOT idle-collapse mid-drag, then release it on pointer-up so the idle timer re-arms. The hold is bidirectional + pointer-anchored.
findings.currentState: FULLY BROKEN, live-confirmed. Loaded the dock-with-slider composition at /compositions/dock-with-slider and ran the exact synthetic gesture the proof gate runs (hover-expand → pointerdown on the slider → pointerleave the dock → wait past the 600ms collapse delay). Result: expandedAfterHover=true, heldAfterPointerdown=FALSE, expandedDuringHold_900ms=FALSE (the dock COLLAPSED under the held thumb), data-held never flips on the dock OR the slider. The keepOpen() token is never acquired, so the dock idle-collapses mid-drag — exactly the defect §1.3 names. The AW.W3 wave claims this was 'fixed' (scope 5, commit-plan 'fix(slider): restore dockKeepOpen acquire/release on in-dock drag'); it was NOT — the contract has in fact never worked through a real reka-ui drag.
findings.rootCause: The @pointerdown="onPointerDown" (and @touchstart/@touchmove/@touchend) listeners in Slider.vue are placed on <SliderRoot> (Slider.vue:151), which is a reka-ui FORWARDING component, not a host element. reka-ui's SliderRoot renders SliderHorizontal → SliderImpl → Primitive through CollectionSlot/PrimitiveSlot and binds its OWN onPointerdown internally (SliderRoot.js:159 + SliderImpl.js:46 do setPointerCapture). The Vue listener placed on <SliderRoot> becomes a $attrs fallthrough that is DROPPED across the Slot/forwardRef boundary — reka's explicit template onPointerdown shadows it rather than merging. Live proof of the mechanism: a native addEventListener('pointerdown') on the SAME data-slot='slider' DOM element FIRES (nativeAddEventListenerRuns=true), and reka's own onPointerdown FIRES (it threw NotFoundError on setPointerCapture during my synthetic drag), yet Slider.vue's onPointerDown — whose first line acquire() is capture-independent and synchronous — NEVER runs (data-held stayed false on every probe). This is the exact stale-binding silent-no-op class in MEMORY.md feedback_glass_ui_binding_verification.md: a reka-ui listener-on-a-forwarding-component that vue-tsc + unit tests pass but only e2e catches. NOT a race with onMouseLeave, NOT a pointer-capture/window-listener issue (the comment at Slider.vue:70-72 misdiagnoses the seam) — the handler simply never binds to the element that receives the event.
findings.gestaltFix: Stop fighting the forwarding boundary with template @event bindings. Acquire the dock-hold from the slider's ACTUAL host DOM element via the existing template ref. In onMounted, resolve getRootEl() (already present, Slider.vue:96-101) and attach native pointerdown/touchstart listeners with addEventListener on that element (proven to fire), teardown in onBeforeUnmount. Keep the window-scoped pointerup/pointercancel release (it works — capture retargets to the captured element and bubbles to window). This collapses BOTH defects: (1) the dock substrate tier-shade — .glass-dock[data-held] CSS is already correct and live-confirmed responsive, it just never gets data-held; (2) the thumb-halo intensification — .glass-slider[data-held] .slider-thumb reads the slider root's data-held, bound to isHeld=computed(() => dock.held.value===true), which lights up the moment keepOpen() fires. Both are downstream of the one never-firing acquire(). Architecturally cleaner: a tiny useDockHold(rootRef) composable colocated under dock/composables/ that owns acquire/release + the pointer/touch wiring, consumed by Slider (and any future in-dock drag primitive) — removes the duplicated acquire/release + touchGate-watch boilerplate from Slider.vue and makes the pointer-anchored hold a reusable, e2e-verified seam instead of a per-consumer hand-roll.
findings.evidence: src/components/ui/slider/Slider.vue:69-82 (onPointerDown + window pointerup, on <SliderRoot> at :151), :103-134 (touch handlers on <SliderRoot>), :138 isHeld binding, :239 thumb-halo CSS. node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Slider/SliderRoot.js:159 + SliderImpl.js:46-52 (reka's own onPointerdown + setPointerCapture). Live probes on /compositions/dock-with-slider [data-testid=dock-slider-hold]: heldAfterPointerdown=false, expandedDuringHold_900=false, nativeAddEventListenerRuns=true while dataHeld=false, substrateRespondsToHeld=true (dock CSS works), haloChanges=false (halo reads slider's own data-held, also gated on the broken acquire). Console: reka's onPointerdown threw 'setPointerCapture: No active pointer' confirming reka's handler ran while ours did not.

findings.requirement: §0 VISUAL TRUTH + §13 — every visual/behavioral wave closes on a LIVE Playwright audit, not a headless gate. The keepDockOpen contract must be guarded by a gate that actually FAILS when the contract is broken.
findings.currentState: The proof:dock-layering-polish gate (scripts/proof-dock-layering-polish.mjs), whose detectSliderHold assertion (:458-479) is the ONLY automated guard of this contract, SKIPS FAIL-OPEN and exits 0 (GREEN) on any runner without a Playwright harness. I ran it against the live demo: 'proof:dock-layering-polish — SKIPPED (no Playwright harness on this runner)', EXIT=0. The detector unit test (dock-layering-polish.detect.test.ts) only asserts detectSliderHold over a SYNTHETIC pre-baked timeline object — it never drives the real DOM, so it is GREEN regardless of whether the live contract works. This is precisely the headless-green/visually-broken GAP the AX requirements call the cardinal lesson of AW (§13 last bullet, §0). AW.W3 was 'closed' on this skipping gate — the contract shipped broken in 3.4.0→3.6.0.
findings.rootCause: The gate's only real assertion lives behind a fail-open Playwright-presence guard, and CI has no Playwright harness, so the assertion is structurally never exercised. The accompanying unit test asserts the DETECTOR (a pure function over a hand-written timeline), not the SYSTEM. A pure-function unit test of a detector cannot catch a wiring break in the thing being detected — the timeline it consumes is fabricated, not captured from the live slider+dock. So both 'guards' are green while the live contract is dead.
findings.gestaltFix: Make the slider-hold contract gateable WITHOUT a browser by testing the seam that actually breaks. The forwarding-drop is a component-mount fact: mount <GlassDock><Slider/></GlassDock> under @vue/test-utils + jsdom, dispatch a real pointerdown on the slider's host element, and assert the dock context's keepOpen() was invoked (spy) / the root carries data-held. This is a headless test that FAILS today and passes after the fix — moving the guard from a skipping e2e to a deterministic mount test. Keep the Playwright proof as the VISUAL confirmation (halo + substrate paint), but the contract's correctness gate must be a mount test that bites in CI. Additionally: the fail-open SKIP should be re-examined tranche-wide as a gate-philosophy wave (§13) — a behavioral gate that silently passes when its harness is absent provides false assurance.
findings.evidence: scripts/proof-dock-layering-polish.mjs:458-479 (detectSliderHold), :544-546 (SKIP fail-open 'no Playwright harness'), :249-307 (sliderHoldProbe). Live run: 'SKIPPED ... EXIT=0'. tests/components/custom/dock/dock-layering-polish.detect.test.ts asserts the detector over synthetic input only. AW.W3 spec docs/tranches/AW/waves/AW.W3-dock-layering-rail-wrap.md:84-92 + :215-218 claim the fix landed and the gate proves it.

findings.requirement: §1.3 (touch parity) — the keepDockOpen hold must also work on touch devices: the touch-gate activation should acquire the dock-hold so a touch-drag of an in-dock slider holds the dock open.
findings.currentState: BROKEN by the same root cause. Slider.vue wires @touchstart/@touchmove/@touchend on <SliderRoot> (:153-155) and a watch(touchGate.isActive) → acquire()/release() (:128-134). The touch handlers are dropped across the same reka forwarding boundary as @pointerdown, so on a real touch device the gate never arms from the slider and the hold never acquires. (Unverified on a touch device in this desktop harness — isTouchDevice is false here — but the binding-drop mechanism is identical and proven for the pointer path.) Note the watch-on-touchGate.isActive is a second, parallel acquire path layered on top of the pointer path — a DRY smell that the proposed useDockHold composable would unify.
findings.rootCause: Same forwarding-boundary listener-drop as finding 1: touch listeners on the <SliderRoot> forwarding component do not reach the host element. The two acquire mechanisms (pointerdown path + touchGate.isActive watch) are redundant parallel wiring of the same hold, both routed through the same dead binding surface.
findings.gestaltFix: Fold into the useDockHold(rootRef) composable from finding 1: attach pointerdown AND touchstart via addEventListener on the resolved host element, drive a single acquire/release, and let the touch-gate's isActive feed the same hold rather than a separate watch. One owner, one acquire path, native binding on the real element — eliminates the parallel touch-watch and makes both pointer + touch holds verifiable by the same mount gate.
findings.evidence: src/components/ui/slider/Slider.vue:103-134 (touch handlers + isActive watch), :153-155 (@touch* on <SliderRoot>). GlassDock.vue:368-393 is the canonical touch-gate consumer pattern the slider mirrors — but GlassDock binds on its OWN host <div class='glass-dock'> (a real element), which is why its gate works and the slider's does not.

proposedWaves.title: Dock-with-slider keepDockOpen — gestalt re-seat of the bidirectional pointer-anchored hold
proposedWaves.scope: Fix the §1.3 keepDockOpen contract at the architectural root: the @pointerdown/@touchstart listeners on reka-ui's <SliderRoot> forwarding component are dropped across the Slot/forwardRef boundary and never fire, so the dockKeepOpen token is never acquired and the dock idle-collapses under a held in-dock slider. (1) Extract a colocated useDockHold(rootRef) composable under src/components/custom/dock/composables/ that owns acquire/release + the pointer-anchored window pointerup release, attaching native pointerdown/touchstart listeners via addEventListener on the slider's ACTUAL host element (resolved through the existing getRootEl/template ref — live-proven to fire), with onBeforeUnmount teardown. (2) Rewire Slider.vue to consume it: delete the dead @pointerdown/@touchstart template bindings on <SliderRoot>, the duplicated acquire/release booleans, and the parallel touchGate.isActive watch (unify onto the one hold). (3) Verify end-to-end live: dock substrate tier-shades (.glass-dock[data-held]) AND thumb halo intensifies (.glass-slider[data-held]) for the gesture, release re-arms the idle timer. (4) Replace the fail-open-skipping slider-hold proof with a deterministic @vue/test-utils + jsdom MOUNT test that dispatches a real pointerdown on the slider host inside a mounted <GlassDock> and asserts keepOpen() fired / data-held set — a gate that BITES in CI (born-RED on HEAD, GREEN post-fix). Keep the Playwright probe as the visual confirmation only. NO new dock API, NO new prop — consumes the existing DockContext keepOpen/release/held seam.
proposedWaves.dependsOn: Sequence after the dock animation/collapse waves that own GlassDock.vue + useDockState.ts (the §1.1/§1.2 one-clock + spring-physics rebuild) so the hold re-seats onto the rebuilt collapse machinery; depends on nothing in this slice beyond a stable DockContext (keepOpen/release/held), which is unchanged.

result.notes: LIVE-VERIFIED, not inferred. I ran the demo dev server (port 5174) + Playwright against /compositions/dock-with-slider [data-testid=dock-slider-hold] and reproduced the AW.W3 proof gesture: the dock collapses under the held slider thumb (expandedDuringHold=false, heldAfterPointerdown=false). The break is a reka-ui forwarding-boundary listener-drop — proven by: native addEventListener on the same DOM node fires; reka's own onPointerdown fires (threw setPointerCapture during my drag); Slider.vue's capture-independent acquire() never runs. This is the MEMORY.md binding-verification class (vue-tsc + units pass, only e2e catches). The contract has effectively NEVER worked through a real reka drag (the @pointerdown has sat on <SliderRoot> since H.W3 f3caa9f). AW.W3 claimed the fix; it did not land — the only guard (proof:dock-layering-polish detectSliderHold) SKIPs fail-open and exits 0 with no Playwright harness (the headless-green/visually-broken gap, §0/§13). The dock-side CSS (.glass-dock[data-held]) is already correct and responsive; the only thing missing is the never-acquired token. Two secondary couplings fall out the same root: the thumb halo reads the slider's own data-held (also gated on acquire), and the touch path duplicates acquire via a parallel watch on the same dead binding surface. CAVEAT for downstream: this slice's fix must re-seat onto whatever GlassDock/useDockState rebuild the §1.1/§1.2 dock-animation waves land — coordinate so the hold wiring is not re-broken by the collapse-machinery rewrite. I did NOT edit, implement, or commit anything (audit-only); dev server + browser were closed after probing.

result.slice: dock-overflow-wrap

findings.requirement: §1.4 — Dock OVERFLOW/WRAP must be natural + idiomatic, handling edge cases. 'The current wrap is not correctly stylized.'
findings.currentState: `overflow="wrap"` is NOT a content-overflow strategy — it is a viewport `@media (min-width: 640px)` toggle. Below 640px the dock force-wraps to a multi-row pill clamped to `calc(100vw - gutter)`; at/above 640px the `@media` block in dock.css unconditionally forces `flex-wrap: nowrap` + `max-width: none`, so the dock NEVER wraps on a wide viewport even when its content overflows. Live-verified: a 40-button wrap dock at 800px viewport renders 1861px wide (overflowing the viewport by 1061px) on a SINGLE nowrap row — `flex-wrap: nowrap`, `rowCount: 1`, `dock.right` far past `window.innerWidth` (dock.css:1167-1192).
findings.rootCause: The wrap recipe is inherited mobile-responsive debt. The very first wrap impl (commit 078dd79, Mar 2026, 'Mobile: content wraps... Desktop: reverts to single-row pill') was authored as a mobile breakpoint hack, never as an over-cap overflow strategy. AT.W7-dock-a's 'clean break' (8e4cb9f) only renamed the class (`.dock-wrap`→`.dock-overflow-wrap`) and tokenized the `640px` literal (`--dock-overflow-bp`); it preserved the viewport-`@media` architecture wholesale, so the surface changed and the semantic defect survived. The prop NAME promises 'wraps when content exceeds the axis cap' (per its own JSDoc + the `overflow` enum framing it as the over-cap sibling of `grow`/`scroll`, which ARE content/cap-driven); the implementation delivers 'wraps only below 640px viewport'. This is precisely the 'fragile viewport/magic-number chain' the §0 mandate forbids.
findings.gestaltFix: Re-express wrap as an intrinsic content-driven reflow, not a viewport toggle. Make `.dock-overflow-wrap .dock-layer--full { flex-wrap: wrap }` ALWAYS-ON and cap the dock inline-size at `min(max-content, --dock-max-inline-size or the viewport gutter)`; flex then wraps to N rows exactly when the row exceeds the cap — at ANY viewport width — and collapses to one row when it fits. Delete the `@media (min-width: 640px)` snap-back block and the `--dock-overflow-bp` token entirely (no content needs a viewport breakpoint once wrapping is content-driven). The pill↔rounded-card radius swap keys off whether it is multi-row (a `:has()`/wrapped-state or container-size query), not a viewport MQ. This removes the magic 640px chain and makes wrap correct at every width.
findings.evidence: src/styles/dock.css:904-950 (wrap recipe) + :1154-1192 (the viewport @media snap-back); src/styles/tokens.css:872-879 (--dock-overflow-bp); git 078dd79 (origin debt), 8e4cb9f (clean break that preserved it). findings.requirement: §1.4 — 'properly WRAPPED + SHADOWED' — the multi-row wrap card must carry an elevation that grounds it as an elevated surface.
findings.currentState: A wrapped multi-row dock carries the IDENTICAL flat omnidirectional `--shadow-dock` (`0 0 20px color-mix(... 14%)`) that a single-row pill carries. Live-verified: a 2-row, 99px-tall wrap card paints the same thin-pill glow as a 40px pill. The `--shadow-dock` token is correct FOR a thin pill ('the dock's own border already defines the silhouette' — tokens.css:527-533) but reads as a flat un-grounded plate on a tall multi-row card. Side-by-side screenshot vs `--glass-shadow-floating` (`0 8px 24px` + hairline + inset highlight) shows the floating-tier shadow grounds the card; the current one does not.
findings.rootCause: The shadow stack is bound ONCE at `.glass-dock` root (box-shadow: glass-edge-light, --shadow-dock) and the wrap recipe overrides border-radius/padding/max-width but NOT box-shadow. There is no elevation-tier transition when the silhouette changes from a thin stadium pill to a finite multi-row card. The pill-glow + card-shape mismatch is a silhouette/elevation coherence gap: the 5-rung glass shadow ladder (resting→floating→overlay) was never wired to the dock's shape morph.
findings.gestaltFix: Lift the wrap (and the big-dock `shape=card`) silhouette to the card/floating shadow tier. When the dock is a finite-radius multi-row/card surface, route its box-shadow through the floating-tier stack (`--glass-material-rim, --glass-under-shadow-vivid, --glass-shadow-floating`) instead of the thin-pill `--shadow-dock` glow — expressed as a `--shadow-dock-wrap`/`--shadow-dock-card` token so it stays consumer-overridable on the cascade (never a dead local). The shadow then transitions on the same `--dock-motion-resize` spring the radius already glides on (box-shadow is in the `:not(.vertical)` transition list), so the pill→card morph lifts elevation in lockstep with the corner morph — one register.
findings.evidence: src/styles/dock.css:108 (root box-shadow), :911-917 (wrap overrides radius/pad/maxwidth, NOT shadow); src/styles/tokens.css:527-536 (--shadow-dock rationale = thin pill); src/styles/glass.css:246-255 (--glass-shadow-floating card tier). Live shadow A/B screenshot confirms.

findings.requirement: §0 — DRY / token-first / no magic numbers; consistency with the AW.W3b card-shell architecture.
findings.currentState: The wrap shell hardcodes `border-radius: var(--radius-2xl)` (dock.css:913), while the sibling big-dock card path (same tranche AW.W3b) uses a dedicated density-scaled `--dock-card-radius` token (dock.css:404-410). The wrap card radius is neither a `--dock-wrap-*` knob nor density-scaled, so a wrap dock and a card dock at the same density paint DIFFERENT finite radii (16px vs 24px) with no rationale, and a consumer cannot retune the wrap radius without overriding the global `--radius-2xl`. The wrap `--radius-2xl` and the desktop-snapback `--radius-pill` are also bare literals in the rule bodies rather than wrap-scoped tokens.

AW.W3b minted `--dock-card-radius` for the card path but left the older wrap path on the bare `--radius-2xl` reference — two parallel finite-radius treatments for the same 'finite multi-row dock' concept.
findings.gestaltFix: Unify the multi-row dock radius on the `--dock-card-radius` token (the wrap card and the grid/card dock are the SAME 'finite, not-a-stadium' silhouette — they should share one radius source, density-scaled). The wrap collapsed/snap-back pill returns to `--radius-pill` (already the morph target). One token, one finite-radius concept, density-aware — removing the 16px-vs-24px divergence and the bare literal.

findings.requirement: §0 — fail explicitly / no silent no-op; orthogonality contracts must hold.
findings.currentState: `overflow="wrap"` silently no-ops on a vertical rail. The wrap recipe is scoped entirely to `.dock-layer--full` (the horizontal two-layer body); a vertical dock (`.vertical`, rail/instrument-strip) has no `.dock-layer--full`, so applying `overflow="wrap"` to a vertical dock paints nothing — the class lands but no rule binds. Live-verified by cloning a rail with `.dock-overflow-wrap`: the wrap radius/flex-wrap rules did not apply (the rail's own `shape-pill` 9999px + `flex-wrap: nowrap` won). The dock.css:342-346 comment even says vertical rails 'wrap to multiple rows (opt-in via overflow="wrap")' — a documented behavior that does not exist.
findings.rootCause: Wrap was designed horizontal-only but the prop accepts it on any orientation with no guard and no rule coverage for the vertical case. The dock.css vertical-rail comment claims wrap support that was never implemented (the vertical column already wraps via `.dock-layer-item-host` column flow, a DIFFERENT mechanism). The enum is over-broad for the recipe.
findings.gestaltFix: Either implement vertical wrap on the rail's column body (so the documented opt-in is real) OR make wrap explicitly horizontal-only and fail loudly — restrict the prop's effect to horizontal docks in GlassDock.vue (don't emit `.dock-overflow-wrap` for vertical) and strike the false vertical-wrap claim from the dock.css comment. Given vertical rails already grow-to-fit + clamp (their natural overflow story), horizontal-only-wrap + corrected docs is the KISS choice. Do not leave a documented opt-in that silently does nothing.
findings.evidence: src/styles/dock.css:342-346 (vertical comment claims overflow=wrap opt-in) vs :904-950 (recipe is .dock-layer--full only, horizontal); live clone of a .vertical rail + .dock-overflow-wrap = no wrap rules applied.

findings.requirement: §1.1 + §1.8 — dock animations must be springy/iOS-like on ONE clock: the box and the inner items must fade/morph IN STEP, never box-shrinks-first-items-lag.
findings.currentState: On the dominant engine (Chromium, where document.startViewTransition exists) the dock takes the NATIVE-VT path. Only the INNER .dock-layers element carries view-transition-name (GlassDock.vue:280, dock.css drives it via the .gl-dock-layer group recipe). The OUTER .glass-dock root — which carries the padding / transform / scale / border-radius morph (dock.css:327-337) keyed to --dock-motion-resize = --duration-normal var(--spring-dock) — is NEVER VT-snapshotted. So a single collapse/expand morph is driven by TWO independent animation mechanisms on TWO elements: the inner box morphs inside the VT snapshot on the browser's VT-animation clock, the outer chrome (padding/radius, which IS part of the box width) morphs on the separate CSS-transition clock. They are not co-temporal.
findings.rootCause: The architecture has THREE size authorities that were unified only at the TOKEN level, never at the MECHANISM level. AV.W9 correctly killed the dual-driver race over .dock-layers width (CSS interpolate-size vs the spring). But the unification stopped at 'every driver reads var(--spring-dock)'. It never reckoned with the fact that a View-Transition snapshots ONLY the named subtree (.dock-layers), leaving the root chrome to morph on a wholly separate CSS-transition timeline. Same curve TOKEN, two different clocks, two different elements — that is the structural 'box vs items' fork. The one-clock requirement cannot be met while the visual box is composed of a VT-snapshotted inner element nested inside a CSS-transitioned outer element.
findings.gestaltFix: Collapse the dock morph onto a SINGLE driver per engine that owns the WHOLE box. Two idiomatic options, pick one: (A) VT-name the .glass-dock ROOT (not just .dock-layers) so the entire box — padding, radius, width, the crossfading panes — is one VT group captured + interpolated as a single snapshot, and DROP the root's CSS --dock-motion-resize transition entirely (it becomes redundant inside the snapshot). (B) Retire the native-VT fork for the dock-collapse morph and run the SpringProgress FLIP path on every engine, driving the root box width+padding off ONE spring clock with the child stagger written from the same per-frame scalar — one driver, one element, one clock, no per-engine feel divergence. Option B is the more defensible per the AX 'excise or fail, no special cases' mandate: it deletes the engine fork that is the source of the dual-feel, and the FLIP path already writes --dock-morph-progress for the child stagger so items demonstrably track the box in-step. Either way, ONE element owns the whole-box morph.

PIPELINE HEALTH: The regen-spring-tokens.mjs → tokens.css → DOCK_SPRING mirror chain is sound and well-gated for the (response,ζ) source-of-truth (proof:spring-tokens-synced is genuinely good). The real pipeline gaps are: (1) the build-time linear() vs runtime integrator 'bit-identical' claim is asserted only at the input-param level, never output-compared, and the two engines actually sample different authorities (linear() on VT, integrator on FLIP); (2) the comment-sync gate's file set is too narrow, leaving stale (0.5,0.5)/+18.5% prose rotting in the parity gate.

The dock's (0.32, 0.7) ~4.6% overshoot is a defensible iOS-control register. W01 must converge on ONE mechanism before any further parameter tuning, or the tuning is meaningless (it only affects whichever path the test engine happens to take).

findings.requirement: §2.1 / §14: CORE BROKEN — the live aurora canvas renders dark; only the preset thumbnails bake (confirmed live at /substrates/aurora). Root-cause WHY the live render diverges from the thumbnail bake.
findings.currentState: CONFIRMED live + root-caused at the GPU level. On a WebGPU-capable machine (the user's Mac/Chrome, navigator.gpu present + non-fallback adapter), the live <Aurora> stage swaps to the WebGPU backend and renders FULLY BLACK (sampled center pixels r:0 g:0 b:0; on the premultiplied swapchain → transparent-black). The preset thumbnail strip bakes correctly because usePresetThumbnails uses createAurora({mode:'capture'}) — pure WebGL2, NO WebGPU probe, NO swap. Playwright confirmed: the live canvas has a WEBGPU context bound (canvas.getContext('webgl2')===null, getContext('webgpu')===truthy), armed=true, opacity=1, sized 2006x1254.
findings.rootCause: A std140 INTEGER-FIELD TYPE MISMATCH between packGPUUniforms (uniformBridge.ts) and the WGSL Uniforms struct (aurora.wgsl.ts). The struct declares five fields as `i32` — stopCount, nucleiCount, warpMode, noiseOctaves, medium (lines 59,60,66,67,68) — but packGPUUniforms writes them into a Float32Array (slots out[1],out[2],out[8],out[9],out[10]; line 153's comment even calls it 'as int-in-float'). WGSL reads the raw 4 bytes of slot 1 as an i32 and gets the IEEE-754 BIT PATTERN of float 3.0 = 1077936128, NOT the integer 3 (device-verified: stopCount_raw=1077936128, nucleiCount_raw=1073741824=bits(2.0), noiseOctaves_raw=1082130432=bits(4.0)). samplePalette() then computes t = id * f32(stopCount-1) ≈ id * 1.07e9 → i0 = i32(floor(t)) overflows out of array<vec4f,8> bounds → U.palette[i0] returns zero → BLACK. Bisection proved it: domainWarp ✓, nucleiField ✓ (it break-clamps at MAX 6), samplePalette ✗ BLACK. (warpMode/medium read 0 only because config 0 ↔ float 0.0 share bit pattern 0 — a coincidence.) The deeper architectural cause: the WGSL pipeline is a hand-transcribed SECOND COPY of the GLSL aurora that drifts — GLSL uploads ints via gl.uniform1i (true ints) so the WebGL2 path is immune; the WGSL twin lost that type discipline. proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence only certifies the spliced COLOR CHUNK (OETF/OKLCh matrices, which I verified work in isolation), never the full fs_main with the real packGPUUniforms upload, and NO gate renders the WebGPU path on a real device + reads back pixels (the headless-green/visually-broken gap, §0/§13). The probe-swap in useAurora.ts:342-355 is SILENT (disposes the WebGL2 inst, reconstructs on WebGPU, no telemetry), so the regression is invisible headless.
findings.gestaltFix: Two-layer fix. (1) IMMEDIATE/CORRECT: eliminate the int-in-float class entirely. Idiomatic options, in order of elegance: (a) declare the five count/enum fields as f32 in the WGSL struct and cast in-shader (let n = i32(U.stopCount)) — keeps the single Float32Array pack path, zero dual-view juggling, and is the cleanest given everything else is float; OR (b) keep i32 in WGSL and write those slots through an Int32Array VIEW aliasing the same ArrayBuffer at byte offsets 4/8/32/36/40. (a) is preferred — uniform-as-all-f32 with in-shader int casts is the canonical WGSL pattern and removes the trap permanently. Add a device-level readback gate (the missing visual-truth proof): render the WGSL fs_main on a real GPUDevice with the real packGPUUniforms buffer and assert non-black center pixels + per-field int parity vs the GLSL oracle — this is the §13 standing 'headless-green/visually-broken' gate made concrete for the substrate. (2) ARCHITECTURAL (the real gestalt, per §2.4 'modern WebGPU' + DRY): the WGSL twin is structurally INCOMPLETE — fs_main has NO medium dispatch (medium is in the struct but never read; line 178 admits the painterly mediums 'run the W7c multi-pass passes' which are NOT wired into the single-pass createGPUAuroraSetup). So even after the i32 fix, WebGPU renders a SMOOTH-ONLY field that diverges from WebGL2's six mediums. Decide: either (i) gate the WebGPU swap OFF by default until the WGSL twin reaches medium parity (the honest substrate-binary stance — ship WebGL2 as the universal path, WebGPU as an opt-in once complete), or (ii) generate the WGSL from the same GLSL source so the two can never diverge (kills the two-copy class at the root, the AV.W1 lesson). Given §2.1 says 'TOTAL migration to modern color spaces' and §2.4 'modern WebGPU rendering', the convergent optimum is a single-source shader pipeline; the minimum-viable BLOCKER unblock is the i32 fix + WebGPU-swap-off-until-parity.

findings.currentState: `mediumVangogh(col, p, t)` is literally `return mediumOil(col, p, t);` — a one-line passthrough (mediums.glsl.ts:335-337). There is NO distinct van-Gogh stroke model. Real Van Gogh atomicity is NOT a length modulation: it is (a) discrete, separable directional dabs whose SHAPE (rhythmic comma/crescent strokes), spacing, and impasto ridging differ from oil bristle-streaks; (b) a turbulent multi-scale cascade where stroke SIZE tracks local energy AND strokes cluster into rhythmic rows that follow iso-contours. The current engine paints a continuous best-of-9 coverage field, not separable atomic dabs — overlapping strokes blend via linear `mix()` in `paintOver`, so the discrete-stroke read is lost.
findings.gestaltFix: Author a FIRST-CLASS `mediumVangogh` body (not a passthrough) with its own stroke grammar: (1) a comma/crescent stroke profile in `strokeShape` (a new shapeType bending the spine + tapering both ends asymmetrically) rather than oil's symmetric taper; (2) explicit ATOMIC dab placement — sparse, high-contrast, with visible inter-stroke canvas gaps (lower density, higher per-stroke opacity) so each stroke reads as a separable mark, not a coverage smear; (3) rhythmic row-clustering: offset stroke cells along the ETF tangent so dabs queue into the Starry-Night swirl rows; (4) per-stroke impasto ridge crowns at FULL height (not the 0.4+0.6·edgeN falloff oil uses) so each atomic stroke catches its own glint. Keep `bestOil`/`curvedStroke` as the placement substrate but parameterize them through a `vangogh` profile struct, not a `uMedium==5` if-branch buried in the shared engine.
