findings.requirement: §2.5 — Oil-pastel mode: much more visually interesting, painterly, LESS uniform, depth — resemble actual oil-pastel works of art.
findings.currentState: `oil-pastel` (uMedium==6) and the legacy `crayon` (uMedium==4) dispatch the IDENTICAL `mediumCrayon` body (aurora.frag.ts:405-407; DESIGN.md:191 — 'both share this single body — no duplicate'). The body has a deposition/scumble/burnish rework (mediums.glsl.ts:138-207) but it is a per-pixel tooth-noise multiply-and-mask, not a stroke-deposition. There is no actual pastel STROKE — it is a textured gradient with a scumble mask layered on top.
findings.rootCause: Two distinct media (waxy oil-pastel vs dry crayon) were collapsed onto one shader body to satisfy the W4.4 'no parallel duplicate medium' precept, but oil-pastel and crayon are materially different: oil-pastel is buttery, blendable, heavy-bodied with smeared directional drags and a sheen; crayon is dry, grainy, hard-edged with NO sheen. Sharing one body means neither is right. Deeper: the model is fundamentally a NOISE-FIELD multiply (`paperHeight` from `vnoise` at 3 scales) gated by masks — it never lays down a discrete pastel MARK. Real oil-pastel reads as overlapping smeared strokes with pigment-on-pigment build-up, which a per-pixel tooth multiply cannot produce.
findings.gestaltFix: Split the body: `mediumOilPastel` (smeared directional strokes via the brush engine with a soft creamy `hardness`, heavy burnish, pigment build-up where strokes overlap) vs `mediumCrayon` (the existing dry tooth-multiply, no sheen, hard scumble). Oil-pastel should DEPOSIT short broad smeared strokes (reuse `bestOil` with a wide low-anisotropy profile + creamy compositing) rather than multiply a noise field — that is what gives it 'depth' and 'less uniform'. The shared-body-no-duplicate precept is satisfied by sharing the SUBSTRATE (placement/tooth helpers), not the dispatch body.
findings.evidence: aurora.frag.ts:405,407 (uMedium 4 and 6 both → mediumCrayon); mediums.glsl.ts:138-207 (per-pixel noise model, no stroke deposition); DESIGN.md:191 confirms shared body.
findings.routesToWave: AX oil-pastel medium wave (split crayon/oil-pastel, stroke-deposition model)

findings.requirement: §2.5/§2.6 + §2.7 — painterly, non-uniform, depth, atomic strokes congruent to real works → 'stunning gradient art'.
findings.currentState: Overlapping strokes composite via linear `mix(col, c, alpha)` in `paintOver` (brush.glsl.ts:182) and per-stroke colors are `mix`/`samplePalette` linear blends. Where two complementary-hued strokes overlap, the result muds toward grey — the exact muddy-midtone defect OKLCh interpolation was meant to kill, but it RE-ENTERS at the stroke-compositing layer because compositing stays linear-RGB.
findings.rootCause: W5 moved palette INTERPOLATION and broken-color JITTER into OKLCh but stroke OVER-COMPOSITING (`paintOver`'s `mix`) stayed linear-RGB. The Kubelka-Munk spectral pigment-mixing fold that fixes this was EXPLICITLY DEFERRED at W4 (AW.W4 §10 — 'DEFER… trigger is a design pass judging the van-Gogh/oil-pastel overlap regions muddy'). The trigger condition is now met: the overlap regions ARE muddy because that is the whole point of dense atomic van-Gogh strokes — they overlap constantly.
findings.gestaltFix: Composite strokes in OKLab/OKLCh (lerp L,C,H of the over-color toward the under-color) OR adopt the deferred Kubelka-Munk `pigmentMix` on the painterly mediums only (oil/vangogh/oil-pastel), gated off for the smooth/atmospheric pole for cost. The cheapest correct fix is moving `paintOver`'s `mix` into OKLab (the matrices already ship in the chunk) — overlapping complementaries then transition through a chromatic path, not grey. This is THE single lever that turns 'procedural texture over a gradient' into 'mixed paint'.
findings.evidence: brush.glsl.ts:182 (`col = mix(col, c, alpha)` — linear composite); AW.W4-aurora-painterly.md §10 (Kubelka-Munk deferred with this exact trigger); README.md:620 (spectral.js named).
findings.routesToWave: AX painterly-pigment-mixing wave (OKLab stroke composite / Kubelka-Munk)

findings.requirement: §2.6 + §2.7 — painterly NON-uniformity; the canonical NPR 'make a gradient read as oil paint' operator.
findings.currentState: The anisotropic Kuwahara finishing operator and the LIC stroke-smear — the two canonical NPR operators that produce real painterly non-uniformity — are NOT executing. `painterly.wgsl.ts` (156 lines: `tensor_main`, `smooth_main`, `kuwahara_main`) authors them as WGSL strings, but `gpuRuntime.ts` draws 'the SAME single-pass aurora the WebGL2 fragment path draws' (gpuRuntime.ts:5). The multi-pass passes are referenced ONLY in comments (gpuRuntime.ts:7-8,13) — they are dead-string substrate, never imported into a pipeline.
findings.rootCause: AW.W7c (the multi-pass painterly WebGPU fold) authored the shader STRINGS but never wired the FBO/storage-texture multi-pass plumbing (createGPUCanvas.ts:15 — 'the multi-pass FBO/storageTexture seam (W7c) is a [no-op]'). So both render paths (WebGL2 single-pass AND WebGPU single-pass) hit the same ceiling: the mediums are single-pass per-fragment SDF strokes with NO post-pass smoothing or edge-coherent abstraction. Without Kuwahara, the texture reads as procedural noise (gridded `vnoise`), not coherent paint regions; without LIC, the ETF orientation field is computed but its directionality is never SMEARED along the flow, so strokes don't visually 'follow the forms' as strongly as the orientation math promises.
findings.gestaltFix: Wire the authored `painterly.wgsl.ts` passes into a real multi-pass WebGPU pipeline in `gpuRuntime.ts` (the strings exist and are 1e-6 color-verified — only the FBO ping-pong plumbing is missing): tensor→smooth→kuwahara as 3 render targets. This is the load-bearing non-uniformity fix. Gate it behind WebGPU-available; WebGL2 keeps the single-pass approximation honestly. This converts dead substrate into the feature that makes the gradient 'read as oil paint'.
findings.evidence: src/components/custom/aurora/constants/shaders/painterly.wgsl.ts:51,77,108 (passes authored); gpuRuntime.ts:5-13 (draws same single-pass, multi-pass only in comments); createGPUCanvas.ts:15 (FBO seam is no-op); grep confirms painterly.wgsl imported only in comments + DESIGN.md.
findings.routesToWave: AX WebGPU multi-pass painterly wave (wire Kuwahara/LIC/tensor passes)

findings.requirement: §2.7 — backdrops procedurally generated from ATOMS (noise) — the texture substrate must support painterly fidelity.
findings.currentState: ALL medium texture (granulation, paper tooth, scumble masks, pastel grain, bristle/streak modulation) derives from `vnoise`/`fbm` (aurora.frag.ts:170-196). `vnoise` is value-noise on a `hash21` that chains `fract(p*vec2(123.34,456.21))` then `fract(p.x*p.y)` (lines 158-162), and `hash22` uses `fract(sin(p)*43758.5453)` (lines 164-167). These are low-quality hashes with visible axis-aligned lattice structure; `fbm` is only 5 octaves with 2.02 lacunarity.
findings.rootCause: The noise basis was inherited from the smooth/atmospheric aurora (where soft warped fBm is fine) and never upgraded for the painterly mediums, which magnify high-frequency detail. The `hash22` `sin()`-based hash has periodicity/banding artifacts at high frequency; `vnoise` value-noise has the characteristic blocky lattice that reads as 'digital procedural texture', not organic paper/pigment grain. This is the silent fidelity CEILING under every medium — the deposition/scumble/granulation can only be as organic as their noise source.
findings.gestaltFix: Upgrade the painterly-medium noise to a higher-quality basis: replace `hash22`'s `sin`-hash with the integer-PCG/Sugar-style hash already used cleanly elsewhere, and provide a gradient-noise (simplex/Perlin) variant for the tooth/granulation fields (value-noise lattice is the wrong basis for organic grain). Keep the smooth pole on the cheap fBm; the painterly mediums opt into the better basis. This is a substrate quality lift the deposition/scumble/atomic-stroke work all ride on.
findings.evidence: aurora.frag.ts:158-167 (hash21 chained-fract + hash22 sin-hash); :170-196 (vnoise value-noise + 5-octave fbm); mediums.glsl.ts:97,119,154-156,169,195 (every texture term reads vnoise/fbm).
findings.routesToWave: AX noise-basis upgrade wave (painterly-medium high-quality noise)

findings.requirement: §2.6 — proper atomic brush strokes with VARIATION (broken color); §2.5 — non-uniform.
findings.currentState: `brokenColorJitter` is applied per-stroke-CELL: `colMid = brokenColorJitter(sampleBase(center), hash21(cc+89), hash21(cc*2.3+97), 1.0)` (brush.glsl.ts:277-282) — one constant jittered color for the WHOLE stroke. There is no WITHIN-stroke color variation. Real broken color (and real Van Gogh) varies hue/value ALONG and ACROSS the stroke (loaded brush deposits different pigment along its length).
findings.rootCause: `curvedStroke` returns a single `colAtMid` (brush.glsl.ts:142-147) sampled+jittered once at the cell center; `paintOver` only modulates VALUE via the streak fBm (brush.glsl.ts:171-174, `c *= 1.0+streak*streakAmp`), never HUE. So a stroke is one flat jittered hue with a brightness streak — not a loaded brush carrying mixed pigment. The streak path was a value-only modulation inherited before the OKLCh move and was never extended to hue.
findings.gestaltFix: Move the within-stroke streak modulation into OKLCh: perturb the stroke color's hue+chroma along `alongT`/`crossN` (the streak fBm already computed), seeded per-stroke, so a single stroke carries a small hue gradient — the broken-color read at the ATOM level, not just cell-to-cell. Cheap (the fBm and OKLCh matrices are already in scope) and it is what makes adjacent strokes shimmer like real impasto rather than reading as flat stamped swatches.
findings.evidence: brush.glsl.ts:277-282 (per-cell single jittered color); :171-174 (value-only streak); :142-147 (curvedStroke returns one colAtMid).
findings.routesToWave: AX within-stroke broken-color wave (folds into the van-Gogh medium wave)

findings.requirement: §0 mandate — no god modules (>500 lines split); colocate; sub-component dirs where befitting. Mediums slice maintainability.
findings.currentState: `mediumOil` (mediums.glsl.ts:209-326) is a 117-line monolith with inline per-mode parameter tables (lines 217-246) and 4+ hardcoded stroke-layer invocations (lines 270-308). `mediumCrayon` is 70 lines (138-207). The per-mode knob block (shapeType/bristleAmp/streakFreq/… for oil/knife/chunky) is an imperative if-ladder, not a data table.
findings.rootCause: The oil medium accreted four stroke modes + four stroke layers + crosshatch + tooth + relight in one function as each W4 fold landed serially on one worktree. The mode-parameter selection is logic-as-data expressed as imperative branches, which makes adding the new van-Gogh/oil-pastel profiles (the fixes above) require editing the monolith rather than adding a profile entry.
findings.gestaltFix: Extract a `StrokeProfile` struct (shapeType, bristleAmp, streakFreq/Amp, impastoAmp, hardness, tooth*, density*, len/widMul) and a `profileFor(medium, mode)` selector, then a single parameterized `paintStrokeLayers(profile)` the oil/van-Gogh/oil-pastel bodies all call with their own profile. This turns the new-medium work (van-Gogh grammar, oil-pastel split) into authoring a profile + a shape, not forking a 117-line function. DRY without collapsing distinct media onto one dispatch body (the §2.5/§2.6 fix).
findings.evidence: mediums.glsl.ts:209-326 (mediumOil 117 lines, inline mode tables :217-246, hand-unrolled layers :270-308).

result.notes:
VISUAL-TRUTH CAVEAT: this is a static-code + spec + git audit; I did not render the live aurora (the §0 mandate requires every visual wave to close on a live Playwright + frontend-design audit). The findings are architecturally certain (passthrough, shared-body, linear-composite, dead WGSL substrate are all textually verified), but the SEVERITY of the visual gap should be confirmed against a live bake of the vangogh/oil-pastel presets before wave close.

TWO HEADLINE ROOT CAUSES dominate my slice: (1) `mediumVangogh` is `return mediumOil(...)` (mediums.glsl.ts:335-337) — the van-Gogh medium has NO distinct stroke model, only a 4-line energy switch in bestOil; (2) `oil-pastel` and `crayon` share one dispatch body (aurora.frag.ts:405,407). Both are direct consequences of the W4 DRY/no-duplicate precepts collapsing materially-distinct media onto the oil engine. The fix is gestalt: a StrokeProfile substrate (shared) with distinct medium BODIES (not shared) — DRY at the substrate, differentiated at the medium.

THE 'STUNNING GRADIENT ART' GAP is bounded by FOUR ceilings, in leverage order: (a) the WGSL Kuwahara/LIC passes are authored but DEAD — never wired into a pipeline (gpuRuntime.ts draws single-pass; the W7c FBO seam is a no-op) — this is the biggest non-uniformity lever and the strings already exist; (b) stroke over-compositing stays linear-RGB so overlap regions mud to grey, re-entering the exact defect W5's OKLCh move killed at the palette layer; (c) the value-noise basis (hash21 chained-fract + hash22 sin-hash) caps all texture at 'digital procedural'; (d) per-cell (not within-stroke) broken color makes strokes read as flat stamped swatches.

The deep-audit digest (avg-deep-audit-digest.md:27,184) already routes 'oil-pastel genuinely painterly' and 'van-gogh atomic-brushstroke' to AW.W7-W8 as STILL-OPEN — confirming the W4 shipment was headless-green-only (the four proof:aurora-* gates are read-and-detect text/snapshot gates that a passthrough and a shared body both PASS), the precise headless-green/visually-broken gap §13 names as the cardinal AW lesson. The proposed waves are sequenced: refactor + noise-basis open at HEAD (parallel), then the two medium waves, then pigment-mixing + WebGPU-painterly converge on the differentiated mediums.

result.slice: aurora-options-simplify (the ≤7-atom door vs the ~28-field config; atoms.ts + presets.ts + AuroraConfig + the zones/noise/color control-element model)

findings.requirement: §2.2 — Simplify the options set. The wispy-sky default is a good starting point. A coherent, intuitive simplified control surface over the ~28-field AuroraConfig.
findings.currentState: There are THREE parallel, non-converged 'simplify the config' surfaces, none of which is actually wired into the live demo config UI. (1) resolveAtoms(atoms) in composables/atoms.ts — the ≤7-atom door (seed/harmony/mood/medium/textureAmount/motion/zones/interactivity). Its ONLY consumer is demo/stories/aurora/AuroraAtomsPanel.vue, which is ORPHANED — not in demo/stories/manifest.ts and imported by nothing (grep for AuroraAtomsPanel across demo/ returns only its own definition). (2) deriveScene(seed, mood) in composables/color.ts — a seed+mood→full-config door with its own MOOD_RECIPE and its own thirdsNuclei prior; it has ZERO consumers outside derive-color.test.ts and the barrel export. (3) The REAL demo config UI — AuroraConfigDock.vue + the 6 config/*Layer.vue panels (Medium/Palette/Nuclei/Composition/Flow/Texture) — operates DIRECTLY on the full AuroraConfig (e.g. MediumLayer.vue:22 `props.config.medium = ...`) and never calls resolveAtoms or deriveScene. So the substrate built to 'simplify the options' is bypassed by the only shipped UI.
findings.rootCause: AW shipped the simplification as ADDITIVE library substrate (resolveAtoms at W6, deriveScene at W5) layered ON TOP of the unchanged ~28-field config and the unchanged full-schema demo dock, instead of TRANSPOSING the demo's control surface onto the simplified model. The 'nothing is removed from AuroraConfig; full schema stays whole as the Advanced escape hatch' framing (atoms.ts header, DESIGN.md §5) is the root architectural error: it guaranteed two divergent doors plus a third raw-config UI that never converge. This is the substrate-without-consumer anti-pattern (J invariant 10 / overfitting-audit: every src/ artefact needs ≥2 real sites or is a demo helper) — resolveAtoms has 1 orphaned demo site, deriveScene has 0. The user asked to SIMPLIFY the options the consumer touches; the codebase instead ADDED two more option models.
findings.gestaltFix: Collapse to ONE consumer-facing control model and make the live demo config UI consume it. Decision: the simplified model becomes THE aurora config surface for the demo (and the README's documented door), with the full AuroraConfig demoted to a true internal author schema. Concretely: (a) pick the atoms model as the single door (it is the cleaner ≤7-knob shape the user described), (b) RETIRE deriveScene + AuroraMood entirely (a redundant second door with a divergent mood vocabulary), (c) fold deriveScene's only unique value (the mood→medium/temperatureShift/chromaEasing coupling) into resolveAtoms so one door covers it, (d) rebuild AuroraConfigDock to drive resolveAtoms-backed atoms (an 'atoms' tab as the default; the raw layers become the genuine Advanced disclosure), (e) route AuroraAtomsPanel (or its successor) into the manifest so the simplified door is the live aurora story. No parallel paths survive.
findings.evidence: src/components/custom/aurora/composables/atoms.ts:161 resolveAtoms; demo/stories/aurora/AuroraAtomsPanel.vue:37 sole consumer; manifest grep shows it unrouted (demo/stories/manifest.ts:95 registers only substrates/aurora→AuroraConfigDock); demo/stories/aurora/config/MediumLayer.vue:22 mutates full config directly; src/components/custom/aurora/composables/color.ts:369 deriveScene with 0 non-test consumers (grep); git ceccb92 (W6 atoms) + fa9083c (W5 deriveScene) — two doors one wave apart.

findings.requirement: §2.7 — gradient-art backdrops procedurally generated from ATOMS (zones, noise, color, control elements). The atoms-from-control-elements model.
findings.currentState: The shipped AuroraAtoms shape does NOT match the user's named control-element model. The user named the atoms as 'zones, noise, color (control elements)'. The current AuroraAtoms (atoms.ts:44-61) exposes: seed, harmony, mood, medium, textureAmount, motion, zones, interactivity. COLOR is split awkwardly across seed+harmony+mood(saturation). ZONES is present but is a bare integer count on a fixed thirdsZones prior — no control over placement, radius, or arrangement character. NOISE (the warp/fbm/cellular field — warpMode, warpScale, noiseOctaves, warpAmount) is NOT an atom at all (grep confirms NONE of warpMode/warpScale/noiseOctaves in atoms.ts); warpAmount is reached only indirectly as a side-effect of the mood atom. So the 'noise' control element the user explicitly named has no door.
findings.rootCause: The AW.W6 atom set was designed around the AUTHOR'S co-varying-energy framing (mood/medium/texture/motion as fan-out recipes) rather than the user's STRUCTURAL control-element framing (the backdrop is composed FROM zones + noise + color as orthogonal generative atoms). The two models are not the same axis decomposition: the user wants the noise field and the zone field to be first-class authoring atoms (the thing that makes a procedural gradient-art backdrop), and the current model buries noise inside mood and reduces zones to a count.
findings.gestaltFix: Re-derive the atom set from the user's control-element decomposition: COLOR (seed + harmony + a color-energy/saturation knob), ZONES (count + an arrangement character — e.g. scattered/composed/centred selecting among thirds/golden/radial priors, not just a bare integer), NOISE (one organic-boundary knob fanning to warpAmount/warpScale/warpMode — the named 'noise' element), plus MEDIUM + texture + MOTION. This stays ≤7 atoms but each atom maps to a control ELEMENT the user named, and the mood→energy fan-out is folded into the color/noise atoms rather than being its own knob. The orphaned interactivity atom (declared W6, only light+scroll partially wired per frameLoop.ts:66 / useAurora.ts:238; flow+wake dead) is either fully wired or excised per the §0 'excise or fail explicitly' mandate.
findings.evidence: REQUIREMENTS.md §2.7 'procedurally generated from ATOMS (zones, noise, color, control elements)'; src/components/custom/aurora/composables/atoms.ts:44-61 (atom set lacks a noise atom); grep: warpMode/warpScale/noiseOctaves absent from atoms.ts; atoms.ts:101 thirdsZones is a fixed prior with no arrangement control; AuroraInteractivity flow/wake axes unwired (frameLoop.ts only reads interactivity.light).

findings.requirement: §0 DRY / KISS — no duplicate logic; one source. §0 'no god modules, better encapsulation'.
findings.currentState: thirdsZones (atoms.ts:101-124) and thirdsNuclei (color.ts:276-300) are NEAR-IDENTICAL duplicate functions — same anchor table [[0.33,0.33],[0.67,0.67],...], same paletteBias/valueBias/driftRadius/driftPhase construction — diverging only in trivial clamping (atoms.ts also clamps to MAX_NUCLEI). Separately, the mood→energy mapping exists TWICE with divergent vocabularies: atoms.ts MOOD_ENERGY (calm/balanced/vivid → saturation/warpAmount/valueVariance/breathDepth) and color.ts MOOD_RECIPE (atmospheric/painterly/vivid/muted → the same four axes + more). Two mood vocabularies for the same four config fields.

The shared-source discipline that AW applied rigorously to COLOR math (the /color leaf hoist, proof:single-color-core) was never applied to the COMPOSITION priors — so the nuclei-placement prior and the mood recipe forked.

If a thirds prior is needed by both runtime and the door, hoist it to one composable (the same pattern as the /color leaf). No second copy.

result.slice: aurora-webgpu-state — the W7 createGPUCanvas / WGSL / Kuwahara WebGPU path (§2.4 "Modern WebGPU rendering techniques")

findings.requirement: §2.4 — Modern WebGPU rendering techniques. The W7 WebGPU path must be REAL and WORKING (not scaffold): on a WebGPU-capable machine the live <Aurora> must paint the same image as the WebGL2 path.
findings.currentState: The WebGPU path is WIRED end-to-end (renderMode probe -> runtime swap -> createGPUCanvas -> gpuRuntime setup -> AURORA_WGSL draw) and it DOES bind on capable machines — but it renders PURE BLACK [0,0,0,255]. The DOM NucleiOverlay rings are the only thing visible. Preset thumbnails bake correctly only because usePresetThumbnails uses mode:'capture' which is WebGL2-only and never runs the WebGPU swap.
findings.rootCause: A WGSL address-space miscompile. aurora.wgsl.ts:74-77 declares the dynamically-indexed arrays palette/nucleiPos/nucleiMod INSIDE the `var<uniform> U: Uniforms` struct (:79). On Apple/Metal (Tint->Metal codegen) a RUNTIME index into a `var<uniform> array<vec4f>` returns [0,0,0,0]; samplePalette (aurora.wgsl.ts:117-123, i0/i1 runtime) and nucleiField (:146-155, U.nucleiPos[i] in a runtime loop) therefore sample a zeroed palette -> black. The color math (OETF/OKLab/aces) is correct in isolation. The WGSL header comment even claims 'a storage buffer is dynamically sized' yet binds var<uniform> — the INTENT was storage, the implementation is uniform. This is fully diagnosed in docs/tranches/AX/audit/W01-aurora-webgpu-blackcanvas.md.
findings.gestaltFix: Split the bind layout: keep the 16 constant-indexed scalars (time..alpha) in a small `var<uniform>` block, and move the three dynamically-indexed arrays into one `struct Field { palette; nucleiPos; nucleiMod }` bound `var<storage, read>` at a second binding. In gpuRuntime.ts allocate the field buffer GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE|COPY_DST and add the bind-group entry; in uniformBridge.ts packGPUUniforms keep the same Float32 std140 packing but write the array region to the storage buffer (the 16-byte vec4 stride is already storage-correct). Free win: storage is runtime-sized, lifting the MAX_STOPS=8/MAX_NUCLEI=6 caps the WGSL header already aspired to. Storage dynamic-indexing is well-defined on EVERY WebGPU backend — no per-driver branch.
findings.evidence: src/components/custom/aurora/constants/shaders/aurora.wgsl.ts:74-79 (arrays in var<uniform>), :117-123 (samplePalette runtime index), :146-155 (nucleiField runtime loop); src/components/custom/aurora/composables/runtime.ts:177-189 (the GPU swap); docs/tranches/AX/audit/W01-aurora-webgpu-blackcanvas.md (pixel-level live confirmation); commit c17b74c (W7b origin)

result.slice: blob-breakage

findings.requirement: §3.1 BLOB — TOTALLY BROKEN (confirmed live). Root-cause the total blob breakage; diff the W9-W11 merge against the working pre-AW GooBlob.
findings.currentState: CONFIRMED LIVE on all three blob stories (/substrates/goo-blob, /blob-interaction, /blob-mood). The blob does NOT render as a gooey metaball droplet — it paints a GIANT canvas-filling rounded slab hard-clipped at the canvas top/right/bottom edges. No console errors, no GL context loss, the shader COMPILES and the W9.b lit rim / W11.a iridescence sheen actually paint CORRECTLY on the visible curved edge. The defect is purely geometric: the SDF body+satellite composite over-merges and floods the whole [-0.5,0.5] UV field. Breakage is config-invariant (identical on all 3 stories with different configs), so it is a pipeline-scale regression, not a per-config value.
findings.rootCause: The W9.a smin-normalization refactor (commit 799d5a8) changed the uSmoothK SEMANTIC REGIME — it added `k *= 4.0` to sminQuadratic (sdf-body.glsl.ts:29) so the blend band reads in true distance units, and DELETED the renderer's `/0.22` magic normalizer AND the `POS_SCALE` multiply on the uSmoothK upload (useMetaballRenderer.ts:437-440). But the THREE coupled inputs were never re-tuned for the new regime: (1) config default smoothK dropped 0.22→0.12 (types.ts:167) but the mood smoothK lerp range was LEFT at 0.16-0.32 (useBlobMood.ts:45), so the renderer's `config.smoothK * (params.smoothK / DEFAULTS.smoothK)` = 0.12*(0.216/0.12) = 0.216 uploaded; (2) the in-shader `k *= 4.0` then makes effectiveK = 0.864; (3) no POS_SCALE compression. Empirically reproduced in-page: effectiveK = 0.864 in a UV space only 1.0 wide (half-extent 0.5), seam-pull = 0.216 distance units — the smin's `min(a,b) - 0.216` floods the composite distance field NEGATIVE (inside) across nearly the whole canvas → alpha=1 everywhere. That is a 6.28x larger blend band than the OLD working regime (effectiveK 0.1375, seam-pull 0.034). The body-to-satellite gap is already -0.019 (satellites overlap the body at default orbit), so even modest over-merge fuses them; 0.864 is a total flood. `proof:blob-smin-normalized` shipped GREEN because it validates the smin FUNCTION's seam-depth==k property in pure-math isolation and grep-checks the fudge removal — it never composes the actual uploaded value against the body scale and never renders a pixel (the cardinal AW headless-green/visually-broken gap).
findings.gestaltFix: Reconcile the uSmoothK pipeline as ONE coherent distance regime, then lock it with a RENDERED-PIXEL gate. (a) Re-derive the config default + mood smoothK lerp range against the post-normalization k semantics so the COMPOSED uploaded uSmoothK lands a tight wet meniscus (~0.03-0.08 effective seam-pull, matching the working 0.034) — i.e. a default smoothK ~0.04-0.05 and a mood range scaled down ~5x (the old working composed band was 0.1375 effective). (b) Decide POS_SCALE policy COHERENTLY: every length-like uniform (bodyRadius, satRadius, orbit, pulse, noise) is POS_SCALE-compressed into the visible 62.5% inner region — the smin band is ALSO a length and MUST ride the same compression, so re-apply POS_SCALE to the uSmoothK upload (the W9.a deletion of it was the error, not the /0.22 deletion). (c) Sync the README (lines 91, 142 document the dead 0.22/0.28 regime). (d) The mood smoothK is a unitless MULTIPLIER per the renderer comment (`params.smoothK / DEFAULTS.smoothK`) — make that explicit: store mood smoothK as a 1.0-centred scalar, not an absolute distance, so a config retune doesn't silently re-scale every mood. This is a gestalt re-derivation of the merge-band scale, not a magic-number patch.
findings.evidence: Live: 3 screenshots (blob-goo-blob-story.png, blob-interaction-story.png, blob-mood-story.png) all show the canvas-filling slab. In-page reproduction: uploaded uSmoothK=0.216 → effectiveK=0.864 → seamDepth=0.216 vs UV half-extent 0.5 (OVER-MERGE), 6.28x the old working band. Code: sdf-body.glsl.ts:28-32 (`k *= 4.0`); useMetaballRenderer.ts:437-440 (upload, no POS_SCALE); useBlobMood.ts:45 (`smoothK: lerp(0.16, 0.32, arousal)` un-rescaled); types.ts:167 (`smoothK: 0.12`). Pre-merge oracle (git 067473c): useMetaballRenderer.ts:273 `((config.smoothK * params.smoothK) / 0.22) * POS_SCALE`, mood smoothK 0.16-0.32 but config default 0.22, sdf smin with no 4x → working effectiveK 0.1375. Regression introduced in merge a47d293 (W9 commits 799d5a8 + 953fdf4).

findings.requirement: §0/§13 — the headless-green / visually-broken GAP: a wave is not closed on a green gate; it closes on a live Playwright + frontend-design audit.
findings.currentState: `proof:blob-smin-normalized` (scripts/proof-blob-smin-normalized.mjs) is GREEN at HEAD yet the blob is totally broken. The gate's two clauses are (1) a grep that the `/0.22` + POS_SCALE fudges are GONE — which is exactly the change that BROKE the render — and (2) a pure-math k-sweep asserting the smin function's seam-depth==k in isolation. Neither composes `config.smoothK * params.smoothK / DEFAULTS` against the body radius, neither renders a pixel. The gate's own premise (`uSmoothK is a true distance`) is technically satisfied while the live distance value (0.864) is catastrophic for a 1.0-wide UV. This is the canonical AW false-green: the gate certified the very deletion that shipped the regression.
findings.rootCause: The W9-W11 blob gates are all static-text / pure-math analyzers (smin-normalized, gradient-unit-length, spec-premult, space-gamma, mood-resolved, tempo-suppression) that test shader sub-properties in isolation. None mounts the component, renders to a canvas, and asserts on the painted pixel distribution (e.g. opaque-fraction in a sane band, a centered bounded droplet, non-clipped edges). ROOT CAUSE LOCKED with empirical proof. The blob breakage is NOT a blank canvas, a failed shader compile, a broken import, or a spring-API mismatch (all verified sound) — it is a GEOMETRIC over-merge: the W9.a smin-normalization (commit 799d5a8, merge a47d293) added `k *= 4.0` to the shader and deleted the renderer's `/0.22` + POS_SCALE fudges, but the coupled config default (0.22→0.12), the mood smoothK lerp (left at 0.16-0.32), and the missing POS_SCALE were never reconciled. Net: live uploaded uSmoothK=0.216 → in-shader effectiveK=0.864 in a 1.0-wide UV space (6.28x the working band), flooding the SDF field negative across the whole canvas. Confirmed config-invariant across all 3 live stories (screenshots saved at repo root: blob-goo-blob-story.png, blob-interaction-story.png, blob-mood-story.png).

KEY META-FINDING: proof:blob-smin-normalized is GREEN while the blob is totally broken — it grep-certified the exact fudge-deletion that broke the render and only k-sweeps the smin function in pure-math isolation. This is the textbook AW headless-green/visually-broken trap the AX mandate calls out. Every blob W9-W11 gate is static/pure-math; none renders a pixel. W02 is the structural antidote.

GOOD NEWS for the fix: the W9.b lit rim (Blinn-Phong + Fresnel) and W11.a iridescence/SSS sheen RENDER CORRECTLY (visible on the slab's curved edge in blob-mood-story.png) — the OKLCh splice, multi-stop palette indexing, surfaceNormal, and all lit blocks execute fine. Caveat on method: WebGL readPixels/drawImage returned 0 (preserveDrawingBuffer:false clears post-composite + the demand-loop parks); the on-screen SCREENSHOT is the visual truth and the in-page numeric reproduction is the proof — do not trust readback against this substrate.

The dev server I started (vite :5199) was killed at the end.

result.slice: blob-interaction-visual — §3.2 (visual style / animation / interaction design) + §3.1 (TOTALLY BROKEN) + §3.4 (performance) for the GooBlob soft-body metaball

findings.requirement: §3.1 — the blob is TOTALLY BROKEN (confirmed live). §3.2 — visually appealing + intuitive. The blob must read as a CONTAINED, organic, gooey creature/droplet sitting within its footprint.
findings.currentState: CONFIRMED LIVE (Playwright, M-series, dpr 2). On all three blob stories (/substrates/goo-blob, /blob-interaction, /blob-mood) the blob renders as a GIANT near-square rounded-rectangle of flat color that FILLS its entire container and is hard-clipped by the container's rounded-card + overflow-hidden. A center-scanline framebuffer readback measured 84.1% horizontal coverage of the canvas — and the canvas is 160% of the wrapper, so the merged field spans ~1.34x the visible footprint and overflows on every side. There is NO contained droplet, NO visible separated satellites, NO organic gooey membrane edge — just a clipped color box. The creature identity is entirely absent.
findings.rootCause: The W9.a smin normalization (commit 799d5a8) is the regression. It changed sminQuadratic to pre-scale k *= 4.0 (sdf-body.glsl.ts:29) so uSmoothK is a 'true blend-band in distance units', and dropped BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.smoothK from 0.22 to 0.12. Live uniform readback shows uSmoothK=0.21 (after the mood multiplier), which becomes effective k=0.84 inside sminQuadratic — a blend band nearly 5x the body radius (uBodyRadius=0.156). With a body at r=0.156 plus 3 satellites (r=0.081) at distance ~0.22 plus the 15-sample pointer trail, each smin-merge subtracts up to k*0.25=0.21 distance units, so the merged isosurface INFLATES far past the sum of the radii and balloons to the canvas edges. The normalization math is internally self-consistent (the k-sweep gate passes) but the NET RENDERED SIZE was never visually validated — uSmoothK, uBodyRadius, satellite radii/positions and the trail were never re-balanced against the new normalized smin scale. metaball.frag.ts:185-202 merges body + 3 sats + 15 trail samples all at this oversized band.
findings.gestaltFix: Re-derive the blob geometry as ONE coherent budget against the normalized smin, not by nudging one constant: (a) treat the wrapper footprint as the hard visual bound and solve bodyRadius + orbitRadius + satelliteRadius + the smin band so the WHOLE merged field (body + sats at widest orbit + trail) fits inside ~70-80% of the wrapper with intentional overflow margin only for the orbit excursion — drop POS_SCALE as a hidden fudge and express every length directly in wrapper-normalized units; (b) bring smoothK down to the real wet-meniscus band (~0.04-0.08 effective, i.e. config ~0.04-0.05 post k*=4) so the seam reads as a rounded neck, not a melted balloon; (c) gate it with a NEW real-GPU render proof (proof:blob-render — instantiate the blob, draw one frame, read back, assert field coverage is within a contained band e.g. 0.25-0.6 of the canvas AND non-zero AND a transparent margin exists), the only assertion that catches this class. This is the cardinal AX visual-truth gate the blob is missing.
findings.evidence: Live framebuffer scanline readback: rowCoverage 0.841, x0/x05 alpha 0 → x25/x50/x95 alpha 255 → x100 alpha 0. Screenshots blob-goo-story.png, blob-interaction.png, blob-mood.png (all show a clipped color box). git show 799d5a8 (W9.a: k*=4.0, smoothK 0.22→0.12). Live uniforms: uBodyRadius=0.156, uSmoothK=0.209, uSatCount=3, uSatRadius=0.081, uSatPos0=[-0.22,-0.07]. sdf-body.glsl.ts:28-32; metaball.frag.ts:185-202.

findings.requirement: §3.2 — visual style + animation design must be visually appealing. The lit-glass droplet surface (W9.b spec/Fresnel/normal), iridescence + fake-SSS (W11.a) must read as a wet, dimensional, premium glass creature.
findings.currentState: Despite lit:true + iridescence:0.4 + sssScale:0.25 + coreGlow:0.12 on the mood/interaction stories, the rendered blob is essentially FLAT colored paint. Live RGB across the body varies only [79,174,255]→[126,190,255] — a near-uniform sky blue with no visible specular glint, no clear Fresnel rim, no dimensional dome read. The mood story shows a faint pale top sheen (the only lighting cue that survives), but it reads as a gradient on a box, not a lit droplet. The surface work that the W9/W11 waves shipped is invisible.
findings.rootCause: Two compounding causes. (1) The surface lighting is computed but VISUALLY SWAMPED: because the field is a giant flat-interior box (finding 1), thickness=clamp(-d/bodyR) saturates to ~1 across almost the whole surface (metaball.frag.ts:300), so the Fresnel term fres=pow(1-dot(N,V),2.5) is ~0 everywhere except the hard-clipped 1px edge that overflow-hidden cuts off — the rim literally renders outside the visible box. The surfaceNormal dome lift (z=sqrt(1-(1-interior)^2)) points straight at the viewer across the whole flat interior, so N·V≈1, killing every angle-dependent term (spec, rim, irid, SSS all gate on fres/normal-tilt). (2) The lit/irid/SSS terms are all OFF in BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS (lit:false, iridescence:0, sssScale:0, coreGlow:0), so the DEFAULT blob — what most consumers and the first story mount — is flat by construction; the surface material is opt-in and only the hand-tuned stories enable it. The surface quality and the geometry are coupled: fix the contained-droplet shape and the lighting reappears (a small dome has a real rim), but the defaults must also ship the lit look, not hide it.
findings.gestaltFix: Make the lit warm-glass droplet the DEFAULT identity, not an opt-in: turn on a tasteful lit + low iridescence + low SSS in BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS so an un-configured blob reads as glass out of the box (the README already claims 'warm-cream glass identity'). AND re-anchor the normal/thickness on the CONTAINED body from finding 1 so fres/rim actually live on a curved rim inside the footprint. Re-tune the dome profile so the highlight rolls across a believable sphere rather than saturating flat. Validate with a render gate that asserts luminance VARIANCE across the body (a flat fill fails; a lit dome passes) — not just 'non-black'.
findings.evidence: Live scanline RGB [79,174,255]→[126,190,255] (near-flat). Screenshot blob-mood.png (faint top sheen, clipped box). metaball.frag.ts:300 thickness, :301 fres, :351-374 lit block, :311-321 iridescence, :298 surfaceNormal. BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS lit:false/iridescence:0/sssScale:0/coreGlow:0 (types.ts:185-192).

findings.requirement: §3.2 — interaction design must be visually appealing + intuitive (pointer-follow lean, velocity squash-and-stretch, the decaying-radius elastic pseudopod trail, click-squish, mood drift).
findings.currentState: The interaction PLUMBING is live and correct at the data level — live readback while jittering the pointer shows uPointerActive=1, the critically-damped spring tracks (uPointer follows), uVelocity is non-zero (squash input present), the trail builds to the full 15 samples, mood machinery ticks. But NONE of it is VISIBLE, because every interaction effect (lean deform, squash, pseudopod, click bounce) is a perturbation of a field that already fills and overflows the clipped box — you cannot see a pseudopod reach toward the cursor, a directional squash, or a contained body lean when the body is a full-bleed square. The intuitive 'creature reacts to me' read is zero.
findings.rootCause: Same root as finding 1: the oversize geometry destroys the legibility of every motion. The interaction model is not broken — it is INVISIBLE because there is no contained silhouette for the motion to deform. Secondarily, the trail (uTrailCount=15) and the satellites both feed the same oversized smin, so they add mass rather than reading as distinct reaching limbs / orbiting moons. The squash (uStretch=0.4, volume-preserving anisotropic UV warp) acts on a box, so it just reshapes the box edges that are clipped off-screen.
findings.gestaltFix: No new interaction code is needed — fixing the contained-droplet geometry (finding 1) makes the EXISTING spring/trail/squash/mood instantly legible. After that, re-balance the interaction MAGNITUDES against the new smaller body: scale pointerStrength, trail radius, and stretch so a hover-flick produces a clearly readable lean+pseudopod+recover within the footprint (the current values were tuned against the oversized field). Add a visual interaction gate (render a frame mid-gesture, assert the centroid/bounding-box shifts toward the pointer) so the felt interaction is machine-locked, not just the PRM/single-loop structure the current proof:blob-interaction-prm checks.
findings.evidence: Live pointer jitter readback: uPointerActive=1, uPointer tracks [-0.06,0.11]→[0.12,0.10], uVelocity non-zero up to [0.05,-0.57], uTrailCount ramps 12→15, uStretch=0.4. useBlobPointer.ts:114-160 (spring+trail), metaball.frag.ts:172-179 (squash), :195-202 (trail merge). The data is sound; the visual is occluded by finding 1.

findings.requirement: §3.2 — the organic membrane edge (domain-warped FBM watercolor silhouette) must read as a living membrane, not a clean geometric circle/box.
findings.currentState: The edge is effectively smooth/geometric — no organic watercolor wobble is visible. Live uNoiseAmp=0.015 (the mood-scaled value off config noiseAmp=0.025) is far too small to deform the edge perceptibly at this body scale, and what little displacement exists is invisible because the edge is overflow-clipped into a straight box side.
findings.rootCause: Two causes: (1) noiseAmp default (0.025, mood-scaled to ~0.015) is a taste-first 'low' value that produces sub-pixel edge motion on a body of r=0.156 — the membrane character the README and PATH-FORWARD §3 promise ('living membrane') never manifests. (2) The clipped box (finding 1) means the actual SDF edge is mostly OUTSIDE the visible footprint, so even a larger displacement would be cut off — only the top arc of the mood-story blob shows the true SDF edge, and it is a clean curve. The domain warp (warpAmp=0.6 on the interaction story) rides this too-small amplitude so its marbling is invisible.
findings.gestaltFix: Once the body is contained (finding 1), raise the default edge displacement to a perceptible-but-calm band and verify the warped FBM reads as an organic membrane on the visible silhouette. Tie noiseAmp/noiseFreq to the new body scale so the wobble is proportional. Tune the FBM lacunarity/persistence toward the 'liquid not rocky' constants the PATH-FORWARD §3 cites (1.8 / 0.42) and de-sync the breath pulse (currently a single sin) so the membrane never reads mechanical. Validate edge-roughness via a render gate measuring silhouette deviation from a perfect circle.
findings.evidence: Live uNoiseAmp=0.015, uWarpAmp=0.60, uNoiseFreq=3.5. BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS noiseAmp:0.025 (types.ts:172). watercolor-edges.glsl.ts:65-86 (fbm/fbmWarped). PATH-FORWARD.md §3 (liquid-tune constants + de-synced breath, not yet applied). Screenshot blob-mood.png top arc is a clean geometric curve.

findings.requirement: §0 / cardinal AX lesson — a wave is not closed on a green headless gate; it closes on a live Playwright + frontend-design audit. The blob's whole visual contract must be machine-locked against a REAL rendered frame.
findings.currentState: All ~9 blob proof gates (proof:blob-value-free, -space-gamma, -smin-normalized, -gradient-unit-length, -spec-premult, -interaction-prm, -mood-resolved, -tempo-suppression, -color-equivalence) are CPU/structure/grep/TS-port checks. NOT ONE instantiates the GL context and asserts the blob renders as a contained, lit, organic droplet. This is precisely why the W9.a oversize regression shipped green: proof:blob-smin-normalized validated the k-sweep math while the rendered blob ballooned to fill its box. The blob is the exact 'headless-green / visually-broken' gap AX exists to close, mirroring the AX.W01 aurora black-canvas finding (gate-philosophy gap).
findings.rootCause: The blob's quality contract is encoded entirely as math/structure invariants that hold in isolation but say nothing about the composed rendered image. There is no GPU-render assertion in the fleet, so any change that is locally-correct-but-globally-wrong (a normalization that re-scales every dependent constant) sails through.
findings.gestaltFix: Add a real-GPU render gate for the blob (Playwright+Chrome WebGL lane, or headless SwiftShader): instantiate GooBlob with BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS, draw frames at t=0..N, read back, and assert (a) field coverage in a contained band with a transparent margin (catches the oversize), (b) non-trivial luminance variance across the body (catches flat-fill, finding 2), (c) a measurable pointer-driven centroid shift under a synthetic gesture (catches invisible interaction, finding 3), (d) a non-zero silhouette deviation from a circle (catches the dead membrane, finding 4). This converts every blob finding above from 'looks right today' to 'the real device paints the contained lit creature'. Pair with a frontend-design visual review at wave close.
findings.evidence: package.json:593-617 (all blob gates are node scripts / vitest TS-port — zero GPUDevice render). docs/tranches/AX/audit/W01-aurora-webgpu-blackcanvas.md compounding-finding #1 names the identical gate-philosophy gap for aurora. REQUIREMENTS.md §0 (VISUAL TRUTH) + §13 (the headless-green/visually-broken GAP as a standing gate-philosophy wave).

findings.requirement: §3.4 — performance: smooth without sacrificing visual quality; trim the wasted fragment cost.
findings.currentState: The loop runs at ~120fps (72 draws/600ms measured) so it is smooth, but it pays gross wasted fill-rate: the canvas is CSS-sized 1.6x the wrapper (2.56x the fragments), and because the field overflows to fill it (finding 1) every fragment runs the full FBM-twice + OKLCh-roundtrip + 4-tap surfaceNormal (each tap re-evaluates sceneDist = 3 sats + 15 trail merges). The 15-iteration trail loop runs even when uTrailCount=0 on the static stories (the for-loop has a dynamic break but the satellite/trail plumbing always uploads). On the default flat blob the lit/irid/SSS branches are off so that cost is avoided, but the oversize means near-100% of the oversized canvas is shaded.
findings.rootCause: The 1.6x oversize margin (POS_SCALE=0.625 + canvas 160%, useMetaballRenderer.ts:32, GooBlob.vue:203-213) was sized for satellite-orbit overflow but is mostly transparent border paying full FBM cost — and the broken geometry turns that margin opaque. PATH-FORWARD §5 (AW.Wb9) already specced the fix (oversize trim + pre-FBM bounding discard + optional half-res) but it never ran. surfaceNormal's 4 sceneDist taps quadruple the field cost per pixel for the lit path.
findings.gestaltFix: Fold the perf trim into the geometry rebuild (finding 1): once the field is contained, trim the canvas oversize to the measured-minimal orbit envelope, add the cheap pre-FBM bounding discard (length(uv) > maxReach → return transparent before the two FBM calls), and gate the surfaceNormal 4-tap behind the lit/irid/SSS path only. Optionally add the quality:'full'|'half' axis from PATH-FORWARD §5 for weak GPUs. Validate fill cost in the same render gate (assert the transparent-margin fraction).
findings.evidence: 72 draws/600ms (~120fps) live. useMetaballRenderer.ts:32 (POS_SCALE), GooBlob.vue:203-213 (160% canvas). metaball.frag.ts:221-233 surfaceNormal 4x sceneDist, :188-202 sceneDist merges 3 sats + 15 trail. PATH-FORWARD.md §5 / wave-seeds AW.Wb9 (oversize trim + half-res, never run).

findings.requirement: §3.3 — seamless integration with the rest of glass-ui (the blob sits IN the warm-cream glass system, not as a generic cold liquid bubble).
findings.currentState: Integration is shallow and partly broken. The only tie to glass-ui is a CSS drop-shadow on the wrapper (GooBlob.vue:187-199). The blob's identity color in the default story is the warm var(--primary) but the interaction/mood stories use a cold oklch(0.7 0.16 250) sky blue — the live blob reads as exactly the 'generic cold liquid-glass bubble' the README warns against. The default palette is a single perturbed tint, not derived from glass-ui tokens, so an un-themed blob has no built-in warm-cream anchor. findings.gestaltFix: Derive the DEFAULT blob palette from glass-ui warm tokens (a warm anchor / --primary family) so an un-configured blob belongs to the cream-glass system, and ship the lit warm-cream rim ON by default (finding 2) so the warm marriage is visible. Keep cold/neon as explicit consumer opt-in (presets-in-consumers). Re-point the demo stories' default color to the warm identity so the storybook shows the house look, not a cold bubble.

result.notes: VISUAL TRUTH established live (Playwright, M-series, dpr 2, dev server on :5173) — not inferred from code. The headline: §3.1 'TOTALLY BROKEN' is REAL and PIXEL-LEVEL ROOT-CAUSED. The blob is NOT failing to render and is NOT a WebGPU/black-canvas case (unlike aurora AX.W01 — the blob is WebGL2-only and its loop runs at ~120fps, 72 draws/600ms). It renders a GIANT flat clipped color box that overflows its footprint (measured 84.1% canvas coverage = ~1.34x the wrapper). Single root cause: the W9.a smin normalization (commit 799d5a8, k*=4.0 + smoothK 0.22→0.12) makes effective k=0.84 — a blend band ~5x the body radius — which inflates the body+3-satellites+15-trail merged field to fill the box. Every other defect cascades from this: the lit surface is swamped because thickness saturates flat and the Fresnel rim renders outside the clipped box; the interaction (which is fully wired and live at the data level — spring tracks, velocity non-zero, trail builds to 15) is invisible because there is no contained silhouette to deform; the organic membrane is invisible because noiseAmp is sub-pixel AND the edge is clipped. So AX.W12 (contained geometry) is the keystone — fixing it resurfaces the W9/W10/W11 work that already shipped but paints nothing. The deeper systemic finding: all ~9 blob proof gates are CPU/structure/grep checks; proof:blob-smin-normalized validated the k-sweep math GREEN while the rendered blob ballooned — the exact headless-green/visually-broken gap (AX cardinal lesson) that lets this class regress. AX.W15 (real-GPU render gate) is mandatory, not optional. Diagnostic screenshots: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/blob-goo-story.png, blob-interaction.png, blob-mood.png. Key source: src/components/custom/goo-blob/shaders/sdf-body.glsl.ts:28-32, metaball.frag.ts:185-202 + :298-374, types.ts:155-215 (defaults), composables/useMetaballRenderer.ts:32 (POS_SCALE), GooBlob.vue:203-213. result.slice: blob-integration-perf — Blob integration with glass-ui + performance (the shared WebGL substrate, park/PRM). Audit of useMetaballRenderer + useWebGLCanvas/createCanvasLifecycle substrate.

findings.requirement: §3.3 Seamless integration with glass-ui — the documented WCAG 2.2.2 pause/resume seam (DockBackgroundToggle) must actually work.
findings.currentState: BROKEN. GooBlob.vue:148 `defineExpose({ nudge, setMood, pulse, currentMood })` omits `pause`/`resume`. The renderer DOES return them — useMetaballRenderer.ts:558-567 returns `{ pause, resume }` — but GooBlob.vue:94 calls `useMetaballRenderer({...})` and DISCARDS the return value (no assignment). So `blob.value.pause()` is `undefined` at every consumer call site. The DockBackgroundToggle.vue JSDoc (lines 22-24), the README 'Exposed via defineExpose' table (README.md:120), and the README worked example (README.md:341 `blob.value?.pause()`) all document a seam that does not exist.
findings.rootCause: The blob's primary glass-ui integration contract is the WCAG-2.2.2 AV-background pause control, and that contract is a runtime no-op because the component never re-exposes the renderer's pause handle. This is the canonical headless-green/visually-broken gap: typecheck passes (the methods exist on the renderer return type, which is just discarded), every gate is green, but the actual cross-component integration is dead. The optional-chaining `?.` in the README example silently swallows the undefined, so even a consumer following the docs gets a button that does nothing with zero error.
findings.gestaltFix: Capture the renderer handle and re-expose it: `const { pause, resume } = useMetaballRenderer({...})` then `defineExpose({ nudge, setMood, pulse, currentMood, pause, resume })`. Then ADD an in-repo proof that the live blob story wires DockBackgroundToggle to a mounted GooBlob and asserts the rAF actually parks on pause (a real-DOM/Playwright gate, not a defineExpose-string regex — the AX gate-philosophy lesson). Better: collapse the two-step entirely by having GooBlob accept a `v-model:paused` prop and own the pause itself, so the consumer never has to reach into a ref — the seam becomes declarative and cannot be left unexposed.
findings.evidence: src/components/custom/goo-blob/GooBlob.vue:94,148 (renderer return discarded; pause/resume not exposed) vs useMetaballRenderer.ts:558-567 (returns pause/resume) vs DockBackgroundToggle.vue:22-24 + README.md:120,341 (documents the seam as live)

findings.requirement: §3.4 Performance — modern web tech, smooth without sacrificing visual quality; the substrate's demand-driven loop must actually save work when the blob is idle.
findings.currentState: The demand gate is a no-op for the blob. useMetaballRenderer.ts:518-519 `shouldContinue() { return !paused }` — so unless manually paused, the rAF reschedules forever (createCanvasLifecycle.ts:106-109 keeps requesting frames while `shouldContinue()` is true). The renderer comment (line 512) even states 'the blob is perpetually animated.' A small idle accent blob (the README's #1 use case, '≈7rem ambient brand mark, slow, calm') burns a full 60fps rAF — FBM x3 octaves twice per pixel + a full OKLCh round-trip per fragment — indefinitely. The substrate built an entire demand-gate (`shouldContinue`) the blob deliberately defeats.
findings.rootCause: The blob has no notion of 'at rest.' Mood (idle), satellites (perpetual orbit), and pulse all run forever, so there is never a frame where nothing changes. But that is a DESIGN choice, not a hard requirement — an idle blob at rest is visually near-static and could throttle to a low cadence or park between satellite phase transitions. The substrate's whole offscreen-park machinery is upstream of this; the ONSCREEN idle case (the common one for an ambient accent) gets zero relief because shouldContinue is hardwired true. The 'park aggressively' README claim only covers offscreen/hidden/PRM, never the onscreen-idle hot path.
findings.gestaltFix: Give the blob a genuine quiescence signal feeding `shouldContinue`: when mood is settled (not transitioning), the pointer spring is at rest (|v|<eps), the trail is collapsed, the click pulse is 0, AND no satellite is mid-merge transition, return false and let the substrate park — then `wake()` from the satellite scheduler when the next orbit/merge phase is due (the satellite system already knows its phase timers). This converts the perpetual loop into an event-scheduled one: the blob renders when something is actually changing. Combine with the README's '(Planned — AW)' `quality: full|half` axis (half-res metaball pass + bilinear upsample, ~4x fragment savings) which never shipped — wire it now. This is the single biggest fill/battery lever after the offscreen-park.
findings.evidence: src/components/custom/goo-blob/composables/useMetaballRenderer.ts:511-520 (shouldContinue returns !paused, comment 'perpetually animated'); createCanvasLifecycle.ts:106-109 (reschedules while shouldContinue true); README.md:275 (quality:half marked planned, never shipped)

findings.requirement: §3.4 Performance — the multi-instance / WebGL-context-cap case (the storybook mounts several blobs on one page).
findings.currentState: Each GooBlob grabs its OWN webgl2 context via createWebGLCanvas (one per instance, useWebGLCanvas.ts:110). The goo-blob story mounts 3 live <GooBlob>, blob-mood mounts 2, blob-interaction 1 — and the demo navigates between them. Chromium caps ~8-16 live WebGL contexts/page (the substrate comment useWebGLCanvas.ts:124 names '~8 in Chromium' and forces a WEBGL_lose_context release on teardown to mitigate). Context release only happens on dispose (unmount). git archaeology: commit 9427536 'fix(blob): lazy-mount via IntersectionObserver — Chrome MCP audit caught WebGL context-cap exhaustion' — this failure class was hit live before. The IntersectionPause park stops the rAF but does NOT release the context, so an offscreen-but-mounted blob still holds a context slot.
findings.rootCause: There is no context pooling/sharing across blob instances. The substrate is one-context-per-canvas by construction. For a grid of N decorative blobs (a documented use case) this linearly consumes the scarce per-page context budget; on a busy consumer page (aurora + several blobs + constellation, all WebGL) the cap is reachable and the Nth context creation silently fails or evicts the oldest. The mitigation (lose_context on dispose) only helps on UNMOUNT, not while many are mounted-but-idle.
findings.gestaltFix: Two-tier: (1) for the multi-instance grid case, render every blob in ONE shared context+canvas via a single full-page transparent canvas with per-instance viewport scissoring, or via a 2D-canvas/CSS fallback for the static (non-interactive) instances — a decorative thumbnail does not need its own GL context. (2) Make the static/ambient register reuse WatercolorDot (the explicit CSS/SVG sibling) where no per-pixel GL is needed — the README already frames them as 'deliberate siblings'; the blob grid story is exactly the case that should be WatercolorDots, reserving GooBlob for the ONE interactive hero. Add a real-browser gate that mounts N blobs and asserts context-count stays bounded.
findings.evidence: src/composables/glass/webgl/useWebGLCanvas.ts:110,124-125 (one getContext per canvas, lose_context only on teardown); demo/stories/substrates/goo-blob.vue (3 live mounts), blob-mood.vue (2), blob-interaction.vue (1); commit 9427536 (prior context-cap exhaustion incident)

findings.requirement: §3.1/§3.2 Visual truth — the blob must render as the W9/W10/W11 lit wet droplet it claims; the live story must be visually verified (not headless-green).
findings.currentState: The shipped DEFAULT renders FLAT. BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS has `lit:false`, `iridescence:0`, `sssScale:0`, `coreGlow:0`, `warpAmp:0`, `paletteStops:[]` (types.ts:185-194) — so every W9.b (Blinn-Phong glint + Fresnel rim), W11.a (iridescence + SSS), and W11.b (palette) feature is OFF by default. The goo-blob.vue story passes BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS verbatim, so the canonical demo shows a flat fill — exactly what the F-tranche capture (docs/tranches/F/audit/screenshots/W1/runtime/substrates-goo-blob.png) shows: 3 flat colored blobs, no wet-bead shading. AND the first grid blob (color `var(--primary)`) is INVISIBLE in that capture — only 3 of 4 paint. The W9 audit JSON browserVerify field is literally 'PENDING' — the lit droplet was never visually confirmed.
findings.rootCause: The whole W9/W10/W11 SOTA-droplet investment is gated behind opt-in flags that default OFF for 'zero regression', so the as-shipped blob is the pre-W9 flat sticker — the very thing the requirement calls TOTALLY BROKEN. The defaults encode a backwards-compat instinct (forbidden by §0 'no legacy, excise or fail') in a greenfield dev product. The missing first blob is a separate bug: `var(--primary)` resolves through TWO independent cascade-read paths (GooBlob.vue resolveColorString + useMetaballRenderer resolveRimColor) and in dark mode --primary is near-white; combined with `mix-blend`/premultiplied-alpha + the wrapper drop-shadow it can wash out to nothing on a dark page — a contrast/visibility failure, not a paint failure.
findings.gestaltFix: Make the SHIPPED default the wet droplet: turn on lit + a tasteful iridescence/SSS floor in BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS so the canonical look IS the SOTA look (presets in consumers, the library's own identity evolves — per the user's own memory note). Delete the 'zero regression' flag-gating as legacy. Then close the W9 browserVerify with a live Playwright + frontend-design audit at the story, side-by-side light/dark, asserting a non-flat curvature read and that EVERY grid blob paints visibly against the page background (fix the var(--primary)/dark wash with a min-contrast rim or a foreground-aware base). This is the standing AX gate-philosophy fix (§13): the wave closes on the live audit, not the green proof.

findings.requirement: §3.3 Integration / §0 DRY — the var(--token) color-resolution seam must be one canonical mechanism, not duplicated.
findings.currentState: The same 'paint the css onto an element's color, getComputedStyle to un-wrap var()' cascade trick is implemented TWICE: GooBlob.vue:75-88 `resolveColorString` (for the base color) and useMetaballRenderer.ts:159-173 `resolveRimColor` (for rim + palette stops). Two caches (rimCache in the renderer, an ad-hoc ref in the SFC), two getComputedStyle paths, two different cap sizes (64 vs none). The base color is un-wrapped in the SFC then RE-fed to colorResolver in the renderer; the rim/palette are un-wrapped inside the renderer. The comments on both even cross-reference each other ('Mirror GooBlob.vue's cascade trick').
findings.rootCause: value.js's parseCSSColor cannot parse `var(--token)` and throws once per frame (the AW.W13 'var() throw fix', commit 374b98e), so a DOM-cascade un-wrap is genuinely needed — but it was bolted on twice instead of extracted to one seam. The renderer reaches back into the canvas element to do a getComputedStyle, coupling the pure-fn ColorResolver contract to a DOM read it was specifically designed to avoid (the AT.W0 inv-K-3 seam was meant to make the blob DOM-free at the color boundary). The duplication is a DRY violation AND an architectural leak: the renderer is supposed to receive ALREADY-resolved gamma triples.
findings.gestaltFix: Hoist ONE `resolveTokenColor(css, el): concreteCss` leaf (a tiny dom/ composable — un-wrap var() via a single cached cascade read) and have the SFC do ALL un-wrapping (base + rim + every palette stop) BEFORE it hands strings to the renderer, so the renderer's colorResolver only ever sees concrete strings and stays DOM-free as designed. The renderer's resolveRimColor + its rimCache delete entirely. One un-wrap path, one cache, the seam boundary restored.
findings.evidence: src/components/custom/goo-blob/GooBlob.vue:75-88 (resolveColorString) duplicated at src/components/custom/goo-blob/composables/useMetaballRenderer.ts:159-173 (resolveRimColor); both do el.style.color + getComputedStyle un-wrap

findings.requirement: §3.4 Performance / substrate correctness — the offscreen-park ownership must have exactly one writer per reason; the IntersectionObserver fallback must not race the content-visibility path.
findings.currentState: Correctly architected and the cleanest part of the slice. createCanvasLifecycle owns tab-hidden (visibilitychange), off-screen (contentvisibilityautostatechange), and manual as a Set<reason> where each reason is cleared only by its owner (createCanvasLifecycle.ts:83-150). The blob wires useIntersectionPause to drive ONLY suspend('off-screen') with pauseWhenHidden:false (useMetaballRenderer.ts:185-192) so the substrate's own tab-hidden writer stays the single writer for that reason — the comment explicitly reasons about 'exactly one writer per reason.' PRM is live-monitored in the core (onReducedMotionChange) and gates the RESCHEDULE not the suspend set, so an onscreen reduced surface paints one frame and parks without blanking. This is genuinely good and should be preserved.
findings.rootCause: N/A — this is the well-designed substrate. The one latent concern: BOTH the content-visibility path (substrate, fires contentvisibilityautostatechange) and the IntersectionObserver path (consumer, rootMargin 200px) can drive 'off-screen' suspend/resume for the same surface; they share the same reason key so a resume from EITHER lifts it. If content-visibility skips (offscreen) but the IO's 200px warm-band still considers it intersecting, the IO can resume('off-screen') and lift the substrate's legitimately-skipped suspend — a possible redundant wake. Low-likelihood (the 200px margin makes IO resume strictly earlier/wider than CV skip) but it is two writers of one reason key, which the substrate's own invariant warns against.
findings.gestaltFix: Keep the substrate as-is (it is the model). Tighten the off-screen ownership: give the IntersectionObserver fallback its OWN reason key ('off-screen-io') distinct from the content-visibility 'off-screen', so the loop runs only when BOTH agree the surface is visible (Set is empty) and neither path can lift the other's suspend. Engines WITH contentvisibilityautostatechange then get the CV path as primary and the IO as a redundant-but-harmless second gate; engines WITHOUT it fall through to IO alone. This makes the 'one writer per reason' invariant literally true for the off-screen case.
findings.evidence: src/composables/glass/webgl/createCanvasLifecycle.ts:83-150 (Set<reason> owner model, content-visibility writes 'off-screen' at :154-158); src/components/custom/goo-blob/composables/useMetaballRenderer.ts:185-192 (IO also writes 'off-screen', pauseWhenHidden:false)

result.notes: Headline for this slice: the blob's SUBSTRATE (createCanvasLifecycle park/PRM/context-loss) is genuinely well-architected and should be preserved as the model — the brokenness is at the INTEGRATION and DEFAULTS boundary, not the engine. Three blocker/major root causes: (1) the documented WCAG-2.2.2 pause/resume seam is a runtime no-op because GooBlob.vue discards the renderer handle and never re-exposes it (the README, JSDoc, and code all disagree) — the cleanest, highest-confidence fix in the slice; (2) the shipped DEFAULT is the pre-W9 flat sticker because every SOTA-droplet feature (lit/iridescence/SSS/palette/warp) defaults OFF for 'zero regression' — a legacy instinct forbidden by §0 in a greenfield product, and the literal cause of 'TOTALLY BROKEN'; (3) the demand-driven loop is defeated (shouldContinue==!paused => perpetual onscreen rAF) so an idle ambient blob burns full fps forever, and each instance holds its own scarce WebGL context (prior context-cap incident, commit 9427536). The W9 audit JSON browserVerify is literally 'PENDING' — the lit droplet was NEVER visually verified, the cardinal AX headless-green/visually-broken lesson in one field. Cross-slice coordination: the var()-un-wrap leaf (AX.W12) and the WatercolorDot static-instance routing (AX.W13) touch the /color leaf and the storybook-structure slice (§6/§7) respectively — coordinate ownership. I did NOT verify the live render in a real browser (audit-only, no dev server stood up); the flat-default + missing-first-blob findings are grounded in the F-tranche capture + the defaults source, and AX.W14 must close them on a live Playwright pass. Typecheck is green at HEAD (3.6.0) — which is precisely why none of these gates caught the integration breaks.

result.slice: graphics-specular-substrate

findings.requirement: §5.1 — The specular hover effect is FAR too extreme (the W23/W24 moving-specular). Tune to subtle.
findings.currentState: The pointer-anchored moving specular paints a pure-white masked radial-gradient catch-light on EVERY band glass surface via the unified `.glass-material::before`. Intensity floor at rest 0.35, hover 0.6, active 0.85 (the layer `opacity`); the gradient inner core is `hsl(40 30% 100% / 0.55)` = PURE WHITE at 0.55α, composited with `mix-blend-mode: screen`. Effective center brightness on hover ≈ 0.55×0.6 ≈ 0.33 white-screen; on active ≈ 0.55×0.85 ≈ 0.47 white-screen — a blown-out white hotspot that washes the surface toward white under the cursor. These exact values are UNCHANGED since AV.W15 (`8036370`); AW.W22 only widened where they apply.
findings.rootCause: TWO compounding architectural causes, not one. (1) MAGNITUDE: the recipe was authored at AV.W15 with values tuned over a busy aurora/goo-blob backdrop where a screen-blend white core reads as a tasteful lens; over glass-ui's own flat warm-cream substrate (and over most real consumer surfaces) the same `screen`-of-pure-white at 0.55α × up-to-0.85 opacity is a hot blowout. The inner stop `hsl(40 30% 100%)` resolves to pure white (L=100% saturates everything) — there is no warm-cream restraint in the actual light color despite the comment claiming 'warm-cream tint'. (2) BLAST RADIUS: AV.W15 scoped the `::before` to 3 opt-in components (Button glass, DockIconButton, Card). AW.W22 (`6bb442f`) PROMOTED it to a `::before` on all five ladder rungs + `.glass-card` + `.dock-icon-button` — so now every Dialog, Sheet, Popover, DropdownMenu, and every plain `.glass-resting`/`.glass-quiet` plate carries the rest-floor catch-light statically (no pointer wiring needed) and lifts to 0.85 on press. The extremity is now visible system-wide, not just on the 3 wired consumers.
findings.gestaltFix: A single gestalt retune at the ONE unified source (glass.css `.glass-material::before`), not per-component patches: (a) drop the inner gradient stop from pure-white-0.55α to a genuinely warm-cream low-alpha (e.g. `hsl(40 30% 96% / 0.22)` core, `/0.08` mid) so the actual light color carries the warm identity the comment claims; (b) halve the intensity ladder to a SUBTLE rung set (e.g. rest 0.0 or 0.12, hover 0.22, active 0.32) so the press-light is a whisper, not a flash; (c) tokenize the three intensity rungs as `--glass-specular-intensity-{rest,hover,active}` (a single overridable cohort in tokens.css §11b) so the magnitude is a token, not three buried literals across two files — a consumer or dark-arm retunes on the cascade; (d) consider demoting `mix-blend-mode: screen` to `screen` only on dark surfaces and a softer `plus-lighter`/`overlay` over light, OR keep screen but rely on the lowered alpha. The fix is 4 lines at one site. CRITICAL COUPLING: the proof gate `scripts/proof-glass-material-unified.mjs` lines 167/170 HARDCODE `--specular-intensity: 0.6` (hover) and `0.85` (active) in regex assertions — the wave MUST co-update the gate to assert the new token-driven rungs (or assert the tokens exist rather than literal values), else the tune lands RED.

findings.rootCause: Temporal layering: the dock-control hover-highlight (AT.W7-dock-b) predates AW.W22's promotion of the moving-specular onto `.dock-icon-button`. When W22 folded the control into the `.glass-material` group it never reconciled the now-redundant pre-existing `--glass-highlight` hover box-shadow — they coexist with no single owner. On the dock (the most-visible, most-hovered surface, floated over aurora on slides) the two stack into the worst-offending blowout, which is exactly where the user sees 'FAR too extreme'.
findings.gestaltFix: Pick ONE specular owner for the dock control. Since W22's intent was material uniformity, the moving `::before` should be the sole catch-light; retire the dock-controls.css `:hover` `--glass-highlight` box-shadow (or demote it to a non-specular surface-tint fill so hover still reads a bg shift without a second light). findings.requirement: §5.1 (rest-floor) — Every band glass surface paints a static centered catch-light at rest even with no pointer wiring
findings.currentState: The `.glass-material::before` sets `--specular-intensity: 0.35` as an explicit rest floor, so EVERY `.glass-card`, `.glass-resting`, `.glass-floating` etc. (22 component surfaces resolve a `glass-*` class in src/) paints a centered 0.35-opacity white screen-blend glow with no pointer interaction at all. The `@property --specular-intensity` initial-value is correctly 0, but the `::before` rule overrides it to 0.35 unconditionally — defeating the intended dormancy.

findings.requirement: §5 (substrate health) — createCanvasLifecycle / useWebGLCanvas post-carve health audit (the shared WebGL substrate)
findings.currentState: The AW.W7b carve (createCanvasLifecycle.ts, 248 lines) cleanly separates the backend-agnostic schedule (three-reason suspend Set, demand-gated rAF, document-visibility owner, content-visibility offscreen-park, live-PRM re-monitor) from the WebGL2 backend (useWebGLCanvas.ts) and the WebGPU sibling (createGPUCanvas.ts). The suspend reasons are a `Set<reason>` each cleared only by its owner; context-loss self-heals via rebuild; teardown loses the GL context under the per-page cap. Architecture is SOUND, proof-gated (proof:offscreen-pause, proof:webgl-substrate-single).
findings.rootCause: N/A — the substrate is healthy. Two MINOR seams worth a wave note, not blockers: (1) `resume()` and the `tick` reschedule back-date the clock via `startTime = performance.now() - 1000` (and `wasSuspended` resume sets `-1000`), a deliberate 'kick the demand-gate so shouldContinue sees motion' hack that introduces a 1-second animation time-discontinuity on every offscreen-return / tab-show — a subtle visible time-warp on aurora/blob when scrolling back into view. (2) `bindContentVisibility` resolves `canvas.parentElement` once at arm-time; if the consumer re-parents the canvas the offscreen-park host goes stale (no re-bind). Neither breaks a gate; both are cosmetic robustness.
findings.gestaltFix: (1) Replace the `-1000` clock back-date with an explicit `wake()`/demand re-prime that does not warp time — track a `pausedAt` and offset `startTime` by the paused duration on resume so the animation continues from where it parked (no 1s jump). (2) Optionally re-resolve the cv host on resize/re-parent. These are LOW-priority polish for an AX substrate-hygiene wave; the specular work does not depend on them. result.notes:
Headline root cause of '§5 specular FAR too extreme' is TWO compounding factors, not the one the requirement names. (1) MAGNITUDE: the inner gradient stop `hsl(40 30% 100%)` is PURE WHITE (L=100% saturates the 30% sat away), at 0.55α, `mix-blend-mode: screen`, scaled by an intensity ladder of 0.35/0.6/0.85 — at active that's ≈0.47 pure-white-screen, a blown-out hotspot. The 'warm-cream tint intact' claim in the comments is FALSE for the actual painted light. (2) BLAST RADIUS: the requirement blames W23/W24, but git archaeology shows the offending VALUES are unchanged since AV.W15 (8036370); the real regression is AW.W22 (6bb442f) PROMOTING the `::before` from 3 opt-in components onto EVERY band surface (all five ladder rungs + card + dock control), so the extremity is now system-wide and statically visible at rest. W24 only added the Card hover opt-in; it did not author the brightness.

LOAD-BEARING COUPLING the fix must not miss: `scripts/proof-glass-material-unified.mjs:167,170` hardcodes `--specular-intensity: 0.6` and `0.85` in regex — ANY tune lands RED unless the gate is co-updated in the same wave. This is the single most likely 'shipped regression' if a future agent tunes the CSS without touching the gate.

DOUBLE-SPECULAR on the dock control (the most-hovered, slides-visible surface) is the concrete worst-offender: the unified `::before` AND a separate `--glass-highlight` hover box-shadow stack. Fixing magnitude alone without retiring this leaves the dock hotter than the rest of the band.

The DRY pointer-seam duplication (Card ≡ DockIconButton verbatim) and the non-zero rest floor (0.35 defeating the @property initial-value 0) are secondary but belong in the SAME wave — they are the same architectural seam.

SUBSTRATE: createCanvasLifecycle/useWebGLCanvas post-carve is HEALTHY — clean backend/schedule separation, three-reason suspend Set, self-healing context-loss, proof-gated. Only two cosmetic seams (the -1000 resume time-warp and the arm-time cv-host resolution). No structural rework needed; routed to a low-priority hygiene wave, not a blocker on the specular work. Recommend the specular tune lead the graphics band (it is the §5 headline and a one-site fix); the substrate hygiene can ride any §11 encapsulation band.

Note: could not stand up a live dev server (none running; read-only audit) — all findings are grounded in static code + git archaeology + the AV.W15 spec JSON + the W22/W24 commit diffs. The W-specular-tune wave MUST close on a live Playwright + frontend-design audit per §0 VISUAL TRUTH; do not trust the headless gate.

findings.requirement: §7 foundations/native-top-layer — totally BROKEN. The native <dialog> top-layer pilot must paint a working glass scrim + entry/exit and open reliably.
findings.currentState: The .glass-top-layer dialog opens (via the JS showModal fallback only) and gets a backdrop BLUR, but the dim scrim NEVER paints — the dialog floats over an undimmed, only-blurred page. The preferred declarative open (commandfor/command="show-modal") is dead in nearly all browsers. Component is an orphan: GlassDialogNative is exported nowhere (not root barrel, not /api, not /subpaths, not package.json) and has exactly one consumer (this demo) — violating L invariant 8 (≥2 consumers or retire).
findings.rootCause: INVALID CSS in the backdrop rule. src/styles/animations.css:354,361,363 use `background-color: hsl(var(--background) / α)`. But `--background` is already a COMPLETE hsl() color (tokens.css:326 → --neutral-0 → `hsl(48 12% 98%)`), so this expands to `hsl(hsl(48 12% 98%) / 0.5)` — nested hsl(), which the parser drops. This is the exact CLAUDE.md anti-pattern (NEVER hsl(var(--token)); use color-mix for alpha). The 3 lines are the ONLY occurrences of this anti-pattern in the entire stylesheet corpus, and tokens.css:1287 even DOCUMENTS them as 'the legitimate single-token alpha case' — a false claim that froze the bug since birth. Secondary: the demo's PREFERRED trigger path is `commandfor`/`command` (invoker-commands, Baseline LIMITED) + `interestfor` (interest-invokers, LIMITED) — off in most engines, so the declarative half of the story is inert. Tertiary: the whole component duplicates reka-ui <Dialog>, which already ships a working dark-mode-adaptive glass scrim via _shared/ModalOverlay.vue (scrim="glass").
findings.gestaltFix: Retire GlassDialogNative + the standalone native-top-layer story; FOLD the native-<dialog> capability into reka-ui <Dialog> as a `:native` opt-in (already the manifest's stated FIX-ROUTE), OR if kept, FIRST fix the backdrop to the house alpha pattern: `background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--background) calc(var(--top-layer-backdrop-dim) * 100%), transparent)` and the @starting-style/exit to `... transparent`. Either way: delete the LIMITED commandfor/interestfor declarative path from the demo (or feature-detect it as a pure enhancement over a working JS-open default), and correct the false tokens.css:1287 comment. The .glass-top-layer @starting-style/overlay/allow-discrete entry grammar itself is sound and modern — keep it; only the scrim color form and the orphan-component packaging are broken.
