findings.requirement: §7 primitives/card — none of the toggles work (broken). The card story's shadow + grain switches must produce a visible change.
findings.currentState: The Switch v-model bindings and the Card :shadow/:grain prop bindings are mechanically CORRECT (reka-ui 2.9.7 SwitchRoot does use modelValue/update:modelValue; the props flip). But flipping either switch produces NO perceptible visual change — the toggles read as dead.
findings.rootCause: DOUBLE-SHADOW + SUB-THRESHOLD OPACITY, compounded by a known-broken staging substrate. (1) SHADOW toggle: every `.glass-{tier}` class already BAKES IN its own elevation shadow — `box-shadow: var(--glass-material-rim), var(--glass-shadow-{tier})` (glass.css ~lines 200-300). The Card then conditionally ADDS a SEPARATE `shadow-card` (= --shadow-md = `0 4px 16px @ 8% alpha`, tokens.css:494,516). Toggling `shadow` off only removes that faint 8%-alpha EXTRA layer; the tier's intrinsic shadow stays, so the card never visibly loses its shadow. (2) GRAIN toggle: the grain ::after runs at `--glass-grain-opacity: 0.025` (2.5%) with `mix-blend-mode: overlay` (tokens.css:668, glass.css:302-317) — imperceptible at rest, doubly so over busy color. (3) BOTH are staged over an Aurora backdrop (card.vue:20,121) that REQUIREMENTS §2.1 confirms renders DARK/broken live — so even the tier-alpha 0.30→0.95 steps the story is built to show don't read. The net effect is three near-invisible deltas presented as the headline interaction.

(a) Make `shadow` MEANINGFUL: either drop the redundant additive `shadow-card` and let the toggle gate the tier's OWN `--glass-shadow-{tier}` (so off = genuinely flat), or remove the shadow toggle as a non-feature. (b) Either raise grain to a perceptible level when ON or cut the grain toggle — a 2.5% delta is not a demoable control. (c) Decouple the card story from the broken Aurora: stage tiers over a STATIC, working high-frequency backdrop (an image/CSS gradient) until Aurora (§2 slice) is fixed — a primitive's story must not depend on a known-broken substrate to be legible. The deeper architectural truth: Card's surface is over-parameterized (tier + surface + shadow + grain + hover) where tier already determines elevation+grain; collapse the orthogonal-but-invisible knobs.

result.notes:
Cross-slice signal: TWO of my three items (card + glass-panel demos) stage their primitives over the Aurora backdrop, which REQUIREMENTS §2.1 confirms renders DARK/broken live (owned by the §2 Aurora slice). So part of their 'broken' appearance is TRANSITIVE — a working primitive made illegible by a broken substrate dependency. The gestalt fix for my slice is to DECOUPLE these stories from Aurora (static backdrop) so they're independently verifiable; but flag for the orchestrator that AX.W13/W14 visual closure may be gated behind the Aurora-fix wave if the demos keep an Aurora variant.

Honest correction to a likely assumption: the card 'toggles don't work' is NOT a reka-ui v-model binding-drift bug (the MEMORY binding-verification class). I verified reka-ui 2.9.7 SwitchRoot uses modelValue/update:modelValue and the v-model + :shadow/:grain bindings are correct. The toggles fire — they just control near-invisible layers (8%-alpha additive shadow over a tier that already has its own shadow; 2.5% grain). It's an architectural over-parameterization defect, not a wiring defect. Don't route it to a binding-sweep wave.

Shared anti-pattern worth a tranche-wide sweep: the invalid `hsl(var(--complete-color) / α)` form. It's isolated to 3 lines today (animations.css top-layer) but a passing dev comment (tokens.css:1287) actively legitimizes it — fix the comment so it doesn't propagate. The house pattern is color-mix(in srgb, var(--token) N%, transparent).

All three items also fail L invariant 8 in some form: GlassDialogNative (1 consumer, exported nowhere) and GlassPanel (0 production consumers) are substrate-without-consumer and should be retired, not merely fixed. That makes 'fix-or-redesign' lean toward RETIRE/FOLD for native-top-layer and GlassPanel, and a genuine redesign only for Card's toggle semantics.

Not in my slice but adjacent and worth flagging: §7 also asks whether hover-popover/configurator/glyph-face/disco-glyph/metric-badge-vs-pill/use-token-color belong as 'primitives' — several share the same substrate-without-consumer / mis-categorization smell I found here; recommend a single storybook-recategorization wave coordinate with the §6 storybook-restructure slice.

The library DEFAULT register is Fraunces: tokens.css:43-44 set --font-stack-display: "Fraunces", Georgia, serif and --font-stack-serif: "Fraunces", Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif; theme.css:107-109 bridge those to --font-display/--font-serif; typography.css:142-147 sets body { font-family: var(--font-serif) }. So by library default, ALL body+heading+prose+display text is Fraunces (a serif). BUT the canonical consumers explicitly reject Fraunces: speedtest MapSkeleton.vue:26 comment reads 'never Computer Modern, never Fraunces, never General Sans' and its document register is "Plus Jakarta Sans" (MapSkeleton.vue:184, MapEmptyHint.vue:184). The DEMO (the dogfood) forces Plus Jakarta onto serif+display via index.html:9 data-typography-preset="brand-uniform-sans" + demo.css:98-102 --font-brand-sans override, so the live demo renders Plus Jakarta (a geometric SANS) everywhere — Fraunces NEVER paints in the demo (demo.css declares @font-face only for Plus Jakarta + Fira Code; grep -c 'font-family: "Fraunces"' demo/demo.css = 0). So if a user picks 'Fraunces' in the configurator (defaults.ts:22-26), it falls through to Georgia, never the shipped face. Both gates (proof:font-canon, proof:font-axes) are GREEN — the textbook AW headless-green/visually-broken gap.
findings.rootCause: Three incompatible design intents were stacked over the AC→AU arc and never reconciled into one register model. (1) f6e68ff decoupled --font-sans from --font-serif so a consumer could brand the serif voice. (2) AC.W6b (commit 2474440) self-hosted Plus Jakarta Sans + Fira Code as the BRAND register — Plus Jakarta is what speedtest+demo actually render, and it carries Capsize-calibrated 'Plus Jakarta Sans Fallback' faces (typography.css:34-63) proving it was meant to be the default. (3) AU.W4 (commit 048ea88, subject literally tagged '[slipped]') shipped Fraunces purely to 'resolve a dangling display token' — it repointed --font-stack-serif AND --font-stack-display at Fraunces to make the WONK/SOFT axes non-inert, but never wired Fraunces into the register consumers use, never gave it a calibrated fallback face, and never declared it in demo.css. Net: the library DEFAULT identity (Fraunces serif body) is a face nobody renders; the consumer identity (Plus Jakarta) is bolted on through a doubly-indirect preset (data-typography-preset → --font-brand-sans → --font-serif) that is so circuitous the demo.css comment at line 92 even mis-describes it. The 'brand-uniform-sans' preset is itself a smell: a NAMED preset that just collapses serif=display=brand-sans exists ONLY because the default register is wrong and consumers must opt OUT of it. typography.css header (line 2) compounds the rot — it claims 'Fraunces serif/display' as the design, contradicting the demo and speedtest. The two proof gates are structurally blind: proof:font-canon only checks that referenced families are SHIPPED or system-named (Georgia passes as system-named, so Fraunces→Georgia fallthrough is invisible); proof:font-axes only checks the woff2 fvar carries WONK/SOFT — neither gate asserts which face actually PAINTS in the live cascade.
findings.gestaltFix: Pick ONE coherent register model and make the library DEFAULT be the register the consumers render — no preset opt-out, no inert face. The evidence says the brand register is Plus Jakarta Sans (text/display) + Fira Code (mono). Gestalt: (1) Repoint the library tokens — tokens.css --font-stack-sans + a renamed --font-stack-text → "Plus Jakarta Sans", "Plus Jakarta Sans Fallback", system-ui, sans-serif as the DEFAULT body/display family; demote the serif/Fraunces register to an OPT-IN editorial display token (--font-stack-display-serif) only if a consumer wants the ornamental WONK/SOFT Fraunces voice — otherwise EXCISE Fraunces entirely (it ships 67KB for zero renderers; per §0 'excise or fail explicitly' + the overfitting-audit ≥2-consumer rule, a face no consumer paints is dead weight). (2) Delete the brand-uniform-sans preset and the data-typography-preset indirection — when the default IS the brand register, the preset has nothing to do. The demo then needs no --font-brand-sans override and no index.html preset attr; it just imports the styles and renders the real default. (3) Fix body{} to read the text register directly, rename --font-serif→--font-text (or keep a serif token ONLY if Fraunces is kept as opt-in). (4) Give whatever default face is chosen a calibrated fallback (Plus Jakarta already has one; Fraunces has NONE — if kept, it needs one, otherwise its font-display:swap FOUTs to Georgia with CLS). (5) Rewrite the typography.css header + fonts/README.md to state the real register. (6) Harden the gates: add a live-cascade assertion (Playwright getComputedStyle on body/headings/.text-display asserts the resolved family is the shipped face, not a system fallthrough) — this is the AX standing 'visual-truth' gate that catches exactly this class. (7) If Fraunces is kept as opt-in, declare its @font-face in demo.css so the configurator 'Fraunces' option actually paints.

findings.requirement: §0 — no inert/dead tokens; every shipped asset has ≥2 consumers or is excised (overfitting-audit). The font subsystem must not ship payload nothing renders.
findings.currentState: Fraunces ships 67KB woff2 + is base64-inlined into dist/styles/fonts.css (~99KB gzip font payload total per fonts.css:8). It is referenced ONLY by the library-default --font-stack-serif/display tokens, which the demo AND speedtest both override away. Net renderers of Fraunces across the demo + the one real consumer: ZERO. Plus Jakarta Sans renders in both. The 'fourier-f' utility (typography.css:421-430) and the WONK/SOFT variation-settings machinery (typography.css:98) exist solely to drive Fraunces axes that never paint in any live surface.
findings.rootCause: AU.W4 shipped a face to satisfy a self-imposed token (the 'dangling display token' it had itself wired), not a consumer need — classic substrate-without-consumer. The proof:font-axes gate institutionalized it: by asserting the woff2 carries WONK/SOFT it made the face 'load-bearing' to the gate while no pixel depends on it. The cost is real: it more than DOUBLES the font critical payload (Fraunces latin = 67KB vs Plus Jakarta latin = 27KB) on a path the corpus already flags as 'over half the entire ./styles critical CSS weight' (fonts.css:8-9).
findings.gestaltFix: Resolve the §7 register decision first (AX.W-FONT-1). If the chosen brand register is Plus Jakarta + Fira Code (the consumer evidence), EXCISE Fraunces entirely: delete src/fonts/fraunces/, the Fraunces @font-face (fonts.css:158-168), the WONK/SOFT --font-display-variation-settings + --font-display-weight machinery (typography.css:98-99 + every font-variation-settings reference in the display utilities), the fourier-f utility, and retire proof:font-axes (the gate guarding a dead face). This drops the critical font payload by ~40KB+ and removes a whole axis of confusion. ALTERNATIVELY, if the ornamental Fraunces display voice is genuinely wanted (a deliberate editorial register for hero display only — NOT body), keep it but (a) scope it to a single --font-stack-display-serif token consumed by ONLY the display-* hero utilities, (b) give it a calibrated fallback face, (c) declare it in demo.css and wire ONE demo surface to render it so it has a live consumer + visual proof. Do not keep it half-wired as today.
findings.evidence: src/fonts/fraunces/fraunces-latin.woff2 (67388 bytes); fonts.css:8-9,158-168; typography.css:98-99,421-430; scripts/proof-font-axes.mjs; zero live renderers (demo forces Plus Jakarta, speedtest forbids Fraunces); contrast: Plus Jakarta latin 27348 bytes.

findings.requirement: §0/§7 — gates must encode VISUAL TRUTH; a green gate must mean the rendered result is correct, not merely that a token names a shipped face.
findings.currentState: proof:font-canon (scripts/proof-font-canon.mjs) and proof:font-axes are both GREEN, yet the rendered font system is wrong (Fraunces never paints; default register disagrees with consumer register; configurator 'Fraunces' option falls to Georgia). proof:font-canon's GENERIC+SYSTEM_NAMED allowlist (lines 32-65) explicitly admits 'georgia', 'times new roman', etc. as paintable — so a stack like "Fraunces", Georgia, serif PASSES even though, in the demo, Fraunces is undeclared and Georgia is what actually renders. The gate verifies name-legality, not paint-reality.
findings.rootCause: Both font gates are static-text linters over CSS source strings; neither opens a browser. They were designed (AV.W10/AU.W4) to catch the narrow 'references a face the browser can never paint' class — and they do — but they are constitutionally incapable of catching 'a shipped face that the live cascade overrides away' or 'a configurator option that falls through to a system fallback.' This IS the cardinal AW lesson (REQUIREMENTS.md §0/§13 'headless-green/visually-broken GAP') manifest in the font slice.
findings.gestaltFix: Add the standing AX visual-truth font gate: a Playwright probe that (1) loads the live demo, (2) document.fonts.ready, (3) getComputedStyle on body, each .text-display-* sample, .text-admin-label/.fira-code, and (4) asserts the resolved fontFamily's FIRST successfully-loaded face matches the intended register (e.g. via document.fonts.check + a canvas width-fingerprint to distinguish the real face from a metric-matched fallback). It must fail RED if body renders Georgia/system-serif instead of the brand face. Keep proof:font-canon as the cheap static pre-check but demote it from 'sufficient' to 'necessary-only.' Retire proof:font-axes if Fraunces is excised.
findings.evidence: scripts/proof-font-canon.mjs:32-65,125-140 (name-legality only, Georgia allowlisted); scripts/proof-font-axes.mjs (fvar-only); both PASS at HEAD while the live demo renders Plus Jakarta (not the default Fraunces) and the configurator Fraunces option renders Georgia; REQUIREMENTS.md §0 'VISUAL TRUTH' + §13 headless-green gap.

findings.requirement: §0 DRY/KISS — no circuitous indirection, no named presets that exist only to undo a wrong default; documentation must match the code.
findings.currentState: The consumer reaches the brand register through a triple-indirection: data-typography-preset="brand-uniform-sans" (index.html:9) → :root[data-typography-preset="brand-uniform-sans"]{--font-serif: var(--font-brand-sans)} (typography.css:132-137) → --font-brand-sans override (demo.css:98-102). The brand-uniform-sans preset also force-changes --font-display-variation-settings:normal and --font-display-weight:600 (typography.css:135-136) to neutralize the Fraunces WONK/SOFT axes — pure cleanup of a register that shouldn't be the default. The typography.css header (line 2) AND fonts/README.md still describe 'Fraunces serif/display' as THE design, directly contradicting the demo + speedtest. demo.css:92 even mis-states the mechanism ('the preset cascades --font-display/--font-serif from the library').
findings.rootCause: Each layer was a patch over the prior layer's wrongness rather than a fix: AU.W4 made Fraunces the default → AC-era consumers needed Plus Jakarta → instead of fixing the default, a 'brand-uniform-sans' escape-hatch preset was minted → the preset needs three sub-overrides to fully neutralize Fraunces (family + variation-settings + weight). The accumulated indirection is the symptom of never having picked one register. The stale header/README are the documentation half of the same un-reconciled accretion.
findings.gestaltFix: Once the default register is corrected (AX.W-FONT-1), this entire indirection collapses: delete the brand-uniform-sans preset block (typography.css:132-137), the data-typography-preset attr (index.html:9), the --font-brand-sans override (demo.css:98-102) — the demo just imports the styles and gets the right register for free. Rewrite the typography.css header (line 1-20) + src/fonts/README.md to state the actual brand register (Plus Jakarta text/display + Fira Code mono [+ optional opt-in Fraunces display-serif if kept]). One register, zero opt-out preset, documentation == code.
findings.evidence: index.html:9; typography.css:132-137 (preset with 3 sub-overrides), typography.css:1-20 (stale 'Fraunces serif/display' header); demo.css:91-102; src/fonts/README.md:24-44 (Fraunces-as-design framing); demo.css:92 (mis-stated mechanism).

proposedWaves.title: Font register reconciliation — one brand register, default == rendered, excise the dead face
proposedWaves.scope: Pick ONE coherent register model grounded in the actual consumers (speedtest = Plus Jakarta Sans text/display + Fira Code mono; 'never Fraunces'). Make the LIBRARY DEFAULT be that register so no consumer opts out. (a) Repoint tokens.css --font-stack-* so the default body/display family is the brand face (Plus Jakarta Sans + its calibrated Plus Jakarta Sans Fallback), not Fraunces; (b) DECISION on Fraunces — excise entirely (delete src/fonts/fraunces/, fonts.css:158-168, the WONK/SOFT --font-display-variation-settings + --font-display-weight machinery, fourier-f utility, proof:font-axes) OR demote to a single opt-in --font-stack-display-serif editorial token with its own calibrated fallback + a live demo surface + a demo.css @font-face; default is excise unless an editorial display register is explicitly wanted; (c) delete the brand-uniform-sans preset + data-typography-preset indirection (typography.css:132-137, index.html:9, demo.css:98-102) — the demo renders the correct default with no override; (d) rename/clean the --font-serif→--font-text semantic if serif is dropped; fix body{} to read the canonical register; (e) rewrite typography.css header + src/fonts/README.md to match. KISS the cascade to: text register + mono register (+ optional opt-in display-serif). Cuts ~40KB+ critical font payload if Fraunces excised. Visual-truth close: live Playwright audit confirms body/headings/display + admin-label/mono all render the intended shipped faces.

proposedWaves.title: Font visual-truth gate — live-cascade paint assertion replacing static-only font gates
proposedWaves.scope: Add the standing AX visual-truth font gate: a Playwright/headed probe that loads the live demo, awaits document.fonts.ready, and asserts via getComputedStyle + document.fonts.check + a canvas glyph-width fingerprint that body, each .text-display-* register, and .fira-code/.text-admin-label render the INTENDED shipped face (not a system fallthrough like Georgia or a metric-matched fallback). Fails RED on the exact class HEAD ships green-but-broken. Demote proof:font-canon to necessary-only static pre-check; retire proof:font-axes if Fraunces is excised in AX.W-FONT-1. This is the font instance of the REQUIREMENTS.md §13 standing visual-truth gate-philosophy wave.

result.notes:
SLICE = fonts. Headline root cause: the font system is three incompatible design intents stacked over the AC→AU arc and never reconciled. (1) AC.W6b self-hosted Plus Jakarta Sans + Fira Code as the BRAND register (Plus Jakarta even has a Capsize-calibrated fallback face — proof it was meant to be the default, and it IS what speedtest+demo render). (2) AU.W4 (commit subject literally tagged '[slipped]') shipped Fraunces and repointed --font-stack-serif/display at it just to make a self-imposed 'dangling display token' non-inert — without wiring it into the consumer register, without a calibrated fallback, without declaring it in demo.css. NET: the library DEFAULT identity (Fraunces serif body, tokens.css:43-44 + typography.css:142-147) is a face NOBODY renders; the consumer identity (Plus Jakarta) is bolted on via a triple-indirection opt-out preset (data-typography-preset→--font-brand-sans→--font-serif). Fraunces ships 67KB of critical font payload for ZERO live renderers. Both proof gates (proof:font-canon, proof:font-axes) are GREEN — the textbook AW headless-green/visually-broken gap, because they lint CSS source strings (name-legality, fvar axes) and never open a browser; Georgia is in proof:font-canon's SYSTEM_NAMED allowlist (lines 53-65) so the "Fraunces", Georgia fallthrough is gate-invisible.

FACTS VERIFIED LIVE: grep -c 'font-family: "Fraunces"' demo/demo.css = 0 (Fraunces never declared in the demo → configurator 'Fraunces' option falls to Georgia). index.html:9 sets data-typography-preset="brand-uniform-sans" which + demo.css:98-102 forces Plus Jakarta onto serif+display → live demo renders a geometric SANS everywhere, never the default serif. speedtest MapSkeleton.vue:26 comment: 'never Computer Modern, never Fraunces, never General Sans'; its register is "Plus Jakarta Sans" (MapSkeleton.vue:184). Both gates run PASS at HEAD (confirmed by executing them).

RECOMMENDED DECISION for the FONT-1 wave: excise Fraunces (no live consumer, doubles the critical font payload, per §0 excise-or-fail + the ≥2-consumer overfitting rule), make Plus Jakarta Sans the default text/display register and Fira Code the mono register, delete the brand-uniform-sans escape-hatch preset entirely. Keep Fraunces ONLY if a deliberate editorial display-serif voice is wanted — and then scope it to one opt-in token + a live demo surface + a calibrated fallback. Either way the cardinal fix is: the library DEFAULT must equal the register the demo+consumers actually render, with zero opt-out indirection, and a live-cascade gate (FONT-2) to keep it true. Two waves proposed; FONT-2 depends on FONT-1.

At /navigation/carousel the CarouselDots row (the 'progress bar' the user means) reads as a malformed, lopsided progress bar: a single bright pill stuck at the left with the rest of the track invisible. (2) DEAD CLASS — the active dot's scale emphasis (scale-[var(--scale-hover)]) emits NO CSS rule at all (computed transform:none; no matching stylesheet rule found) — the Tailwind-v4 arbitrary-value-with-css-var content-scan non-emit class (same family as the §13 W24 card-lift @utility non-emit). The active dot relies solely on w-6 width, which on its own reads as a 'progress fill', not a position pip. (3) AFFORDANCE DRIFT — the dots predate the glass-atoms band (no .tap-squish press-spring, no transition-control, off the four-state contract), the very restyle AW.W30 was meant to apply but NEVER RAN; and AW.W30 §3.5 explicitly scoped Progress OUT ('the pager has no progress affordance'), so this defect was deliberately left unaddressed by the deferred carousel wave.

KISS: it is one SFC (CarouselDots.vue) + a token choice; no new primitive, no Progress fork.

findings.requirement: §10.1 — A slides bottom progress bar that is a PAGE-BOTTOM element, NOT baked into the dock (as it was before, as on mobile). The /deck family.
findings.currentState: PARTIALLY SHIPPED but the headline contract is UN-ADOPTED. glass-ui ships a `DeckProgress.vue` thin :value wrapper (src/components/custom/deck-progress/DeckProgress.vue) + a `.glass-progress-rail` CSS recipe (src/styles/glass.css:577-592) on the root barrel — this is the AW.W16 library half. But the slides consumer (the actual page-bottom bar) NEVER adopted it: slides/src/deck/DeckView.vue:105 still renders a hand-rolled `<div class="deck-progress" :style="{'--p': nav.progress.value}">` with its own `.deck-progress` + `::after` rule (DeckView.vue:238-263) and its own `--deck-progress-*` token set (slides/src/styles/deck.css:285-297). The de-dock itself IS correct in slides (the bar is `position:fixed; bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom); z-index:40`, below the dock — the in-dock underline was removed). So the page-bottom placement requirement is MET in slides today, but via a parallel hand-rolled rail, not the library `DeckProgress`. The wave's own two-consumer ledger names slides H.W1 as 'consumer #2 — PORT, adopts the library rail LOOK, deletes its hand-rolled rail CSS'; that port never happened (grep for DeckProgress/glass-progress-rail in slides/src returns ZERO).
findings.rootCause: The ≥2-consumer rule (CLAUDE.md design axis 3, L invariant 8) that JUSTIFIES the `DeckProgress` + `.glass-progress-rail` primitive is UNSATISFIED at HEAD. AW.W16 shipped the library surface (consumer #1 = the demo story) on the PROMISE that slides H.W1 would be consumer #2. But H.W1 never ran (REQUIREMENTS.md §171: 'slides H W2-W11 the real visual-refinement waves — never run, blocked behind the user's WIP'). The deeper architectural why: AW.W16 and slides H.W2 evolved IN PARALLEL with no shared rail — slides hand-rolled `.deck-progress` (a `<div>` + `::after` width-driven fill, `transition: width`) while glass-ui authored `.glass-progress-rail` (a `<Progress>` ProgressIndicator restyle, `translateX`-driven). They are two DIFFERENT fill mechanics for the same visual, so the primitive currently has exactly ONE consumer (the demo) — it is substrate-without-a-real-consumer, the precise anti-pattern the binary invariant forbids.
findings.gestaltFix: Decide the rail's home in ONE direction and converge, do not keep two parallel rails. Two coherent options — (A) PORT slides to the library: replace the slides `<div class="deck-progress">` + its `.deck-progress`/`::after` CSS + the `--deck-progress-*` tokens with `<DeckProgress :value="nav.progress.value" class="deck-progress">` and a slim consumer `.deck-progress` rule carrying ONLY the pinned chrome (position/bottom/z-index), retinting via `--progress-rail-fill: var(--ncsu-red)` etc. This makes slides consumer #2 and clears the invariant — BUT it requires the library recipe to actually be correct (see the next two findings, which currently block a clean port). (B) If the library rail cannot match the slides look without forking the fill mechanic, RETIRE `DeckProgress` + `.glass-progress-rail` from glass-ui (delete the wrapper, the recipe, the demo story, the gate) and let the rail stay slides-local — a hand-rolled `<div>` + `::after` is a 6-line consumer recipe with no library-worthy abstraction (the math is a one-liner, the chrome is consumer-owned, the look is one box-shadow). The honest read: a single `<Progress>`-restyle for a 5px bar may not earn its keep as a shipped primitive. AX must pick A or B; the current limbo (shipped-but-unadopted) is the worst of both.

findings.requirement: §10.1 (library-look correctness) — the `.glass-progress-rail` recipe must actually paint the rail LOOK (thin track, token fill, leading-edge glow) so a consumer can adopt it.
findings.currentState: The recipe is in `@layer components` (src/styles/glass.css:31 `@layer components` encloses line 577). Its `background: var(--progress-rail-track,...)` on the track and `background: var(--progress-rail-fill,...)` on the indicator are OVERRIDDEN by Tailwind's `bg-secondary`/`bg-primary` utilities that `ProgressDefault.vue:26,32` bakes inline — those utilities live in `@layer utilities`, which outranks `@layer components` regardless of source order. So `:root { --progress-rail-fill: ... }` does NOT retint the fill (it loses to `bg-primary`), and `--progress-rail-track` does NOT retint the track (loses to `bg-secondary`). The token-first contract the recipe and the proof gate ADVERTISE ('a consumer overrides :root { --progress-rail-fill } to retint with zero library edit') is FALSE for the two color axes. Only `height`, `border-radius:0`, and the `box-shadow` glow win (no competing utility).
findings.rootCause: A cascade-layer inversion. The recipe assumed plain class-vs-class specificity (`.glass-progress-rail` vs `.bg-primary`, equal, source-order decides) but Tailwind v4 puts utilities in a NAMED layer that always outranks `@layer components`. The recipe restyles the WRONG surface: it tries to override a color the inner `ProgressDefault` hardcodes as a utility, which by construction cannot lose to a component-layer rule. The proof gate (scripts/proof-deck-progress-rail.mjs) only string-asserts the recipe READS `--progress-rail-*` tokens — it never renders to confirm they WIN — so the gate is green while the contract is broken (the exact headless-green/visually-broken gap REQUIREMENTS.md §171 calls the cardinal AX lesson).
findings.gestaltFix: Make the recipe win the cascade idiomatically. Either (a) author `.glass-progress-rail` in `@layer utilities` (or as a Tailwind `@utility`) so it ranks alongside `bg-primary`/`bg-secondary` and source order can win — combined with making the rail recipe a SIBLING utility the consumer applies, not a component-layer afterthought; or (b) the cleaner fix per the token-first axis: `ProgressDefault.vue` should read its fill/track from `--progress-fill`/`--progress-track` tokens (the gradient variant already does per Progress.vue:34) instead of hardcoding `bg-primary`/`bg-secondary`, so the `default` variant is token-retintable at the source and `.glass-progress-rail` only needs to set those tokens + the geometry. Option (b) also fixes the latent issue that the `default` Progress variant is the ONLY one not token-retintable. Whichever, the proof gate must be upgraded from a string-scan to a real computed-style assertion (render `<DeckProgress>` with a `:root` override and assert the painted fill is the override color) so this class of break cannot ship green again.
findings.evidence: src/styles/glass.css:31 (`@layer components`),577-592; src/components/ui/progress/ProgressDefault.vue:26 (`bg-secondary`),32 (`bg-primary`); src/components/ui/progress/Progress.vue:34 (gradient reads --progress-track/--progress-fill — default does not); scripts/proof-deck-progress-rail.mjs (string-scan only, no render)

findings.requirement: §10.1 (the leading-edge glow — the rail's signature look) must render.
findings.currentState: The glow is a `box-shadow: 4px 0 8px ...` on `.glass-progress-rail > *` (the ProgressIndicator). But the indicator is `w-full` translated by `translateX(-X%)` inside a root that is `overflow-hidden` (ProgressDefault.vue:26,32-33). The recipe never lifts that `overflow-hidden`. The indicator's right edge sits exactly at the fill boundary and the `4px 0 8px` box-shadow extends RIGHTWARD into the hidden overflow region — so the glow is CLIPPED away by the root's `overflow:hidden`. The advertised 'leading-edge glow on the fill's trailing edge' is largely or entirely invisible. (Contrast: the slides hand-rolled `.deck-progress::after` at DeckView.vue:253-261 ALSO sits in an `overflow:hidden` root, so its `box-shadow` glow is clipped too — but slides tuned the glow to a TIGHT 2px inset-ish spread that mostly reads as an edge brightening rather than a halo, which is why it survives. The library's 8px-blur rightward glow does not.)
findings.rootCause: A clip/overflow mismatch between the rail recipe and the `<Progress>` substrate it composes. `ProgressDefault` MUST clip (`overflow-hidden`) so the `w-full translateX` indicator does not spill — that clip is load-bearing for the default progress look. But a leading-edge GLOW is fundamentally an OUTSIDE-the-fill effect, which the clip kills. The recipe tried to add an outside effect to an inside-clipped substrate — architecturally incompatible. This is the AW.W16 'compose <Progress>, do not fork' constraint colliding with reality: the glow the wave wanted cannot be achieved by restyling the clipped `<Progress>` indicator.
findings.gestaltFix: Render the glow as the indicator's TRAILING (left/inset) edge inside the clip, not a rightward box-shadow — e.g. an `inset` box-shadow or a `linear-gradient` mask on the indicator's right portion that reads as a brightening leading edge WITHOUT extending past the fill boundary, so the clip can't eat it. This is exactly what the slides bar does (a tight glow that lives at the edge). Alternatively, if a true OUTSIDE halo is the design intent, the rail cannot compose the clipped `<Progress>` default and the AW.W16 escalation trigger fires ('the recipe needs a forked track to achieve the glow' — wave file line 30) — route to a deliberate decision: tune the glow to an in-clip edge effect (preferred, no fork) OR accept the rail is a thin token-tinted bar with no halo. Verify the chosen look with a live Playwright screenshot, not the string-scan gate.
findings.evidence: src/styles/glass.css:589-591 (`box-shadow: 4px 0 8px`); src/components/ui/progress/ProgressDefault.vue:26 (`overflow-hidden`),32-33 (`w-full` + `translateX`); slides/src/deck/DeckView.vue:256-260 (the tuned-tight slides glow that does survive its own clip)

result.notes:
SLICE VERDICT: The §10 'slides primitive / deck' requirement is NARROWER than its phrasing implies. There is no real '/deck family' to build — the slides deck engine (useDeck/useDeckNav/DeckPager/deckSpring/reveal/pagerWindow) is correctly slides-local single-consumer logic and MUST stay there (lifting it would manufacture substrate-without-consumer, violating the binary invariant). The ONLY library surface in scope is the bottom-bar rail LOOK.

The HEADLINE finding: AW.W16 shipped the rail's library half (DeckProgress + .glass-progress-rail) on the promise that slides H.W1 would be its 2nd consumer — that port NEVER happened (zero DeckProgress/glass-progress-rail references in slides/src). Slides hand-rolled a parallel .deck-progress <div>+::after bar with a DIFFERENT fill mechanic (transition:width vs the library's translateX). So the library primitive has exactly ONE consumer (the demo story) — substrate-without-a-real-consumer, the precise anti-pattern CLAUDE.md design-axis-3 forbids. AX must converge: adopt slides onto the library rail (consumer #2) OR retire the library rail and keep it slides-local. The current shipped-but-unadopted limbo is the worst outcome.

The de-dock placement itself (the actual §10.1 ask — bar at page-bottom, not in the dock, as on mobile) IS correctly done in slides today (DeckView.vue:105, position:fixed bottom z-index:40 below the dock; the in-dock underline was removed). So the user-visible requirement is MET — but via a hand-rolled bar that bypasses the library primitive the tranche built for it.

Two TRAP findings that block a clean port and that the green gate HIDES: (1) cascade-layer inversion — the recipe's token colors lose to Tailwind's bg-primary/bg-secondary in @layer utilities, so the advertised :root --progress-rail-fill retint is silently a no-op; (2) the leading-edge glow is clipped away by ProgressDefault's overflow:hidden. The proof:deck-progress-rail gate is a string-scan (and isn't even registered in package.json), so both ship green — the cardinal AX headless-green/visually-broken gap. Whatever AX decides (adopt or retire), the gate must become a render assertion and the close must be a live Playwright audit.

This slice is SMALL and surgical — one convergence wave (AX.W31) + a shared close-pass gate-registration wave (AX.W33). It has a real cross-cutting dependency on the §1 dock convergence (the bar's page-bottom z-index/clearance must agree with the de-docked dock's final geometry).

findings.requirement: §4.1 — Constellation abstracted into a glass-ui component; verify the abstraction is complete + consumer-ready for slides.
findings.currentState: TWO parallel constellation implementations exist. glass-ui ships a clean, neutral `<Constellation>` (src/components/custom/constellation/Constellation.vue + constellationField.ts) that composes the useCanvas2D substrate and exposes a `drawOverlay(ctx, field, now)` skin seam — landed AW.W17 (da0495b). But slides STILL runs its own 510-line src/decks/til-briefing/constellation.ts (`createConstellations` data-canvas scanner + a hand-rolled shared RAF). slides imports glass-ui/constellation NOWHERE (grep: NOT IMPORTED). The glass-ui demo story (demo/stories/substrates/constellation.vue) is the only consumer of the new component — so it satisfies the ≥2-consumer invariant ON PAPER, but the real intended consumer (slides) never ported. The abstraction is consumer-READY in form but not consumer-ADOPTED, and the deck-domain skin (anomaly node, resolved-check, callout label) was never built against drawOverlay.
findings.rootCause: The AW.W17 extraction was a fresh greenfield component modeled on the slides version, NOT a port of slides onto it — the two were never reconciled in the same wave. The earlier F-tranche audit (slides docs/tranches/F/audit/L05-handrolled-to-gu.md, finding F05) explicitly said KEEP-LOCAL because NCSU-red anomaly identity was 'structurally embedded'. AW.W17 then RESOLVED that exact objection by inventing the neutral lattice + `drawOverlay` skin seam (anomaly = consumer skin, not field mechanics) — but no follow-up wave re-pointed slides, so the F05 KEEP-LOCAL verdict was never revisited and the duplication ossified.
findings.gestaltFix: Build the slides anomaly skin as a `drawOverlay` pass (pulse ring + core + resolved-check + dashed callout label, reading `--constellation-accent`) and a thin Vue wrapper over `<Constellation>`, then DELETE slides' constellation.ts entirely. The drift (anomaly re-targeting) is the one mechanic drawOverlay cannot express — it mutates node position, and the overlay receives the field AFTER stepField. Resolve by adding an optional `stepOverlay(field, k, now)` hook to the component (runs inside stepField, before draw) OR by letting the consumer mutate `field.nodes[focalIndex]` from drawOverlay (positions are read each draw, so an overlay write the frame before paint is visible). The cleaner gestalt is a `focalIndex?: number` prop + a `pinFocal` flag so the component pins node[0] (vx=vy=0) and the consumer drifts it — but that re-introduces deck domain. Keep it as the `stepOverlay` seam: a generic 'mutate the field before paint' callback parallel to drawOverlay.

findings.requirement: §4.2 — Constellation visibility (not visible enough in dark mode, nor quite enough in light mode) must be a library-level concern, not re-tuned per consumer.
findings.currentState: glass-ui's constellation ships ZERO `--constellation-*` default tokens in its own stylesheet (grep on src/styles/ = no hits). Its DEFAULT_PALETTE is three hardcoded hex constants in constellationField.ts and it reads only three tokens (`--constellation-node`, `-node-dim`, `-line`). slides, meanwhile, reads SEVEN tokens (`-node`, `-node-dim`, `-accent`, `-alpha`, `-edge-alpha`, `-edge-anomaly-alpha`, plus `--foreground` for the line) and defines a full light + dark arm in deck.css §1/§10 — multiple waves of visibility tuning (H.W4: node colours lifted off the ink ground on dark, edge-alpha multipliers promoted to tokens, anomaly core 4.2→5.6) live ENTIRELY in slides. The library captured none of that hard-won dark/light contrast knowledge.
findings.rootCause: The AW.W17 extraction lifted the MECHANICS (four neutral passes + the substrate) but not the PALETTE INTELLIGENCE — the dark-mode-lift, the field-yields-to-type alpha, the per-mode edge multipliers. Those were treated as 'consumer skin' and left in slides, but they are NOT deck-identity (NCSU-red is; a node colour that reads on a dark ground is universal). The presets-in-consumer line was applied too aggressively: the lattice's legibility floor is library identity, only the accent hue is consumer preset.
findings.gestaltFix: Ship a `--constellation-*` token block in glass-ui tokens.css with a light arm and a `.dark` arm carrying the H.W4-derived legibility values (node lifted off ground on dark, the `--constellation-alpha` field-yields-to-type knob, the `--constellation-edge-alpha`/`-edge-anomaly-alpha` multipliers). Wire constellationField.ts's readPalette to read the full set with these as fallbacks. The `--constellation-accent` hue STAYS a consumer override (slides aliases it to `--ncsu-red`) — that is the legitimate preset boundary. Net: a consumer drops in a constellation and it is legible on both grounds with zero tuning; only the brand accent is theirs.

result.notes:
SCOPE CAVEAT: this audit covers ONLY the §11.5 library-optimum slice (glass-ui-vs-slides gaps + constellation abstraction completeness + /constellation consumer-readiness). I did NOT audit aurora/blob/dock internals, storybook structure, sliders, or specular (other slices own those).

HEADLINE: glass-ui has done the HARD ABSTRACTION work (neutral Constellation + drawOverlay seam landed AW.W17; vReveal + useCountup landed AV.W3/AW.W15; DeckProgress + .glass-progress-rail landed AW.W16), but the CONSUMER-ADOPTION half never ran for ANY of them. slides still runs a 510-line constellation.ts, a local reveal directive, a local useCountup, and a hand-rolled .deck-progress div — all duplicating shipped glass-ui exports. The pattern is the §13 'consumer adoptions (dirty-tree blocked)' bucket: the library grew the primitive, the consumer kept the copy, and the loop never closed. The library-optimum is INCOMPLETE not because the primitives don't exist but because slides was never re-pointed onto them.

CROSS-CHECK FOR OTHER SLICES: (1) The constellation `stepOverlay` seam I propose touches constellationField.ts — coordinate with whoever owns the substrate/useCanvas2D wave. (2) DeckProgress composes <Progress> (the slider/progress slice §9 may touch Progress styling — the .glass-progress-rail recipe rides on it). (3) The /deck lift decision (AX.W-deck-primitive-decision) intersects §10's slides-bottom-bar requirement and the §13 chronic-deferral list — it is the single biggest un-executed library-optimum item and should be a NAMED decision in the tranche plan, not left implicit.

INVARIANT NOTE: the ≥2-consumer rule is the gate on the /deck lift. Constellation already passes (demo story + slides, once ported). DeckProgress passes (the AW.W16 wrapper + slides, once ported). vReveal/useCountup pass (existing motion demos + slides). The /deck ENGINE does NOT pass cross-repo today (3 in-repo decks only) — hence the explicit ratify-or-manufacture-consumer decision.

GOOD SIGNALS (not findings): slides correctly consumes glass-ui for dock, dialog, dropdown-menu, forms, button, controls, status-dot — the dock/dialog/dropdown consumption is healthy and the API bindings (position='inline', density, startCollapsed, collapseDelay, Button variant='glass', keepOpen/release) are all still valid against current glass-ui.

findings.requirement: §7 PRIMITIVES — 'Fonts — none are correct.' §0/§11.3 — encapsulation, single source of truth.
findings.currentState: Font tokens are fragmented across THREE files with conflicting defaults. tokens.css:43-45 defines --font-stack-display/-serif → 'Fraunces' (ornamental display serif), --font-stack-sans → Helvetica Neue. theme.css:107-110 bridges --font-display/-serif/-sans to those stacks. typography.css:84-99 then ALSO declares --font-brand-sans (Helvetica Neue) + the display variation-settings, and body{font-family:var(--font-serif)} (:142) makes ALL default body copy render in Fraunces — an ornamental display serif as the default body face of a glass UI library. The brand-uniform-sans preset (typography.css:132) is the only escape and has no internal consumer.
findings.rootCause: Font ownership was never consolidated: tokens.css owns the stacks, theme.css owns the bridge, typography.css owns the brand-sans + variation-settings + the body cascade. The body-defaults-to-Fraunces decision (serif body) is the visual root of '§7 fonts none are correct' — a display serif is wrong for body copy, and the 3-file split makes the default impossible to reason about in one place.
findings.gestaltFix: Consolidate ALL font tokens into ONE block (tokens.css §font or typography.css :root): the stacks, the brand-sans, the display variation-settings, the mono. Re-decide the body default — a glass UI body should default to the sans stack, reserving Fraunces for display/headline tiers only (body{font-family:var(--font-sans)}, headings opt into --font-display). This is the §7 fix at its root: correct the default + collapse the 3-file fragmentation into one source.

findings.requirement: §0 — no fragile magic-number/calc/min-max/viewport/z-index chains; style changes isomorphic.
findings.currentState: Audited every calc()/clamp()/viewport/z-index/min-max site (44 z-index, 38 calc, 18 clamp, 17 viewport). The vast majority are token-driven and sound: z-index is a full token registry (tokens.css §3 → theme.css --z-index-* bridge), calc chains read named tokens (density multipliers, golden-ratio radii), the typography clamp ladder is φ-keyed. The ONE residual bare magic number is the dock overflow breakpoint @media (min-width:640px) at dock.css:1167 — but it carries an inline comment tying it to --dock-overflow-bp (a var() cannot drive a media feature in Baseline CSS, documented at :1156-1166). The specular intensity literals (separate finding) are the real magic-number violation.
findings.rootCause: The fragile-chain class was largely already remediated across prior tranches (the z-index registry, the named --dock-overflow-bp). The CSS-spec limitation that var() can't feed a media-feature is a genuine constraint, not a defect — the inline-documented literal is the idiomatic workaround.
findings.gestaltFix: No structural change needed for the breakpoint (CSS-spec-bound; correctly documented). If container-query support lands for the dock root in a future engine, the @media could become @container — already noted at dock.css:1161 (AV.W16 TW3 KEPT-as-media rationale). The actionable magic-number is the specular ladder, tracked separately.

result.notes:
SLICE SCOPE: I audited src/styles/* exhaustively (24 files, 8352 lines) plus the SFC/composable coupling for any CSS-adjacent finding. I did NOT audit the dock ANIMATION CORRECTNESS (§1.1-1.8 the shrink-before-items defect) as that is JS/morph-driver territory for the dock slice — but I verified the dock STYLING architecture (the clip-reveal aperture, the spring-keyed stagger calc-ramp at dock.css:754-795) is structurally sound and token-driven; the §1.1 lag is almost certainly in the JS driver's --dock-morph-progress write timing, NOT the CSS.

HEADLINE FINDINGS (5 actionable): (1) four CSS god-modules >500 lines (tokens 1728 / dock 1227 / utilities 1119 / glass 691) — utilities.css is the worst, a kitchen-sink mixing ~190 lines of component metric-badge CSS with cross-cutting atoms; (2) .floating-panel is a DEAD orphan (zero consumers) shipping a full class+keyframe+theme-bridge chain — clean excision; (3) the §5 specular 'too extreme' is rooted in HARDCODED intensity literals in glass.css (0.35/0.6/0.85) not tokens — a token-first violation that also blocks consumer tuning; (4) the specular pointer-tracking JS is duplicated verbatim across Card.vue + DockIconButton.vue with no shared composable; (5) §7 fonts: the body defaults to the Fraunces DISPLAY SERIF and font tokens are fragmented across 3 files.

POSITIVE CONFIRMATIONS (the slice is healthier than feared on two axes): archaic-CSS is CLEAN (zero float/clear/zoom; one legitimately-required -webkit-background-clip); the magic-number/calc/viewport/z-index chains are almost entirely token-driven and sound (z-index is a full token registry; the one bare @media breakpoint is CSS-spec-bound and documented). So the AX styling work is mostly DECOMPOSITION + EXCISION + TOKENIZATION, not a rewrite.

CROSS-SLICE HANDOFFS: the glass-material naming drift + the specular composable straddle my CSS slice and the components/composables slice — flagged in both waves. The metric-badge ownership (utilities.css home) intersects §8 speedtest-repatriation; I scoped only the 'it's mis-filed in a global utilities.css' structural defect, not the ownership question. The instrument-chassis/glyph-face CSS files have live consumers but §7/§8 mandate their component removal — their CSS excision follows the component decision (NOT my slice to call).

The git archaeology confirms the naming drift traces to commit 8554e33 (W22/W23 glass-material fold) — a batch-1 merge §14 explicitly says to 'audit, not trust the green claims'; the code shipped correct but the file names + cross-file doc comments lagged.

result.slice: composables-state

findings.requirement: §11.3 — better composables/useX state management; derived state must be encapsulated, not hand-synced (the §0 'fail explicitly / no fragile chains' + DRY mandate).
findings.currentState: useDockState exposes `expanded` and `isPinned` as standalone mutable `ref`s that are MANUALLY re-derived from the `state` machine on every transition via a `syncDerived()` helper. There are 18 `state.value = …` assignment sites in the file, each of which must remember to call `syncDerived()` immediately after (grep shows the 18 mutations + 17 paired `syncDerived()` calls). The doc-comment literally calls these refs `derived` (`expanded`: '`true` whenever `state !== "collapsed"` — derived ref').
findings.rootCause: The state machine was authored before the J.W5.C `isHeld` lift made the file reactive-derivation-aware. `expanded`/`isPinned` predate that and were left as imperatively-mirrored refs. The real architectural why: there is no single source of truth — `state` is the truth, but two of its projections are stored as independent writable cells that the code must keep coherent by hand. Any future code path (or a refactor) that mutates `state.value` and forgets `syncDerived()` silently desyncs `expanded`/`isPinned`/the `onStateChange` callback. `isHeld` (added later) correctly uses `computed()`, proving the pattern was already known in-file.
findings.gestaltFix: Delete `syncDerived()` and the two writable refs. Make `expanded = computed(() => state.value !== "collapsed")` and `isPinned = computed(() => state.value === "pinned")` — pure derivations, impossible to desync. Fold the `getAlwaysExpanded()` clamp into the `alwaysExpanded` watcher (already `immediate:true`) rather than re-applying it inside `syncDerived`. Move the `onStateChange` side-effect onto a `watch(state, (n,o)=>onStateChange?.(n,o))`. Every mutation site then becomes a bare `state.value = …` with zero bookkeeping; the return shape (`Ref` vs `ComputedRef`) is API-compatible because `UseDockStateReturn` already types `expanded`/`isPinned` as `Ref<boolean>` (a `ComputedRef` is assignable). Net: −1 helper, −17 call sites, divergence becomes structurally impossible.
findings.evidence: src/composables/custom/dock/composables/useDockState.ts:83-109 (the refs + syncDerived), and the 18 `state.value =` / 17 `syncDerived()` sites enumerated by grep; consumed at src/components/custom/dock/GlassDock.vue:203-238 (destructured as plain refs, fed into provideDockContext + the visualExpanded computed).

findings.requirement: §0/§11.1-2 — no mixed-concern god-ish modules; no non-token imperative styling; ship only ≥2-consumer substrate (visual-load-bearing-ness invariant 10). §7 'glass-panel — all of them SUCK (redesign)'.
findings.currentState: `composables/glass/useGlassRenderer.ts` (257 lines) bundles TWO unrelated concerns under one composable-named file: (a) `useGlassRenderer()` — a tiny reactive tier-detection composable, and (b) `createGlassFilter`/`destroyGlassFilter` — a 90-line imperative, DOM-mutating SVG-displacement-filter factory that appends `<canvas>`/`<svg>` to `document.body`, writes `el.style.backdropFilter`/`border`/`boxShadow` directly with HARDCODED `rgba(255,255,255,0.25)`/`rgba(0,0,0,0.05)` colors, uses `(window as any).chrome`, and shares NO state with the composable. `createGlassFilter` has exactly ONE consumer: GlassPanel.vue (the component §7 marks for redesign).
findings.rootCause: The file conflates a reactive detector with an imperative effect-factory because both touch 'glass rendering', but they are different service boundaries: detection is declarative/reactive; the filter is an imperative DOM side-effect with manual lifecycle. The hardcoded rgba + direct `el.style` writes violate the token-first invariant (J invariant 1: every visual behaviour is a CSS custom property; no consumer/source hardcodes color). The single-consumer filter is substrate-with-one-binary — it survives only because GlassPanel (itself flagged for redesign) still calls it. `(window as any).chrome` is a brittle UA-shaped detection.
findings.gestaltFix: Split the file along its service boundary. Keep `useGlassRenderer.ts` as the pure reactive detector (the `tier` ref + `detectTier()` only; replace `(window as any).chrome` with a capability probe — it already CSS.supports-tests, so the chrome check is redundant noise). Move the imperative filter into the glass-panel package's own dir (it is GlassPanel-private, not a shared composable) OR delete it when the §7 GlassPanel redesign re-expresses the refraction as a token-driven `@utility`/SVG-in-CSS recipe (the architecturally-correct home — the displacement map + specular highlight belong in the CSS/SVG layer reading `--glass-*` tokens, not a JS canvas writing `el.style`). The hardcoded rgba borders/shadows become `--glass-border`/`--shadow-*` token reads. This is coordinated with the AX glass-panel redesign wave; the composables-state slice's contribution is the SPLIT + token-ization mandate.
findings.evidence: src/composables/glass/useGlassRenderer.ts:23 (`(window as any).chrome`), :203-212 (direct el.style + hardcoded rgba), :147-230 (the 83-line imperative factory); sole consumer src/components/custom/glass-panel/GlassPanel.vue:4-9,83-93; §7 flag at docs/tranches/AX/REQUIREMENTS.md:98.

findings.requirement: §11.3 — pipeline orchestration / reuse the canonical motion + DOM primitives; §0 DRY (don't re-roll requestAnimationFrame or listener lifecycle that an existing composable owns).
findings.currentState: The sidebar state sub-tree hand-rolls infrastructure the repo already ships as composables. `useSidebarFollow.ts` (247 lines) hand-rolls: a raw `requestAnimationFrame` damped-scroll loop (two rAF ids, manual cancel) instead of `useRAFLoop`/`useSpring`; a 5-listener `bindSidebar()` add/remove block that is DUPLICATED across `bindSidebar` (add+remove) and `onUnmounted` (remove again); a hand-rolled `escapeSelector()` CSS.escape fallback. `useScrollTracker.ts` independently hand-rolls its own rAF + scroll-listener add/remove lifecycle (1 addEventListener pair). The repo already has `useRAFLoop` (a full clock with pause/visibility/PRM/dispose), `useResizeObserver`, and a `useDocumentVisibility` leaf that AV.W14 explicitly folded the motion composables onto.
findings.rootCause: The sidebar sub-tree was authored as standalone DOM-imperative composables and never re-based onto the motion/dom primitive layer that matured later (AV.W14 did this fold for useRAFLoop/useIntersectionPause but did NOT reach the sidebar sub-tree). The damped `scrollTop += delta * damping` loop is a hand-rolled critically-damped approximation — exactly what `useSpring` (response/damping ODE) models analytically and bit-identically to the dock. The duplicated listener bind/unbind is a classic missing-`useEventListener`/missing-cleanup-helper smell that breeds the leak class (a listener removed in two places is one rename away from a leak).
findings.gestaltFix: Re-base both sidebar composables onto the existing primitives. (1) Replace the hand-rolled damped rAF in useSidebarFollow with `useSpring` (one source of truth for the approach curve — same ODE the dock uses, and the `manualOverride` becomes a `spring.stop()`). (2) Factor the repeated `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener` set into a single `bindListeners(el, map)` returning a disposer, or use a `useEventListener`-style helper, so the listener list lives in ONE place and cleanup is structural (no double-remove). (3) Drop the bespoke `escapeSelector` for a shared `cssEscape` util (or rely on the platform `CSS.escape`, SSR-guarded once). useScrollTracker's rAF + scroll listener fold onto `useRAFLoop` + the listener helper identically. Net: the sidebar sub-tree stops being an island and composes the library's own clock/observer/DI seams — the §11.3 'pipeline orchestration / service boundary' intent.
findings.evidence: src/composables/sidebar/useSidebarFollow.ts:87-132 (hand-rolled rAF damp), :179-201 + :234-243 (duplicated bind/unbind of 5 listeners), :48-53 (bespoke escapeSelector); src/composables/sidebar/useScrollTracker.ts:89,186-199 (independent rAF + listener lifecycle); the available primitives at src/composables/motion/useRAFLoop.ts + useSpring.ts; AV.W14 fold record at docs/tranches/AV/PROGRESS.md:218.

findings.requirement: §3 (visual-load-bearing-ness, L invariant 8) — substrate ships only with ≥2 consumers or is formally retired; §0 'excise or fail explicitly'.
findings.currentState: `useOptionalDockLayerGroupContext` is minted by the DI factory, exported from dockLayerContext.ts AND re-exported from dock/composables/index.ts, documented as 'Befitting silent default; reserved for future consumers' — but grep confirms it has ZERO consumers anywhere in src/ or demo/ (only the barrel line references it). The sibling `useOptionalDockContext` by contrast has 7 real consumers (Slider, popovers, etc.).
findings.rootCause: The createStrictContext factory returns BOTH `use` and `useOptional` over one key, and the dockLayerContext call site exported the optional shape speculatively 'for future consumers' — a substrate-without-consumer. The factory makes minting it free, so it leaked into the public dock barrel surface without a binary consumer. This is exactly the speculative-substrate class the AX mandate excises (a strict-throw is the only correct shape for `<DockLayer>` outside `<DockLayerGroup>`, mirroring the SortableContext 'strict-only, no useOptional shipped — invariant 25 per intent' precedent).
findings.gestaltFix: Stop exporting `useOptionalDockLayerGroupContext` from dockLayerContext.ts and the dock barrel — leave the factory's `useOptional` un-bound (the factory still returns it; it's just not surfaced), exactly as sortable-list/context.ts does ('the factory's `useOptional` over this key is left unexported by design'). `<DockLayer>` is meaningless outside `<DockLayerGroup>`, so strict-only is the correct intent and matches the documented matrix. Zero behavior change, removes a dead public symbol.
findings.evidence: src/components/custom/dock/composables/dockLayerContext.ts:56-57 (export + 'reserved' comment); re-export at src/components/custom/dock/composables/index.ts:19; grep for consumers returns only the barrel; the precedent at src/components/custom/sortable-list/context.ts:24-27.

findings.requirement: §0 — fail explicitly / no fragile correctness traps; §11.3 DI service boundary must be sound for all type instantiations.
findings.currentState: `createStrictContext.use()` guards with `if (!ctx) throw …` (createContext.ts:65). This treats ANY falsy injected value as 'outside the provider'. All 3 current instantiations carry object/ref types (DockContext, DockLayerGroupContext, UseSortableReturn) so it never misfires today — but the factory is the public canonical DI pair, and a future `createStrictContext<boolean>`/`<number>`/`<string>` would throw the 'outside provider' error on a legitimately-provided `false`/`0`/`''`.
findings.rootCause: The guard conflates 'not provided' (vue `inject(KEY)` returns `undefined`) with 'provided-but-falsy'. The correct sentinel test is `=== undefined`, not `!ctx`. Vue's `inject(KEY)` returns `undefined` exactly when no provider exists, so the strict signal is unambiguous without the falsy coercion.
findings.gestaltFix: Change the guard to `if (ctx === undefined) throw …` (and type the inner `inject` result accordingly). This makes the factory correct for every `T` including falsy-valued contexts, with zero change to the 3 current call sites. A latent-trap excision, not a workaround.
findings.evidence: src/composables/context/createContext.ts:63-69 (the `if (!ctx)` guard); the 3 instantiations all object-typed (dockContext.ts:42, dockLayerContext.ts:37, sortable-list/context.ts:28) — safe today, trap latent.

findings.requirement: §11.3 — idiomatic reactive state; avoid manual reactivity-version hacks where a tracked collection suffices.
findings.currentState: useKeyboardShortcuts maintains a plain `Set<RegisteredShortcut>` plus a separate `version = ref(0)` that every `registerShortcut`/cleanup manually bumps (`version.value++`) so the `labeled` computed re-runs (it reads `version.value;` as a fake dependency). This is a hand-rolled change-notification for a non-reactive Set.
findings.rootCause: A native `Set` mutation isn't tracked by Vue, so the author added a manual version counter to force the computed to invalidate. It works but is a smell — the reactivity is bolted on beside the data instead of being intrinsic to it. createGlobalState memoizes it so it's a singleton; correctness is fine, but the `version.value;` no-op read in the computed is a fragile idiom (a refactor that 'cleans up' the unused read silently breaks invalidation).
findings.gestaltFix: Replace the `Set` + `version` pair with a reactive collection: either a `shallowRef<Set<…>>` and `triggerRef` on mutation, or a `reactive(new Set())` / `ref(new Map())` keyed by the entry — so the `labeled` computed depends on the collection directly and the `version` ref + the fake-dependency read both disappear. Minor; behavior-identical, removes the bolted-on counter.
findings.evidence: src/composables/keyboard/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:214-232 (the Set + version + the `version.value;` fake-read in labeled), :248-255 (the manual `version.value++` bumps).

proposedWaves.title: Dock state-machine encapsulation: collapse derived refs to computed + excise speculative optional context + harden strict-context guard
proposedWaves.scope: Refactor useDockState so `expanded`/`isPinned` become `computed()` derivations off the `state` machine (delete syncDerived + its 17 call-site obligations; move onStateChange to a watch). Un-export the zero-consumer `useOptionalDockLayerGroupContext` (strict-only per intent, matching SortableContext). Change createStrictContext's guard from `!ctx` to `ctx === undefined` so the canonical DI pair is correct for falsy-valued T. Public API byte-stable (UseDockStateReturn types unchanged; ComputedRef assignable to Ref). REFACTOR — no visual change, but re-run the live dock interaction audit (hover/pin/click-away/keepOpen) since useDockState is §1's state core.
proposedWaves.dependsOn: none (foundational; lands before the §1 dock animation waves so they build on a coherent state core)

proposedWaves.title: Re-base the sidebar composable sub-tree onto the library's motion/DOM primitives
proposedWaves.scope: Refactor useSidebarFollow + useScrollTracker to compose useSpring (replacing the hand-rolled damped rAF approach curve — same ODE as the dock), useRAFLoop where a raw clock is still needed, and a single listener-bind/dispose helper (excising the duplicated 5-listener add/remove block + the double-remove cleanup). Drop the bespoke escapeSelector for a shared/platform CSS.escape. Pure encapsulation refactor; verify sidebar follow/scroll-track behavior live (the slides sidebar is the consumer).

proposedWaves.title: Split useGlassRenderer into reactive-detector vs imperative-filter; token-ize the filter for the GlassPanel redesign
proposedWaves.scope: Separate the pure reactive tier-detector (useGlassRenderer — also drop the brittle `(window as any).chrome` for the existing CSS.supports probe) from the imperative createGlassFilter/destroyGlassFilter (move into the glass-panel package as component-private, or delete when the §7 GlassPanel redesign re-expresses refraction/specular as token-driven SVG-in-CSS reading --glass-* tokens). Excise the hardcoded rgba borders/shadows. Coordinated with the AX glass-panel redesign wave.
proposedWaves.dependsOn: AX glass-panel-redesign wave (§7 primitives), AX.W-state-dock optional

proposedWaves.title: Keyboard registry reactive-collection cleanup
proposedWaves.scope: Replace the Set + manual `version` ref + fake-dependency read in useKeyboardShortcuts with an intrinsically-reactive collection (shallowRef+triggerRef or reactive Set/Map). Behavior-identical; removes the bolted-on change counter. Low-risk hygiene; bundle with other AX small-composable cleanups.

result.notes:
Overall the composables/state layer is in GOOD shape — the AV.W14 DI + render-loop work is genuinely exemplary and should NOT be re-litigated: the createStrictContext/createOptionalContext factory has 6 clean adopters with a documented strict-vs-optional matrix; the WebGL substrate (useWebGLCanvas) + compile.ts + useDocumentVisibility leaf + the ColorResolver DI are textbook service boundaries; useSortable's 5-service decomposition (dragController/dropResolver/ghostRenderer/touchGate/transitionTiming) is the gold-standard orchestrator pattern in the repo. No god-modules in the slice (largest is useLayerTransition at 479, a justified VT/FLIP fork; useCanvas2D 332; useGlassRenderer 257). No nested imports, no test-in-src (both gated). The goo-blob BLOB_CONFIG_KEY hand-rolled inject is a DELIBERATE, documented exception (external-provide default, DEC-AT-2) — correctly NOT minted by the factory; leave it.

The real findings are FOUR localized encapsulation gaps, in priority order: (1) useDockState's derived-ref hand-sync (major, routes into §1 dock — fix BEFORE the animation waves so they sit on a coherent state core); (2) the sidebar sub-tree as an island that never re-based onto useSpring/useRAFLoop (major, DRY); (3) useGlassRenderer's mixed-concern file with non-token imperative DOM mutation (major, but gated behind the §7 GlassPanel redesign — coordinate, don't fork); (4) a zero-consumer optional-context export + a latent falsy-T guard trap in the otherwise-excellent DI factory (minor each). Plus one cosmetic keyboard-registry version-ref smell.

findings.requirement: §12 Constellation visibility (dark + light) — the lattice must read as a neutral web with ONE red anomaly, visible on both cream and ink.
findings.currentState: BROKEN LIVE, despite H.W4 claiming it fixed. Measured on slide 1 (?freeze&light, 1512×862): 86.3% of all painted constellation pixels are strong red (red=15,492 px vs neutral=2,353 px). The web reads as a RED SPLATTER, not a neutral lattice. 8,544 of the red pixels are >200px from the anomaly anchor — i.e. the bulk of the inter-node web edges paint red, not neutral.
findings.rootCause: constellation.ts:107 reads the neutral edge color via `this.cLine = readVar(c, "--foreground", "#1c1714")`. `--foreground` resolves to `light-dark(hsl(24 10% 10%), hsl(48 10% 90%))`. Canvas2D REJECTS `light-dark()` (verified live: `ctx.strokeStyle = 'light-dark(...)'` leaves the sentinel unchanged). On the rejected assignment, `strokeStyle` STAYS at its previously-set value — and in `drawEdges` the immediately-prior value is the red `accentColor` (#cc0000) from any anomaly edge. So every neutral edge paints RED (verified live: feeding cLine after accent yields strokeStyle '#cc0000'). H.W4 promoted `--constellation-node/-node-dim/-accent` to plain-hex PRECISELY because 'Canvas2D rejects light-dark()' — but it LEFT `cLine` reading raw `--foreground`, the single most voluminous element (every inter-node edge). The fix was incomplete: it patched the node fills and the anomaly accent but missed the neutral edge stroke.
findings.gestaltFix: Promote the neutral edge color to a Canvas2D-safe plain-hex/hsl token, exactly as H.W4 did for the node tokens. Add `--constellation-edge` (plain hsl, NOT light-dark) to deck.css §1 (light arm) and §10 (`:root.dark .deck` dark arm), and change constellation.ts to `this.cLine = readVar(c, '--constellation-edge', '#1c1917')`. This closes the last light-dark()-into-Canvas2D leak and makes the neutral lattice paint its intended ink/cream hairline so the red anomaly is the single focal event. (Architectural note: a cleaner gestalt is a single `readCanvasColor()` helper in constellation.ts that asserts plain-hex and throws on a light-dark() value — fail-loud per §0 — so this class can never silently recur.)
findings.evidence: constellation.ts:107 (cLine = readVar(c,'--foreground',...)); deck.css:30,37 (--foreground/--red-text are light-dark()); live Playwright: strokeStyle='light-dark(...)' rejected→stays sentinel; drawEdges() (constellation.ts:259) sets `red ? accentColor : this.cLine`; measured red=15492 / neutral=2353 (ratio 6.6:1 red) on slide 1 freeze&light.

findings.requirement: §13 — The headless-green vs visually-broken GAP must become a standing AX gate-philosophy wave: every visual wave closes on a live audit, not a headless proof.
findings.currentState: UNADDRESSED at the gate level — this is the cardinal lesson the whole audit confirms. The AW gate-fleet is rich (proof:aurora-* ×6, proof:blob-* ×6, proof:dock-animation-live, proof:animation-coherence, proof:glass-material-*, proof:demo-dock-nav...) and the tranche shipped them GREEN, yet aurora AND blob render pure black and proof:dock-animation-live fail-OPENs on CI. The F-tranche W1-runtime-smoke.json loads 124 routes, asserts mainTextLength + consoleErrors (0 errors), and passes — while never sampling a single canvas pixel.
findings.rootCause: Structural: glass-ui carries ZERO browser dependency by design (a correct library precept), so every behavioral/visual gate is either (a) a CPU oracle-equivalence test (color-math in isolation — green even when the live render is black), (b) a static-bake snapshot (the thumbnail path — green even when the runtime path is dead), or (c) a Playwright gate that fail-OPENs (SKIPs) on CI because no playwright harness is installed. There is NO fail-CLOSED gate that asserts a live runtime canvas paints color. 'Green gate' and 'visually true' became fully decoupled.
findings.gestaltFix: Stand up a SEPARATE visual-test workspace (a dedicated package or workspace with Playwright as a devDependency, kept entirely off the zero-dep library publish surface) that runs a fail-CLOSED π visual-runtime lane: (1) proof:substrate-paints-color — readPixels both aurora + blob, assert maxChannel>0 over the interior; (2) proof:dock-animation-live promoted from fail-open SKIP to fail-CLOSED in this workspace; (3) a per-story canvas-paint coverage walk (every WebGL/Canvas2D story asserts non-black). Make 'live-re-diagnosis BEFORE the fix' a wave-open ritual (the W1 misdiagnosis precedent). This is the FIRST wave (AX.W1) and every visual wave depends on its lane existing.
findings.evidence: Aurora maxChannel=0, blob maxChannel=0 (live); proof:dock-animation-live SKIPs fail-open (W1-collapse-live.json capturedIn); F/audit/W1-runtime-smoke.json asserts text+console only, 124 routes 'pass' with black canvases among them. All aurora/blob gates are oracle/snapshot, not live-pixel.
findings.routesToWave: AX.W1 (gate-philosophy + visual-runtime π lane — FIRST wave, dependency of every visual wave)

result.notes:
SCOPE OF MY SLICE: I audited the AU/AV/AW plan vs the actual delivery (3.4.0→3.6.0 + batch-1 @ eaba94f / HEAD at-dock-convergence) with live Playwright pixel-readback, git archaeology, and source inspection. I did NOT implement anything.

THE THREE-BUCKET VERDICT:
• VISUALLY-TRUE: dock simple-collapse (W1, container-type removal, shipped 3.4/3.5 — confirmed live), dock render geometry, slider two-only + rounded knob (AV.W11), W28 dock-based demo nav (sidebar + bottom-bar docks both live), W31 token-level animation coherence, the four READMEs exist.
• HEADLESS-GREEN-ONLY (green gate, visual truth unverified or fail-open): dock lockstep/springiness W2/W3 (proof:dock-animation-live SKIPs fail-open on CI), all aurora gates (oracle-equivalence/snapshot only), all blob gates (color-port only).
• REGRESSED (shipped green, broken live): AURORA renders PURE BLACK (maxChannel=0/1600px live) and BLOB renders PURE BLACK (maxChannel=0/24000px live) — BOTH from the SAME shared-substrate root: the AW.W7 createCanvasLifecycle.ts demand-gate/park carve (commits c17b74c + 008e6b4). This is the single most important finding: the entire aurora band (W4-W8) and blob band (W9-W11) shipped 'green' on top of a dead shared substrate.

THE CARDINAL LESSON (§13 gate-philosophy): glass-ui's zero-browser-dependency precept means every visual/behavioral gate is a CPU oracle, a static bake, or a fail-open Playwright SKIP — none asserts a live runtime canvas paints color. 'Green gate' and 'visually true' are fully decoupled. The F-tranche W1-runtime-smoke loads 124 routes, checks console+text, passes — with black canvases among them. AX.W1 (the visual-runtime π lane, fail-closed, in a separate Playwright workspace off the publish surface) is the structural fix and MUST be the first wave.

DEFERRED / CHRONICALLY-DEFERRED (all confirmed at HEAD): band-G W29 (aurora-configurator), W30 (carousel), W32 (lighthouse) NEVER RAN (zero commits); W33 close NEVER RAN (proof-aw-final.mjs MISSING, no FINAL.md); §7 prune targets all survive (keep-and-documented behind speedtest external consumers — the muster-block / dirty-sibling wall); §8 speedtest repatriation muster-blocked; §9.1 glass-scrubber rename skipped (variant still 'standard'); specular extremity §5 not separately re-verified.

WAVE STRUCTURE NOTE: My slice proposes 11 anchor waves covering the plan-delivery + deferred-item + gate-philosophy scope; the full AX tranche is 30+ dock-first waves — the aurora painterly/OKLCh/options/WebGPU/interactive bands, the blob bands, the glass-atoms re-audit, constellation, and the storybook waves will be proposed by sibling slices. I deliberately kept my IDs sparse (W1,W2,W3,W8,W26-W33) to leave room; the orchestrator should renumber into the dock-first ordering. CRITICAL ORDERING: AX.W1 (gate-philosophy) → AX.W2 (substrate repair) must open the tranche because every aurora/blob/dock visual wave depends on the substrate painting + the fail-closed visual lane existing. Do NOT let the close wave (AX.W33) renumber-drift the way AW.W33 did (W18→W21→W27→W33, never reached) — fix it at the tail with hard depends-on every wave.
